Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

spatialkit (development version)

Breaking changes

Defaults and results that differ from 2.0.0. Each entry says how to get the old behaviour where there is a way.

  • resolution_profile() scores pooled values by default (estimate = "auto") at 4.5 observations per cell (obs_per_cell = "auto"), with the centres fitted to every row. A call with a numeric response, no predictors and none of levels, n_levels, min_cell_n, sample_n and range_floor returns one level where it returned a ladder of about 20, and its count is larger: on 3,000 rows, 667 cells where the ladder stopped at 333. elbow is NA on one level. The profile gains scored_per_cell, loo, loo_se, share_alone and own_weight, attr(, "estimate") and a print line, and a layer whose scored rows share locations raises spatialkit_repeated_locations. A call that sets one of those five arguments keeps the ladder they describe and gains the same columns, and since it now carries the pooled estimate, select_resolution() with no criterion reads it by the size: it returns the level nearest round(n / 4.5), on the automatic ladder its top level, with spatialkit_size_not_reached, where 2.0.0 returned Cp’s pick. criterion = "cp", or estimate = NULL in the profile, gives Cp’s count, with the noise variance of the entry on Cp below. On the default ladder no variogram is fitted (sac = "auto"): cp and reliability are NA, attr(, "cp_noise") says why, and nothing is said about a variogram; on any other ladder it is estimated as before. The default ladder’s fits are bounded: from the 3 starts of the density kind the call stops above about 122,000 rows with an error of class spatialkit_work_limit that names the ways on (the limit is set where the fit takes about a minute, so a call just below it runs that long and prints nothing while it runs), and without the Matrix package moran_i and moran_z are NA above 22,500 rows, with spatialkit_moran_skipped. A profile passed straight as a count (get_voronoi_seeds(n = prof), voronoi_seeds_kmeans(k = prof), build_tessellation(approx_n_cells = prof)) is read by the size and no longer by cp. estimate = NULL, obs_per_cell = NULL gives the previous ladder and columns, except cp wherever the entry on Cp’s noise variance below applies; sac = NULL estimates the variogram on a ladder of sizes too.

  • resolution_profile(), get_voronoi_seeds() and voronoi_seeds_kmeans() build density-weighted regions by default (partition = "density"), kept from the best of 3 k-means++ starts (nstart = NULL, kmeans_nstart = NULL). Their cells are small where observations are dense, and hold about the same number of observations each once there are more cells than dense places. Every default call of the three functions returns other centres and other cells. The profile, its selections and its seeds carry the partition record (attr(, "partition"), sel$partition), and the prints name the kind. In the profile wss stays the unweighted sum, wss_spread is the spread of the weighted one, and a start runs for at most 100 steps of Lloyd’s iteration. The seeding functions put the rows in coordinate order first, so their seeds no longer depend on the order of the rows, and get_voronoi_seeds()‘s attr(, "kmeans") gains converged and objective. density_power and density_k are read, and a default call can raise spatialkit_empty_cells and spatialkit_not_converged. A cloud get_voronoi_seeds() draws inside a boundary is uniform, so the kind has no density to follow there. method = "random" and "provided" are unchanged, and a selection or a profile passed as the count returns the centres it scored, as before, except off a profile without an estimate fitted to a subsample, whose chosen level is refitted to every point (see the entry below on the refit of the chosen level). partition = "kmeans" gives the previous regions with their previous starts: the profile’s best of 25 k-means++ starts, the seeding functions’ stats::kmeans() from 10 random starts on the rows as they come. A call that named partition = "density" and no number of starts runs 3 starts where it ran 25 (the profile) or 10 (the seeding functions); nstart = 25, kmeans_nstart = 10 or nstart = 10 restores that.

  • get_voronoi_seeds() given a number of starts that is not whole, such as kmeans_nstart = 2.5, and no partition now stops: the density kind refuses it, with “kmeans_nstart must be NULL or a single positive whole number of starts; got 2.5.” With partition = "kmeans" the call returns as before.

  • select_resolution() reads a profile by criterion = "auto": the size for pooled values, the leave-one-out minimum for plain means, cp for a profile built with estimate = NULL. On a profile with an estimate the count is the level nearest round(n / 4.5), not Cp’s minimum: on the default profile that count itself, and on a ladder of counts the nearest level, with spatialkit_size_not_reached when it is not the count. A response with no structure is still reported, by another test: structured = FALSE, and spatialkit_no_structure where the count becomes cells, from the leave-one-out error against one mean. The count is then the size’s where Cp’s was 2 cells or the like, since a size does not shrink for want of structure, and spatialkit_bound_chosen is not raised for a size. On a profile without an estimate the criteria are read as before, and criterion = "cp" reads cp on a profile that has it; what is new there is the cp column itself where the entry on Cp’s noise variance below applies, the record a cp selection carries, and the seeds of a profile fitted to a subsample (see the entry below on the refit of the chosen level). The default profile, one level with no variogram, has none, and criterion = "cp" or "reliability" on it is an error that says what to pass. For Cp’s count as 2.0.0 read it, build the profile with estimate = NULL, obs_per_cell = NULL (and partition = "kmeans" for the same regions): Cp’s noise variance is then the variogram’s nugget, as in 2.0.0, wherever that nugget is above the fit’s lower bound and no more than the semivariance of nearest-neighbour pairs.

  • summarize_by_cell() adds the pooled columns by default (estimate = "pooled"): ..pooled_*, ..pooled_w_* and ..pooled_target_* for every numeric response and predictor, and the attributes "pooled" and "intervals". Every existing column is unchanged. The default call can now raise the warnings of the pooled values, each once per call: spatialkit_pool_unavailable (a layer with no geometry, which the call accepts; no row with a value, a cell and a location; no two rows in any cell; values beyond what the arithmetic of pooled values holds), spatialkit_pool_degenerate (one cell, no spread inside any cell, or no signal between cells), spatialkit_pool_few_cells (2 to 9 cells), spatialkit_pool_few_df, spatialkit_no_structure (a response the cells do not help with), spatialkit_pool_rows_skipped, and, on cells that carry a count record, spatialkit_estimate_mismatch and spatialkit_cells_differ. Small layers and layers without spatial structure raise several. estimate = "mean" returns the previous frame.

  • resolution_profile() no longer stops when a ladder set with levels has a level of more than 5,000 cells and the Matrix package is not installed: moran_i and moran_z are NA at such a level, with a warning of class spatialkit_moran_skipped, and every other column is computed. Installing Matrix gives the two columns.

  • The FNN package moves from Suggests to Imports and installs with spatialkit. The nearest-neighbour searches use it, among them the one behind the weights of the density kind, now the default partition. The package’s own searches, which compare every pair of locations and give the same results in a time that grows with the square of their number, remain for a session in which FNN cannot be loaded.

  • estimate_sac_range() fits its variogram model without iteration, so the same layer gives the same verdict, range and nugget whatever the unit of the response or of the coordinates and whatever the order of its rows. The criterion is gstat’s (squared error weighted by N/h^2); for each trial range the nugget and partial sill are solved exactly, and the range is searched on a grid and refined. Every range and nugget moves a little. Only the exponential family is fitted: the spherical fallback is gone. rejected_reason no longer takes "variogram model did not converge"; attr(attr(x, "variogram_model"), "converged") is FALSE when the criterion has no minimum inside the ranges searched. Nothing is printed to the console.

  • estimate_sac_range() tests for spatial structure before it returns a range: Moran’s I of the modelled variable on its 2, 4, 8 and 16 nearest neighbours, with the smallest one-sided p-value multiplied by four. When that is not below the new argument structure_alpha (default 0.05) the result is NA with rejected_reason "no spatial structure detected at the nearest-neighbour scale" and a pure-nugget model. On white noise (300 points) a finite range came back for 24 of 60 layers and now comes back for 1. The test has little power where few neighbours lie inside the range. structure_alpha = 1 switches the refusal off. A variogram that no model with a range fits better than a constant is refused as "the empirical variogram is flat: no spatial structure at the lags resolved".

  • estimate_sac_range() gains lags = c("adaptive", "equal") and n_lags, and "adaptive" is the default: the first bin ends where the closest max(50, n / 4) pairs lie, and the rest widen geometrically to the cutoff. Fifteen equal bins hid structure shorter than the first bin: on a clustered layer with a true range of 30 the median estimate was 77 and is now 29. A longer second structure seen at equal lags is kept in the model and sets the range (structures, short_range), and a range the adaptive lags leave past the largest lag falls back to the equal-lag result (lag_fallback). Ranges, nuggets and the block sizes of make_folds(auto_range = TRUE) change. lags = "equal" keeps the old bins.

  • estimate_sac_range() never returns the largest directional range in place of an all-pairs fit that identifies no range: the result is then NA. The directional ranges are still attached, and anisotropy_used is always FALSE.

  • resolution_profile(range_floor = FALSE) is the default. The ladder starts at 2 cells; the floor the autocorrelation range implies is reported in the bounds and the print, and is a level of the ladder when the layer supports it. A range is an estimate and can be spurious, and a ladder that started at it could not show the counts below. select_resolution(criterion = "reliability") reads the levels at or above the floor, so it returns the floor, as it did when the ladder started there; its new argument range_floor = FALSE reads every level. resolution_profile(range_floor = TRUE) starts the ladder at the floor.

  • resolution_profile() takes its support ceiling from the rows that carry a response (and every predictor, when predictors are given), not from every point. A layer with a response on a quarter of its rows gets a quarter of the ceiling, ceiling_from reads "min_cell_n (rows with a response)", and a warning of class spatialkit_response_ceiling gives both counts. New columns cells_resp and cell_resp_mean count the cells that hold a scored row and the scored rows per such cell.

  • moran_z is a diagnostic of the cell means and is no longer read as a count rule. It grows as cells get finer than the range and is near zero at the coarsest counts it is computed at, whatever the data. select_resolution(criterion = "moran_z") is an error of class spatialkit_diagnostic_criterion unless diagnostic = TRUE; summary() leaves it out unless it is named in criteria; plot() draws its curve with no selected level. determine_optimal_levels() still ranks by it under criterion = "morans_i", and raises a warning of class spatialkit_diagnostic_ranking when it does; under "combined" it is reported and no longer ranks (below).

  • get_voronoi_seeds(), voronoi_seeds_kmeans() and build_tessellation() read a resolution_profile() built without an estimate by cp or not at all (one built with an estimate, the default, is read by criterion = "auto"). A profile whose cp is NA was read by the next finite criterion with a log line; it is now an error (class spatialkit_no_default_criterion when another criterion is finite). A geometry-only profile whose only finite criterion is elbow is still read by it. Pass select_resolution(profile, criterion = ) to choose another criterion.

  • select_features_forward() accepts a candidate by a new default rule, rule = "se": its pooled gain has to exceed tol and the mean of its per-fold gains has to exceed se_mult (default 1) standard errors of that mean. With tol = 0 any gain was accepted. rule = "tol" is the old test. Every learner now has a baseline, so the selection can be empty (see Bug fixes).

  • area_of_applicability() weights the predictors by the model’s variable importance by default (weights = "auto"): pmax(importance, 0) when the model carries a finite importance for every predictor and has out-of-bag skill, equal weights otherwise, with the reason logged. params$weights_source says which. weights = NULL gives equal weights as before.

  • area_of_applicability() measures location for a gwr_fit, a bayesian_fit and a forest fitted with include_coords = TRUE, which predict as a function of location. Location has an index of its own (DI_location, element location): the distance to the nearest training point over the mean distance between training points, with the same folds and threshold rule. A point is inside only when it is inside on both indices; n_outside_predictors counts the predictor index alone, and a threshold the caller passes sets that index alone. The forest keeps its coordinates in the predictor index as ..x and ..y, so for it DI <= threshold is the old answer under the same weights; its params$coords reads "location index and predictors", and print() names both. Three more things change for the forest. A row outside on location is FALSE also when a predictor is missing, where it was NA, so n_na can fall and n_outside rise. Folds that split repeat visits to a site can give it a location threshold of 0, with the spatialkit_aoa_zero_threshold warning, and then only points at a training location are inside. A train_sf passed in a geographic CRS (longitude/latitude), which the predictor index measured in degrees, is refused: project it, or pass coords = "no". The default train_sf is the forest’s own data, which fit_rf_model() projects. For a GWR or a Bayesian fit coords = "no" gives the old result; for the forest it leaves the coordinates out of both indices. coords = "yes" measures location for any model.

  • fit_rf_model() splits an unordered factor or character predictor with respect.unordered.factors = "order", which ranger’s help recommends; ranger’s default, "ignore", splits on the order the levels are stored in. Forests with such a predictor change. Pass respect.unordered.factors through ... to set it yourself. $info$categorical_predictors and $info$respect_unordered_factors record what was done, and print() shows it. print() also reads “no spatial information used” for a forest fitted without the coordinates.

  • The local regressions of a GWR are solved by the package, by pivoted QR on predictors centred in each window, and GWmodel is no longer needed to fit, predict, cross-validate or select (sp still is). A window of deficient rank neither stops the fit nor returns coefficients made of rounding error: a coefficient it cannot estimate is NA, and a warning of class spatialkit_gwr_rank_deficient counts them. On windows of full rank the results equal GWmodel::gwr.basic()’s to rounding error. fit$engine is a list in GWmodel’s layout (SDF, GW.diagnostic, GW.arguments, lm) and no longer an object of class gwrm. print() heads the fit <GWR>, not <GWR (GWmodel)>.

  • With bandwidth = NULL, fit_gwr_model(), gwr_model_selection() and cv_gwr() select the bandwidth by a search of their own: 16 log-spaced bandwidths are scored and the best is refined. GWmodel::bw.gwr()’s golden-section search assumes one minimum and returned a near-global bandwidth when AICc had two. The scored curve is kept in info$bandwidth_search. Selected bandwidths can differ from 2.0.0’s; supply bandwidth to fix one. Below 20 observations the bandwidth is searched like any other.

  • fit_gwr_model(), gwr_model_selection() and cv_gwr() select the default bandwidth by the leave-one-location-out sum of squares, not AICc, when rows share a location (repeat visits, replicate samples). AICc counts such rows as independent and is lowest where the windows reproduce each location’s mean. A warning of class spatialkit_gwr_repeated_locations gives the counts; info$n_locations and info$bandwidth_search$approach record it. A layer with no repeated location is searched by AICc.

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model(standardize_predictors = TRUE) scales its automatic slope prior to the response: normal(0, 2.5 * sd(y)) under an identity link and normal(0, 2.5 * sd(log(y))) for the lognormal families. The fixed normal(0, 5) shrank a slope of about 14,000 per SD on a response in dollars to 0.06. Other links keep normal(0, 5). The prior used is stored as $info$b_prior; pass prior to set your own.

  • $info$convergence_ok of a Bayesian fit follows Stan’s own diagnostics more closely. It is FALSE on any divergent transition, an R-hat above 1.05, an R-hat above 1.01 with an effective sample size under 100 per chain, a bulk or tail effective sample size under 100 per chain, or an E-BFMI under 0.3 in a chain. Short runs that passed can now fail. A failed verdict raises one warning of class spatialkit_convergence that names each failed check and its remedy.

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model() samples at adapt_delta = 0.99 by default, where it sampled at 0.9, and so do cv_bayes(), compare_models_cv() and every other call that leaves control unset. At 0.9 ordinary data left a few divergent transitions, and one is enough to set convergence_ok to FALSE and raise spatialkit_convergence: four layers of 250 points fitted at the default length from three seeds each had 1 to 24 in every fit, and none at 0.99. Sampling takes about two to three times as long, and a fit at a given seed draws other values, so its estimates, intervals and predictions change. control = list(adapt_delta = 0.9) restores the previous setting. The warning’s advice prints adapt_delta as it was set; it printed 0.975 as 0.97, 0.995 as 0.99 and 0.999 as 1.00.

  • summarize_by_cell(deff = "variogram") falls back to "kish", not to the uncorrected standard error, when no usable variogram exists. The warning of class spatialkit_deff_fallback gives the reason. A new column deff_method, present whenever a design effect is requested, names the correction each row carries. A variogram refused because the response shows no spatial structure is not a fallback: its pure-nugget model gives a design effect of 1. It gives that design effect to every column, and a warning of class spatialkit_deff_no_structure names the predictor columns summarised under it, since the verdict is about the variable the variogram was fitted to; deff = "kish" corrects each predictor by its own ICC.

  • summarize_by_cell(deff = "kish") estimates the ICC of each predictor on its own. One ICC was pooled over every predictor listed, so listing a second predictor changed the first one’s standard error. attr(, "icc")$pred and attr(, "deff_applied")$icc_pred are vectors named by predictor column.

  • summarize_by_cell(deff = "kish"), and a "variogram" request that falls back to it, return NA standard errors, in every cell of two or more values, for a column whose ICC cannot be estimated: its values in one cell, fewer than two cells holding two or more of them, or values that fall in no cell or differ only there (rows with no cell id give no cell to the ICC). They returned the uncorrected ones, as for an ICC estimated at or below 0, under the same label. ..neff_*, ..ci_* and, for the column that sets it, cell_weight are NA in those cells too, so a regression weighted by cell_weight leaves them out; a cell of one value keeps its cell_weight of 1. A warning of class spatialkit_icc_unavailable names the columns and the reason, attr(, "icc") holds NA for each, with reason, and under estimate = "pooled" the method of attr(, "intervals") names them. An estimate at or below 0 still gives an ICC of 0 and the uncorrected standard errors, and a column whose values are all equal, those of rows with no cell id included, keeps standard errors of 0 (its ICC is NA, with the reason “the column does not vary”). deff = 1 gives the uncorrected standard errors in every case.

  • Voronoi cells built on seeds reach the edge of the data the seeds stand for. build_tessellation(seeds, method = "voronoi") without a boundary clipped the cells to the seeds’ own hull, and the observations outside it were dropped by the assignment: a quarter of 3,000 uniform points at 25 k-means seeds. The seeding functions now attach the boundary they drew in, or the hull of the points they clustered, as attr(, "cover"), and the cells are built over it. Pass boundary to set the extent yourself.

  • assign_features_to_polygons() stops on a duplicated or missing value in the polygon ID column. Nine polygons with a zone attribute called id came back as three. When the rows that share an ID are parts of one unit, merge them first with dplyr::summarise(dplyr::group_by(polygons_sf, <ID column>)).

  • Conditions that were log lines are R warnings with a class, so tryCatch(), withCallingHandlers() and options(warn = 2) see them: rows dropped before a fit (spatialkit_rows_dropped), a constant predictor (spatialkit_constant_predictor), features in no polygon (spatialkit_unassigned), fewer folds than asked for (spatialkit_k_reduced), a cell count chosen by a bound of the ladder (spatialkit_bound_chosen) and a profile the layer does not support (spatialkit_not_supported). ?resolution_profile lists the classes of the resolution functions.

  • determine_optimal_levels() returns NA where its WSS curve has no elbow (on_no_elbow = "na", the default). The count it returned there is where the chord rule lands on a curve with no bend, about the square root of max_levels whatever the points, so the ladder chose it and not the data. A ladder too short to show an elbow gives NA too, and so does a layer of one or two points or of one location, where it gave 1. The NA comes with a warning of class spatialkit_no_elbow that says why and carries the count as k, and with attr(, "structured"), FALSE, and attr(, "sag"), the largest log-log sag of the curve. Every result at the default carries the two attributes, structured being TRUE when the WSS curve has an elbow, and the counts themselves are unchanged. Under the model-aware criteria a curve with no elbow leaves no window to score: the call returns NA without ranking counts by Moran’s z, its NA carries the "diagnostics" of the sweep (every Moran’s I NA, eval_ks empty), and its log lines no longer say the window is scored or the call falls back to the geometric ranking. build_tessellation() and get_voronoi_seeds() stop on the NA and say where it came from. on_no_elbow = "warn" returns the count, with the same warning and without the structured and sag attributes.

  • determine_optimal_levels() keeps the criterion it is given. Supplying both response_var and predictor_vars switched criterion = "geometric", the default, to "combined", also when "geometric" was named, so the count read the response unasked. Such a call now returns what the call without the two variables returns, with no "diagnostics" attribute and no spatialkit_diagnostic_ranking warning, and a line logged at the INFO level says that criterion = "combined" reports Moran’s I of the cell means. The columns must still exist; a factor or character response is refused only under a criterion that reads it. Name criterion = "combined" for the path the switch took, whose ranking the next entry changes.

  • determine_optimal_levels(criterion = "combined") ranks the counts around the elbow by the WSS curve’s log-log sag alone. Moran’s z of the cell means is dropped from the ranking, not replaced by another statistic: averaged with the sag, it put first ten, the lowest count it can be computed at, or the count after it. On a curve with no elbow the sag is flat and the counts below ten, which Moran’s z cannot score, took the last place on its axis; with an elbow its |z| is near 0 at the coarsest counts it scores whatever the response. On 600 uniform points with a smooth field, under on_no_elbow = "warn", the call returned 10 6 5 where "geometric" returns 6 5 7, and it now returns 6 5 7; on eleven clusters with a smooth field it returned 10 11 12 and now returns 11 12 10, the elbow, 11, first. The sag is that of the sweep’s WSS curve, the one the elbow is read from, so with an elbow the elbow comes first and the counts after it follow by sag; they can differ from the two neighbours "geometric" returns. With no elbow the order is "geometric"’s. The k-means re-run behind Moran’s I no longer ranks: where it landed in a worse optimum at the elbow than the sweep did, another count went first, and on eighteen loose clusters the elbow, 15, was not among the counts returned. Its WSS stays in attr(, "diagnostics") as wss_eval, beside moran_i and moran_z, and combined_rank is the rank of the sweep’s sag. Where Moran’s I can be computed at no count of a window that reaches ten cells (a constant response, too few cells holding a row with one, or too few in the half select_on = "split" reads), "combined" returned the geometric ranking without diagnostics; it now ranks as it does otherwise, with moran_i and moran_z NA and a logged warning, so neither the response nor the split changes the counts it returns. "morans_i" still falls back there. "combined" no longer raises spatialkit_diagnostic_ranking. criterion = "morans_i", which still ranks by Moran’s z, does; the condition no longer carries upgraded, and its message names resolution_profile() and select_resolution(), which run on the default profile, where it named select_resolution(criterion = "cp"), an error there. No argument gives the earlier ranking.

  • Cp’s noise variance in resolution_profile() is no longer a nugget at the variogram fit’s lower bound (0, or at most 1e-4 of the sill), and it is held to the semivariance of nearest-neighbour pairs the variogram carries (attr(sac, "short_lag_semivariance")); Bug fixes has the details. Wherever either applies, the cp column, Cp at one cell (attr(, "one_cell")) and Cp’s count differ from 2.0.0’s on every ladder that fits a variogram, estimate = NULL, obs_per_cell = NULL included, and no argument gives the earlier noise variance back. attr(, "cp_noise") names the source used and, under the hold, the one it replaced. A selection by cp off a profile without an estimate gains count_rule, which its seeds, the cells built on them and the assigned layer carry on.

  • select_resolution() refits the level it chooses off a profile without an estimate fitted to a subsample (a ladder of counts on more than sample_n points) to every point before it hands the seeds on (Bug fixes has the details). So those seeds, and the seeds get_voronoi_seeds() and voronoi_seeds_kmeans() return for such a selection or profile, are not the centres 2.0.0 returned, partition = "kmeans" and estimate = NULL, obs_per_cell = NULL included. The centres the profile scored, which 2.0.0 returned, are attr(profile, "centres")[[as.character(sel$best)]], in the CRS attr(profile, "centres_crs").

  • resolution_profile() raises one warning of class spatialkit_size_not_reached for all the sizes of a ladder held for the same reason, where it raised one for each size. Its obs_per_cell and wanted hold one element for each such size, in the order of the ladder, so a script that read them as single numbers gets vectors where several sizes are held; used and reason are single values as before. One size held gives the condition it gave.

  • estimate_sac_range() gives the rejected_reason “no variogram model could be fitted: fewer than three lag bins hold point pairs” where it gave “no variogram model could be fitted (singular fits)”: nothing was fitted in that case. A script that compared the reason with the old text can compare its start, “no variogram model could be fitted”, which both share.

  • estimate_sac_range() needs 30 distinct locations as well as 30 rows (Bug fixes has the details). A layer of 30 or more rows at 2 to 29 distinct locations, to which 2.0.0 fitted a variogram, gets the unclassed NA whose rejected_reason begins with the count of its distinct locations. So on such layers a range that came back is NA, summarize_by_cell(deff = "variogram") returns Kish standard errors with spatialkit_deff_fallback, and make_folds(auto_range = TRUE) builds geometric blocks. No argument gives the earlier result back: a range read off fewer than 30 locations is not identified.

  • new_spatial_fit() stops on a fit its methods cannot use, with an error that names the argument and what it got: data_sf must be an sf object, formula a formula, response_var the name of one attribute column of data_sf (a column other than its geometry), predictor_vars a character vector of its attribute columns (character(0) for none), subclass one class name and info a list. It also stops when predictor_vars names the response, when the left side of formula does not hold response_var (a transform such as log(price) ~ elev holds it), and when an object classed sf has no geometry column (its "sf_column" attribute missing, not one name, or naming a column that is not an sfc). It built a fit from any of them: the response among the predictors was measured in area_of_applicability()’s distances and had to be present in the new rows, a formula such as elev ~ price with response_var = "price" printed one model while summary() and model_metrics() scored the fitted values against price, the object classed sf without geometry made summary(), model_metrics() and area_of_applicability() stop with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”, a column number or a factor as response_var made summary() and model_metrics() score the fitted values against the column at that position, a misspelt name or the geometry column’s name failed later in another function with a message about something else, and a data_sf without geometry made residual_morans_i() blame a missing residuals() method. A fit_fn that passed st_drop_geometry(train_sf) has to pass train_sf. One whose fit names a column the training rows lack (a predictor derived inside fit_fn, say) fails every fold of cv_spatial(), with the message in fold_status: add the column to train_sf before building the fit, or leave it out of predictor_vars, as the README’s trend_fit does with the coordinates it derives. A brms::bf() formula is passed as its $formula. In select_features_forward(), a fit_fn whose fit for no predictors is refused (predictor_vars = NULL where character(0) is meant, say) can no longer give the null-model baseline: the baseline is the training-fold mean, as for any learner that cannot fit the empty set, and baseline$type says "fold mean".

  • new_spatial_fit() stops when the right side of formula and predictor_vars disagree: when predictor_vars names a column the right side does not use, or the right side uses an attribute column of data_sf, other than the response, that predictor_vars does not name. Both are read by all.vars(), so transforms (log(elev)), interactions, ., names that are not columns of data_sf and the reserved coordinate names ..x and ..y build; the columns of an offset() or a grouping term count as used. A fit_fn that derives coordinates x and y for a trend surface, on a layer that keeps its coordinates as columns x and y, is refused: the error says to name such columns in predictor_vars or to derive them under names that are not columns of data_sf. It built such a fit, whose print() showed one model while area_of_applicability() measured distances in other predictors and residual_morans_i() rebuilt the OLS design from them: a fit of price ~ elev with predictor_vars = "slope" put rows 10 standard deviations outside the training range of elev inside the area of applicability, and its Moran test switched to the randomisation null in silence. A fit_fn whose formula and predictor_vars disagree fails every fold of cv_spatial(), with the message in fold_status.

New features

  • resolution_profile(), get_voronoi_seeds(method = "kmeans") and voronoi_seeds_kmeans() gain partition = c("density", "kmeans"). "kmeans" is what each function did: centres that minimise the sum of squared distances from the points. "density", the default (see Breaking changes), weights each point by its local density (the points in the disc that reaches its density_k-th nearest neighbour, default 8, over the disc’s area) to the power density_power (0 to 2, default 1). The cells are compact, and at power 1 they hold about the same number of points each once there are more cells than dense places; with fewer cells the counts are about as uneven as under "kmeans". On 2,000 simulated points with 28 dense places the coefficient of variation of the cell counts was 0.90 under "kmeans" and 0.97 under "density" at 10 cells, and 0.95 and 0.31 at 60 cells. The result does not depend on the order of the rows, the unit of the coordinates or whether FNN is installed, and points at one location share a cell.

  • The same three functions gain init: "kmeans++" draws a start’s centres one at a time, each in proportion to its squared distance from those already drawn, and "random" draws distinct locations at random, as stats::kmeans() does. resolution_profile() defaults to "kmeans++", as before. The two seeding functions default to NULL: random starts for partition = "kmeans", the run they have always made, and k-means++ for partition = "density".

  • resolution_profile() and voronoi_seeds_kmeans() gain iter_max, the most iterations a start runs for. NULL, the default, is 50 for the k-means each has always run and 100 for random starts in the profile and for partition = "density". A kept start that was cut off at the limit, or at kmeans_iter in get_voronoi_seeds(), is a warning of class spatialkit_not_converged that carries level, iter and iter_max. The k-means kind from its own starts reports as before.

  • A result built with partition = "density", or with an init other than the k-means kind’s own, says so: attr(, "partition") on a profile and on seeds, $partition on a select_resolution() result, params$partition on a tessellation from build_tessellation() or create_voronoi_polygons(). The record holds kind, init, density_power and density_k, and for a profile and for seeds a seeding function placed, the iterations the kept start took and whether it converged. A selection or profile passed as the count gives the centres it scored, so the regions built are the regions scored. Results of the k-means kind from its own starts carry no record and are unchanged.

  • Under partition = "density" the profile’s wss is the within-cell sum of squares with every point counted once, so wss and elbow compare between kinds; the weighted sum the centres minimise is attr(, "partition")$objective. print() of the profile and of a selection, and summary() of the profile, name the kind. determine_optimal_levels() keeps plain k-means.

  • Two more warnings have a class. spatialkit_partition_unused: a selection or profile passed as the count together with a partition, init or density setting it was not built with; the scored centres are returned. spatialkit_empty_cells: a density partition in which a centre holds no point, which happens at counts from about a fifth of the points up, mostly from random starts.

  • summarize_by_cell() gains estimate = "pooled". Beside each mean it returns a pooled value, ..pooled_*: the cell’s mean pulled toward the count-weighted mean of the 8 cells whose observations’ centroids are nearest, ..pooled_target_*, with the weight ..pooled_w_* on its own mean. The weight grows with the cell’s count and with how much the cells differ from their neighbours. A cell with one observation gets a value; a cell with none gets NA. It works on any polygons. Every present column is unchanged, and estimate = "mean" returns the frame it always did; "pooled" is the default (see Breaking changes). attr(, "pooled") records the fit, and whether the cells predict a left-out observation better than one mean for all rows. On 200 simulated layers of 1,500 clustered observations in cells of 4.5 on average, the root mean squared error of the pooled value at held-out observations among the others was 0.96 of the plain mean’s (dev/sim-pooled-values.R; ?summarize_by_cell describes the simulation).

  • summarize_by_cell() gains obs_level: ..obs_lo_* and ..obs_hi_*, a range for one further observation in the cell, as the pooled value plus two quantiles of its leave-one-out residuals. It is a statement about observations on average and describes observations among those summarised; it is too narrow for a place with none nearby. conf_level and the ..ci_* columns are unchanged; that interval is not a range for an observation. On the same layers the range at 0.90 held 89.6 percent of the observations held out among the others and 75.1 percent of those in a held-out block, and ..ci_* at 0.90 read that way held 58.9 percent of the first. attr(, "intervals") says what each interval in the frame covers.

  • resolution_profile() gains estimate and obs_per_cell. obs_per_cell sets the ladder in observations per cell and accepts fractions; the centres are then fitted to every row. With estimate the profile adds loo, the leave-one-out error of that cell value on every row of the layer with a response, in the cells the seeds will build, with loo_se, scored_per_cell, share_alone and own_weight. It needs no variogram. print(), summary() and plot() of such a profile show it.

  • resolution_profile()’s sac accepts "auto": the variogram is estimated as before unless obs_per_cell sets the ladder, where none is fitted, cp and reliability are NA, and attr(, "cp_noise") says why. "auto" is the default (see Breaking changes).

  • resolution_profile()’s nstart, get_voronoi_seeds()’s kmeans_nstart and voronoi_seeds_kmeans()’s nstart accept NULL, the kind’s own number of starts: the earlier default for partition = "kmeans" and 3 for partition = "density". NULL is the default (see Breaking changes). On a ladder set by obs_per_cell a fit whose cost grows with the square of the rows is stopped above a limit, with an error of class spatialkit_work_limit that names the ways on; so is the search behind the weights of partition = "density" when the FNN package is not installed.

  • select_resolution() gains criterion = "size" (the level at obs_per_cell observations per cell, 4.5 unless given), "loo" (the lowest leave-one-out error) and "auto" (size for pooled values, leave-one-out for plain means). A size does not test the response, so structured is computed for it from the leave-one-out error against one mean for the layer. A profile built with estimate, passed straight to a seeding function as the count, is read by "auto", which is the default (see Breaking changes).

  • A selection made by these rules carries count_rule, and the seeds, the tessellation, the assigned layer and the summary carry it on. summarize_by_cell() warns (spatialkit_estimate_mismatch) when the count was chosen for one cell value and the summary reports the other, and (spatialkit_cells_differ) when the cells or rows it is given are not the ones the count was scored on.

  • The record holds the centres the profile scored (scored$centres). build_tessellation(method = "voronoi") and create_voronoi_polygons() build the cells of those centres in the CRS the profile worked in, with no crs or a geographic one, whatever CRS the seeds arrive in (degrees, or the CRS of a boundary they were placed in), each seed put at its centre as the record holds it. On such cells assign_features_to_polygons() gives a point on the edge between two cells the cell resolution_profile() scored it in: its nearest centre in the record’s CRS, and of two the same distance away (squared distances within one part in ten million of each other) the lower-numbered one. On gridded locations (raster cell centres, a regular sampling grid) the rows each cell holds are then the rows its count was scored on, and the summary’s check reads match. cell_values_at() places a location on such an edge in the same cell, without seeds and with the seeds in any order. Polygons without the record, cells whose record says they are other cells built from the count, and features that are not points are placed by the polygons alone.

  • New cell_values_at(): the value and interval of the cell at other locations, with each location’s distance from the nearest observation.

  • Each warning of the pooled path of summarize_by_cell() is raised once per call and reason and names the columns it applies to, in its text and in a columns field. Where the pooled columns cannot be computed they are NA with a warning and the plain columns are returned; the function raises no error for them.

  • New condition classes: spatialkit_pool_unavailable, spatialkit_pool_degenerate, spatialkit_pool_few_cells, spatialkit_pool_few_df, spatialkit_pool_rows_skipped, spatialkit_repeated_locations, spatialkit_few_residuals, spatialkit_estimate_mismatch, spatialkit_cells_differ, spatialkit_size_not_reached, spatialkit_ladder_unused, spatialkit_moran_skipped, and the error class spatialkit_work_limit. spatialkit_no_structure is also raised by summarize_by_cell(estimate = "pooled"), and by the seeding functions for a count set by a size.

  • make_folds() gains method = "knndm", the k-fold version of nearest-neighbour distance matching (Linnenbrink et al. 2024). It builds k folds whose held-out distances are as close as a set of candidates allows to the distances from prediction_points to the data, and has no row limit, where "nndm" takes at most 5,000 rows and one fit per point. The candidates are the random partition and, for up to 50 cluster counts, the samples clustered on their coordinates and packed into k folds; the one with the smallest Wasserstein distance to the target is returned, and params$candidates lists them all. The match is coarser than NNDM’s. Two cases raise a classed warning: prediction points nearer to the data than any fold can hold a point out (spatialkit_nndm_out_of_reach), and folds still closer to their training data than the prediction points are to the samples (spatialkit_knndm_short_of_target). The rule that packs clusters into folds is this package’s and was not checked against CAST::knndm().

  • make_folds() gains max_test for "buffered_loo" and "nndm": folds are built for a seeded random subset of that many held-out points, with every row still available for training. "buffered_loo" then runs on layers its storage limit refuses. It does not lift the 5,000-row limit of "nndm"; "knndm" is the design above it.

  • fold_separation() gains prediction_points: the locations to be predicted. The held-out distances are then set beside the distances from those points to the training data, and the result’s target attribute carries a reading: "closer" (the cross-validated error tends to read low for that target), "farther" (it tends to read high), "matched" or "mixed". NNDM and kNNDM folds are read against the prediction distances they carry. The table gains target_median_dist and dist_gap.

  • Every classed estimate_sac_range() result says how far its nugget can be trusted. nugget_at_bound is TRUE when the fit put the nugget at zero, which is the bound of the search and not an estimate; first_lag is the shortest lag resolved; short_lag_semivariance is the semivariance of nearest-neighbour pairs with no model, an upper bound on the nugget. ?sac_nugget describes them. The result also records n_used, n_missing, n_subsampled, structure_p, morans_i, lags and lag_boundaries.

  • estimate_sac_range() reads rows that share a location as one place. The test for spatial structure is made on the location means, pairs at zero separation are in no lag bin, and their semivariance, the variance between visits, is returned as zero_lag_semivariance. When the rows outnumber the locations by 30 or more, the nugget fitted to the variogram is not let under it (nugget_floor). With detrend = "reml" the fit takes one row a location, drawn under seed, and takes no such floor. A layer needs 30 distinct locations, not only 30 rows.

  • select_resolution(criterion = "cp") says when the count is not identified. structured is FALSE when one cell for the whole layer scores no more than tol above the optimum (below it included), or when the cell means at the optimum differ from one mean by no more than chance (an F test at 5 percent, adjusted for the levels searched; structure_p). The pick is unchanged. On white noise of 300 points it was FALSE on 145 of 150 layers. The functions that take the count raise a warning of class spatialkit_no_structure. resolution_profile() keeps what one cell scores in attr(, "one_cell").

  • determine_optimal_levels() gains on_no_elbow = c("na", "warn", "error"); its default is in Breaking changes. "na" returns NA_integer_ in place of the chord rule’s answer and "warn" returns that answer, each with a warning of class spatialkit_no_elbow that carries the count and structured = FALSE; "error" stops with an error of that class. criterion = "morans_i" and "combined" run with a response and no predictors, where they fell back to the geometric ranking. A layer of one or two points, or with every point on one location, is read by the same rule (NA at the default, 1 under "warn"); it returned 1 with nothing said.

  • A GWR fit gives its standard errors. coef(fit, se = TRUE) returns the local estimates with their standard errors and t values, and predict(fit, newdata, se.fit = TRUE) the standard error of the fitted value (se.fit) and of a new observation (se.pred). They follow GWmodel’s definitions, treat the bandwidth as known, and are not adjusted for the number of local tests. print(summary(fit)) shows the effective number of parameters and the AICc and RMSE of a global least-squares fit on the same rows (info$global_ols): a GWR whose AICc is no lower has not shown that its coefficients vary.

  • fit_gwr_model(predictor_vars = character(0)) fits the model with a local intercept alone, the kernel-weighted mean of the response. It is the baseline a GWR with predictors has to beat, and select_features_forward() fits it as the null model of a GWR sweep.

  • predict() on a GWR says when a location is beyond the reach of the fit. When a new location’s nearest training point is farther than the widest kernel at any training location reaches, the prediction is returned and a warning of class spatialkit_gwr_extrapolation gives the count. The warning that counts NA predictions has class spatialkit_gwr_not_estimable. Both carry their counts as fields. predict_surface(), cv_gwr(), cv_spatial(), cv_block_size_sweep() and select_features_forward() raise each once per call, with totals.

  • gwr_model_selection() scores the model without predictors as <none>, and best is character(0) when it wins. The table gains delta, each model’s criterion minus the best one’s, and print() lists the models within 2 of the best and names the smallest (within_2, smallest_within_2). The sweep runs on the package’s own solve, so a candidate that is constant inside some windows no longer stops it. dmat_max_n is accepted and ignored.

  • area_of_applicability() gains categorical = c("refuse", "indicator", "drop") for factor and character predictors. "refuse" is the default, as before. "indicator" codes each level as a 0/1 column with one shared scale per predictor, and a row on a level no training row has gets DI = Inf. "drop" computes the index on the numeric predictors.

  • select_features_forward() gains null_fn, a function that fits the no-predictor model for a learner that cannot. history always starts with the step-0 row and gains gain, fold_gain and fold_gain_se; the result gains baseline (its type, score and the path reached) and fold_scores.

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model() reports what its GP basis resolves. The reduced-rank basis cannot represent structure below a floor, 14 to 33 percent of the extent along each axis at the defaults, stored in map units as $info$gp_resolution and shown by print(). The new argument gp_resolution asks for a resolution in map units and derives gp_k and the length-scale prior from it, up to 50 functions per dimension. Before compiling, a variogram range below the floor can raise a warning of class spatialkit_gp_resolution. After sampling, $info$gp_adequacy$status is "ok", "below_resolution", "unresolved_short_range", "no_signal_above_floor" or "not_checked", from the length-scale posterior, the process’s share of the variance and a short-lag Moran’s I of the residuals; the two that say the basis is too coarse raise spatialkit_gp_adequacy. convergence_ok stays about the sampler.

  • cv_bayes()’s fold_metrics and compare_models() gain a gp_adequacy column beside convergence_ok. cv_bayes() and cv_spatial() collect the classed warnings a Bayesian fit raises in each fold and raise each class once, naming the folds (fields folds, fold_messages).

  • build_tessellation() and create_voronoi_polygons() gain cover: the observations, or a polygon, that the cells have to hold when the generators are seeds made elsewhere. Seeds with neither a boundary nor a cover raise a warning of class spatialkit_no_cover. params gains boundary_source, n_outside and cover_outside.

  • assign_features_to_polygons() records the features no polygon holds as attr(, "unassigned") (n, which), beside "ties", and names the column the polygon IDs were read from when polygon_id_col is absent. The new argument quiet silences that message.

  • fold_separation() measures what blocked cross-validation is for: the distance from every held-out point to its nearest training point, summarised per fold. Until now the only evidence a fold scheme worked was a proxy — the block size compared against the estimated autocorrelation range, which make_folds() warns about. That is a statement about the design; this is the result. The returned table carries n_train, n_test, n_blocks, min_dist, median_dist and mean_cor, the mean correlation: the mean of exp(-3 d / range) over the held-out points, so a point at a twentieth of the range weighs more than one at nine tenths of it. Nothing is estimated: the distances come from the geometry and the range is the one the folds already carry or the one you pass. A range that records its CRS (the folds’ own params$sac_range and params$crs, or an estimate_sac_range() result) is compared with distances measured in that CRS, so a copy of the layer in other units gives the same answer; sac and the distances are in the units of the CRS the crs attribute names, metres for lon/lat input. fold is the fold_id a cv_*() result’s $folds carries, so a join on it pairs each fold’s error with its own distances. A units object for sac is refused. As in cv_*(), a make_folds() result whose recorded rows sit at other locations in data_sf is refused; the location check is skipped when one layer is POINT and the other is not, so folds built on polygons still measure their pointized copy. print() reports the distances and says which way the score tends to err only when it is given the prediction locations (prediction_points, below); it shows the first ten folds of a design with more than twenty. The range line gives the CRS’s unit (“in metres”).

  • summary() on a resolution_profile() puts every criterion’s pick in one table: the level each prefers, the flat region around it, whether a ladder bound is doing the choosing, and the levels that lie in every band. Reading the criteria off a profile took one select_resolution() call per criterion, and the comparison had to be assembled by hand. The intersection of the bands is often empty, which is a result rather than a failure: it says the field has no single resolution that satisfies every way of asking. Nothing in the table chooses, and the help page says so. Each region comes back in full on the "bands" attribute.

  • Every cv_*() result now says what became of each fold. fold_status is a data.frame with one row per fold supplied — fold, status, message — where status is "ok", "error" (the fit or its predict() threw; message is the error text), "skipped" (nothing scorable: too few matched rows, a prediction of the wrong length, no finite observed/predicted pair), "dropped" (an empty test set or fewer than two training rows once incomplete rows were removed, so the fold never reached the fitter) or "worker_error" (a parallel worker died). The per-fold error text was already collected and thrown away except when every fold failed, so a partial failure — “3 of 5 folds produced predictions” — left its causes only in console scrollback, which a script, a callr job or a knitted document does not keep. This is worth most where a run is expensive: a cv_bayes() fold whose sampler failed now names the reason in the returned object. Beside it, orphan_rows holds the row IDs no fold names (they enter no training set and are never scored — non-empty only when the folds were built on a different or subsetted layer), n_unknown_ids counts the distinct rows the folds name that the data does not have, and n_dropped the rows prep_model_data() removed before any fold was fitted. The four together account for every row and every fold, so n_folds_attempted - n_folds_succeeded never has to be explained from the log. A parallel worker that was killed outright (for lack of memory, say) is a "worker_error" too and enters the first-error text; it used to show as "skipped" (“no result returned”) and was left out of that text. An "ok" row carries a message when the fold’s fold_info_fn failed.

  • prep_model_data() records what it removed. attr(x, "dropped") is a list with n, n_geometry, which (positions in the input), row_id (when the layer carries ..row_id) and reason, one of "geometry", "missing" or "non_finite" per dropped row. The three masks behind that decision were already computed and collapsed into a log line; the row identities reached nothing, and through the eight-plus internal call sites even the count was invisible, so a fit’s $n was the post-cleaning row count with nothing saying how many rows were lost or why. Every fit now carries the count as $info$n_dropped, and every cv_*() result as n_dropped. Silently losing a third of the rows is a classic cause of a suspiciously good score. The layer carries the class "spatialkit_rows" after "sf" (c("sf", "spatialkit_rows", "data.frame")): [ returns a plain layer without the record, and dplyr::bind_rows(), vctrs::vec_rbind() and dplyr::union_all() return a plain sf (with the class ahead of "sf" they failed on two layers with the same record, ‘attr(obj, “sf_column”) does not point to a geometry column’). dplyr::filter(), slice(), arrange() and distinct() now drop the record as [ does (they kept it, so filter() down to 3 of 5 rows still reported the parent’s counts). Each record carries n_rows, the number of rows it was made for. sf::st_drop_geometry() keeps the rows and the record; binding such data frames keeps the first one’s record, whose n_rows then no longer matches, and the package’s readers ignore it.

  • make_folds(method = "block_kfold") returns the block design it built the folds from. assignment gains a third column, block_id; params gains blocks (an sf layer of the block polygons in the CRS the folds were built in, numbered to match), block_sizes (points per block, indexed by block_id, so a block kept empty by drop_empty_blocks = FALSE shows as a zero) and fold_blocks (which blocks were packed into each fold). blocks$source_row is the row each block came from in the layer it originated in — a cell’s index in the full grid_nx by grid_ny grid, or the row of the blocks argument — because dropping the empty blocks renumbers the rest: nine supplied blocks of which three are empty come back as six rows numbered 1 to 6, and a join by row position would mis-attribute every block after the first gap. blocks[params$blocks$source_row, ] recovers them with their own columns and in their own order. The folds account for every block exactly once, empty ones included, so a fold’s territory on the map is all of its blocks rather than only those holding points; and blocks_used is the number of blocks the design has, which equals nrow(params$blocks) and length(params$block_sizes), with sum(params$block_sizes > 0) giving how many of them hold points. The grid is the design of a blocked cross-validation: without it a user could not draw the blocks over their data, see that 40 of 64 blocks were empty, or tell whether a fold is one contiguous region or several. plot_folds() now draws those outlines under the points when the folds carry them, and takes blocks = FALSE to suppress them. Its subtitle states the parameter that sets how far the held-out points sit from their training data (the block size, the buffer, the number of location groups or the median NNDM exclusion), with the units of the folds’ CRS; folds built from points without a CRS get no units rather than “(NA units)”.

  • estimate_sac_range()’s returns are uniform. The four directional variograms and their fits run unconditionally on every call, and the rejected-range paths used to discard them — precisely where a user most needs to know whether the field is anisotropic. Every classed return now carries directional, anisotropy and anisotropy_used, and three new attributes report the sweep rather than collapsing it: directional_status (per azimuth, why that direction is NA in directional — "ok", "over_cutoff", "not_converged" or "no_fit", which were indistinguishable before), directional_fitted (the range each direction’s fit reported whether or not it was usable, so a refused directional range — the most informative number in an anisotropic failure — stays recoverable) and, under keep_directional_fits = TRUE, directional_fits (each direction’s empirical variogram and fitted model). Those four objects are off by default because they dominate the result when present — 42.2 KB of a 58.8 KB object at n = 400, against 16.6 KB without them — and make_folds(auto_range = TRUE) calls this on every build. print() names the reason and the refused value for a direction it cannot use.

  • A roster of quantities the package already computed and dropped are now returned. summarize_by_cell() attaches the Kish ICCs it estimated as attr(, "icc") whether or not either was large enough to apply — the case with no "deff_applied" is exactly the one where a user wants to know what the ICC came out as — and the "variogram" path adds deff_rows, the per-cell design effect at the cell’s row count that the log line reduced to a median and a max. A summarize_by_cell() call that requests a design effect (any deff other than 1) also returns a logical deff_applied column, TRUE on every row when a correction was applied (a Kish fallback included; deff_method names the correction) and FALSE when none was (the standard errors are then the uncorrected ones, or NA where a Kish ICC cannot be estimated); unlike the "deff_applied" attribute it survives rbind() and dplyr::bind_rows() of many results. At the default deff = 1 the column is not added. assign_features_to_polygons() reports the features that matched more than one polygon and had the tie_break rule decide for them, as attr(, "ties") and a log line; a tie-break firing on a third of the features means the polygon layer overlaps and every cell count built from it is suspect. The layer carries the "spatialkit_rows" class after "sf", as prep_model_data()’s does, so binding such layers returns a plain sf. The "ties" record is dropped by the same dplyr row verbs as prep_model_data()’s, and with largest = TRUE it also counts features that overlap two or more polygons by exactly the same area. ensure_projected() attaches crs_choice, the projections it considered with each one’s measured worst-case distance error. Every path that picks a local projection reports what it picked, the two that compare nothing included: a UTM zone on a local extent, and the equal-area projection chosen for a layer straddling the antimeridian. residual_morans_i() returns the residual kurtosis the randomisation variance conditions on, the design rank p behind the residual moments, exact, whether those moments are exact for these residuals, and weights_summary, a description of the weight matrix it used: n, storage (the matrix class), neighbours (the smallest and largest number of neighbours any row has, NA for a dense matrix, where counting them would allocate a second one), kept and desc, the line print() shows. The matrix itself comes back as weights under keep_weights = TRUE and is NULL otherwise, because it is n by n: at n = 500 it is 50.3 KB of a 53.5 KB object in its sparse form, 112.7 KB at n = 120 when the dense fallback is taken (going sparse needs both FNN and Matrix, so a no-Suggests install always falls back), and 191 MB at the n = 5000 that fallback is capped at — against the 3.2 KB everything else occupies — and scoring a list of fits would hold one matrix per fit. The result is classed "morans_i" and prints through a print() method that shows the statistic, its null and the weights line; [ drops the class, and $, [[ and unlist() read the result exactly as for a plain list. fit_gwr_model() keeps info$nonfinite_coef, the per-row, per-term mask behind n_local_singular, and fit_bayesian_spatial_model() keeps rhat_failed / neff_failed, the parameters that failed each convergence check by name — “max R-hat 1.09” is not actionable where “sdgp_gp..x..y has R-hat 1.09” is. determine_optimal_levels()’s model-aware diagnostics gain knee_k and failed_k (whose interpolated WSS entries are not measurements). build_tessellation() records the points whose cell assignment was repaired by nearest-cell snapping, and how far outside each sat, as params$snapped — a comment had long said it should. area_of_applicability() returns the scaling (per-predictor training centre and SD) the dissimilarity index is computed in, without which a location’s DI cannot be traced to the predictor that put it outside, and n_outliers, the training DI values the threshold’s fence set aside. get_voronoi_seeds(method = "kmeans") returns the clustering as attr(, "kmeans") — which cloud points fed which seed, the cluster sizes and the within-cluster sums of squares. gwr_model_selection() reports criterion_by_name, criterion_column and criterion_verified, so a script can gate on the case its log calls “unverified” instead of reading the label.

  • estimate_sac_range()’s result gains a plot() method. plot(estimate_sac_range(pts, "z")) draws the empirical variogram, with the fitted model and the effective range overlaid where a range was identified, and a subtitle saying why not where it was not: the variogram never reached a sill, both model fits were singular, the optimiser halted, or a range_frac below 1 refused a range inside the fitted lags. Nothing is recomputed — the plot reads the attributes the estimate already carries — and the same drawing routine now serves plot.spatial_fit(type = "variogram"), so the two pictures agree. The “attached for inspection” messages estimate_sac_range() logs when it returns NA used to point at plot(type = "variogram"), which is the method for a fitted model and could not take the estimate; they now point at plot() on the returned value.

  • summarize_by_cell() gains conf_level. With conf_level = 0.95, every numeric response and predictor column gets four more columns beside its ..sd_* and ..se_*: ..neff_*, the column’s effective sample size in the cell (its non-missing count over its design effect — the per-column version of cell_weight); ..df_*, the degrees of freedom the interval uses; and ..ci_lo_* / ..ci_hi_*, a t interval for the cell mean as an estimate of the grand mean, built on the design-effect-corrected standard error. The default conf_level = NULL adds none of these columns. The degrees of freedom are n - 1 at deff = 1, for a numeric deff and for deff = "kish", because the interval’s spread is estimated from the within-cell variance, whose n - 1 df survive exchangeable correlation whatever the design effect (measured 95% coverage on the Kish path at an ICC of 0.2 / 0.6 / 0.9: 0.954 / 0.953 / 0.952; an effective-sample-size df of neff - 1 gives 0.992 / 1.000 / 1.000 and is not used). Under deff = "variogram" the df are the Satterthwaite

    1. moment-matched df of the within-cell variance under the fitted correlation, a fraction of n - 1 that shrinks with the range: 0.960 and 0.958 coverage at exponential ranges of 150 and 400 on a 1000-unit domain, against 0.931 and 0.918 with n - 1. The help page’s “Confidence intervals” section has the reasoning and the numbers. ..neff_*, like ..df_* and the interval, is NA for a column with a single non-missing value in the cell, where cell_weight still counts it.

  • compare_models_cv() gains block_size and auto_range, and now hands response_var and predictor_vars to make_folds() when it builds the shared fold set. With the defaults the folds are the same geometric blocks as before, so an existing comparison does not move; what changes is that the fold-leakage diagnostic (above) can now fire for the one function that compares models, which until now was the one whose folds could never be checked against the range. select_features_forward() gains auto_range for its inner folds for the same reason, and records it in $params. A shared fold set that cannot be built is an error. It used to be a log line and a fall-back to each backend’s default blocks, which were given neither argument: block_size = 1e6 (one block, which cv_rf() refuses) returned a five-fold comparison on geometric blocks, and auto_range = TRUE the small blocks it exists to prevent, with no R condition.

  • compare_models_cv()$overall carries the Bayesian backend’s calibration when a Bayesian model ran: coverage_50, coverage_80, coverage_95 and mean_CRPS, the same fold-weighted summary cv_bayes() returns as predictive_coverage, with NA on the GWR and RF rows. A model that predicts well on average and covers badly (Heaton et al. 2019) is now visible in the table a user picks from, not only in $bayes_cv. model stays the last column.

  • fit_rf_model() gains replace and sample_fraction, which reach ranger::ranger() as replace and sample.fraction; both were already accepted through ..., but are now recorded in $info and printed with the fit (“Sampling: bootstrap, with replacement (100.0% of rows per tree)”). The defaults are ranger’s, so no forest changes. The help page carries Strobl et al.’s (2007) case for replace = FALSE. Passing the ranger spellings through ... is now refused like the other arguments the wrapper sets. replace = FALSE with sample_fraction = 1 grows every tree on every row, so no row is out of bag. The fit now warns that fitted(), the OOB error and the permutation importance are all NaN (they were NaN in silence), and print() on such a fit says the OOB error and the permutation importance are undefined, where it dropped the OOB line and printed the importance line empty. area_of_applicability(weights = pmax(imp, 0)) failed on that importance with a hint to use the very pmax() it had been given, because pmax() keeps NaN; it now names the predictors whose weight is NaN, says why (no row is out of bag), and says what to do instead: refit with out-of-bag rows, or pass weights = NULL. With permutation importance, the fit’s own warning now says as much: area_of_applicability() cannot be weighted by that importance, so pass weights = NULL.

  • area_of_applicability() records the method of the folds its threshold came from as $params$folds_method ("block_kfold", "random_kfold", … from a make_folds() result; "labels" or "splits" when the input cannot say) and prints it, because the threshold is a statistic of a cross-validated hold-out and pairs with the CV error from the same kind of hold-out. An AOA built on random_kfold folds logs a caution saying it does not belong beside a blocked cv_*() result.

  • estimate_sac_range() gains detrend = c("ols", "reml") and reml_max_n. A variogram fitted to least-squares residuals underestimates the range, because the trend fit absorbs part of the long-wavelength variation (Lark, Cullis and Welham 2006). Measured for this estimator on simulated fields (n = 300, true effective range 300), as the median ratio to the estimate from the true field: a white-noise covariate 1.00; a spatially smooth covariate 0.97; a linear trend in the coordinates 0.92; a quadratic one 0.75. detrend = "reml" fits the trend and an exponential-plus-nugget covariance together by REML with nlme::gls() and returns the REML range — 0.95 to 1.06 on the same designs — with the empirical variogram of the REML residuals attached for inspection. It is cubic in n, so it runs on at most reml_max_n

    1. points; a fit that does not converge falls back to OLS with a warning. The default stays "ols", so nothing changes unless asked; the help page’s new section carries the numbers. Iterating GLS trend fits against variogram refits (Neuman and Jacobson 1984) was measured too and recovers only part of the bias (0.80 in the quadratic case), so it was not added. nlme joins Suggests. A fitted range too short for enough pairs of points to lie inside it is refused, with rejected_reason = "fitted range is below the shortest lag fitted" and the bound it fell short of as the range_floor attribute. For the least-squares fits the bound is the shortest lag the empirical variogram resolves (the mean separation in its first bin); it did not fire on white noise or on fields with a 60 m range. The REML range is fitted to the point pairs, not to those bins, so its bound is the distance within which 30 pairs of the points the REML fit used lie, or that first lag when it is shorter. On white noise (n = 300, 30 draws) the REML fit returned ranges of 0.18–23.6 m in 19 draws (one of 0.27 m sized a 3642 x 3676 block grid, refused as a unit mistake); the 16 of them up to 12.5 m are refused and the estimate is finite in 13 of 30. REML estimates of a true 30 m range that the first lag alone would have refused (14.5–28.8 m, in 10 of 20 draws at n = 400 and 6 of 15 at n = 300) are returned, and at n = 400 the same holds at cutoff = 0.5 and 0.1. The bound is about identification, not a test for spatial structure. A refused REML result keeps its reml list.

  • sac_nugget() returns the nugget variance behind an estimate_sac_range() result, and every classed result — identified or rejected — now carries it as a nugget attribute (NA when no model could be fitted). It was reachable before only by reading the Nug row of the attached gstat model. Results also record detrend_method ("ols", "reml" or NA), and with detrend = "reml" a reml list (n_used, subsampled, nugget_prop, sigma2).

  • estimate_sac_range() refuses a range fitted through an empirical variogram that decreases with distance over its shorter lags: a net fall of more than 15% of the mean semivariance there, weighted by pairs. A model that rises to a sill has nothing to identify on such a curve, and the result is NA with rejected_reason = "empirical variogram decreases with distance", the refused value in rejected_range, and the variogram attached; plot() captions it. The shape is what a periodic (hole-effect) structure or a variance that differs between a dense cluster and the rest of the layer produces — measured on 60 draws each: 98% of fields with a periodic component and 100% of the clustered case are flagged, against 0% of an exponential field with a range of 100 or more on a 1000-unit extent, 2–3% at very short ranges, 2% of white noise — and not what a trend produces, which is a variogram that rises without a sill and is refused as before. The one other path that returned a bare NA from inside a completed fit (a non-positive fitted range) now returns the classed, inspectable shape too.

  • resolution_profile() and select_resolution(): the number of cells, scored on every criterion at once. Given a ladder argument (n_levels, for one; at the defaults it scores one size, see Breaking changes), resolution_profile() runs a log-spaced ladder of level counts from 2 to a ceiling the support implies (floor(n / min_cell_n), where n is the rows of the layer that carry a response, not the sample_n subsample the k-means runs on), reports the floor the autocorrelation range implies (ceiling(area / range^2)), fits each level as the best of its partition’s k-means++ starts (25 for partition = "kmeans"), and returns a data.frame with the WSS elbow statistic (read on log-log axes, and NA when the points have no cluster structure to bend the curve), Mallows’ C_p of the piecewise-constant approximation of the response (or of its residuals on the predictors, fitted on the rows with a complete response and predictors, with the nugget from the fitted variogram as the noise variance and the penalty set for the whole layer), the standardised residual Moran’s z of the cell means (a diagnostic, not a count rule), and an analytic reliability of the cell means — the share of their spread that is between-cell signal rather than sampling noise, from the variogram alone via Krige’s additivity relation (Cressie 1996), the shrinkage factor of Fay and Herriot (1979) — plus the cell-support and cell-diameter columns and the between-restart spread. A floor above the ceiling is reported as a finding rather than resolved silently. select_resolution() reads a level off one criterion together with its flat region and says when a bound, not the criterion, is choosing. The flat region is a set, not an interval: the criterion curves are not monotone, so a region can skip a rung of the ladder, and it is printed as the runs the criterion accepts (“19 to 21, 26, 31 to 33”) rather than a range that would quietly include the levels it rejected. Two things measured before this shipped, both on the help page: on smooth fields with a small nugget C_p descends to the support ceiling (every replicate at effective ranges 90–900 with nugget 0.3 on a unit sill; interior only at nugget 2), and the reliability optimum agrees with the empirical one from true block means on simulated fields but is broad — flat to within 2 percent over a factor of 3–6 in the number of cells. Read the flat region. determine_optimal_levels() is unchanged in shape and keeps its integer-vector interface. A supplied sac whose range was refused (an NA with a rejected_reason) is not read as accepted: cp keeps that fit’s nugget and warns, naming the reason, reliability is NA (it needs the range), and a fit that did not converge, or whose range is below the shortest lag fitted, gives neither its nugget nor its range (the whole refused fit used to be used, and a correlation function whose range could be many times the extent pinned the reliability optimum to the first level, with no R warning). A range below the shortest lag means the structure cannot be told from a nugget, so the nugget is not identified either: on white noise detrended by REML it was 6e-7 on a sill of 0.99, and C_p, with no penalty, ran to the support ceiling (33 cells). A nugget of 0 (under 1e-4 of the sill, since a REML fit stops short of its bound: 6e-7 passed a test for exactly 0), on which C_p has no penalty and falls to the ceiling, is warned about, and so is a sac whose detrended flag does not match the variable scored (a residual variogram on the raw response moved the C_p pick from 2–4 cells to the ceiling of 44 in five of five simulated fields); attr(x, "variogram") records detrended. When no sac is passed, these warnings name the variogram the profile estimated (kept in attr(x, "sac")), not a sac argument the caller never gave. A supplied sac is read in its own CRS: the points are transformed to attr(sac, "crs") first, as summarize_by_cell() does (a range in US feet put the floor of a metre layer at 2 where the same range in metres put it at 8). A sac given as a units object (set_units(1.5, "km")) or a character string is refused by name; a units object used to be read as a number in the CRS units, so 1.5 km became a range of 1.5 m and a floor of 41 million cells. A plain number is taken as the range alone: it sets the floor, and reliability is NA. Wherever the variogram gives no nugget (none was fitted, its fit did not converge, its range is below the shortest lag, or sac is a range alone), cp takes Mallows’ own noise variance, the residual mean square RSS / (m - L) of the finest level whose cells hold two scored rows each on average, and the profile warns; attr(x, "cp_noise") records which variance was used, and the print says so. It counts the structure within those cells as noise too, so on average it is no smaller than the nugget and errs towards fewer cells. cp used to be NA at every level in all four cases, so a workflow that reads C_p by default (build_tessellation(approx_n_cells = <profile>), summary()) fell through to another criterion with a log line at most. Reliability’s domain term is taken over the convex hull the area is measured on, not the bounding box: on a 3000 x 120 strip the reliability pick is 6 cells whether the strip lies axis-aligned or rotated by 45 degrees (it was 8 and 2), and 10 either way on a square (it was 10 and 8), and reliability values shift slightly on every profile. Row order does not change the profile (see the determine_optimal_levels() item under Bug fixes); over permutations of one 2000-point layer, WSS used to move by up to 2.6 percent and the C_p pick across its flat region (222, 173 and 135 cells). The ceiling reaches the number of distinct locations when locations repeat (and explicit levels up to it are kept) instead of stopping one short; with no location repeated, the print says the ceiling is one short of the points rather than crediting the distinct locations. Points with empty or non-finite coordinates are dropped with an R warning, as in determine_optimal_levels(); it was a log line alone. range_floor = FALSE, the default, starts the ladder at 2 whatever the range and only reports the floor, so profiles whose range estimates differ (cross-validation folds) have comparable ladders; with the floor applying on one fold and not the next, reliability and the elbow moved by a factor of 10–15 between folds. range_floor = TRUE starts the ladder at the floor. Under select_on = "split" a supplied sac is flagged in the log, since it must be fitted on the selection half, and the help page shows the two-call workflow.

  • select_on = c("all", "split") on determine_optimal_levels(), resolution_profile() and select_features_forward().
