Whenever a selection reads the response — a level count chosen under criterion = "morans_i", or a predictor set chosen by a forward sweep — what is estimated afterwards on the result is post-selection, and its standard errors are descriptive rather than at nominal coverage (Gao, Bien and Witten 2022). select_on = "split" is sample splitting: the layer is cut into two spatially blocked halves (make_folds(k = 2, method = "block_kfold")), the selection reads the response on the first only, and the row positions of both come back (as a "split" attribute on the first two functions, as $split on the third) so the estimation can be done on the half the selection never saw. The positions index the layer as passed, for all three functions (select_features_forward()’s were positions after its completeness filter, so with seven incomplete rows pts[fs$split$estimation, ] held 47 rows of the selection half and 4 of the dropped ones). When the default six-block split leaves fewer than 10 points in a half (a small layer, or a small group far from the rest), it is retried on grids of about 16, 36 and 100 blocks, with a warning, instead of stopping, and the split records grid, n_blocks, balance (a 2:1 split on clustered layers used to pass silently) and each half’s extent. The halves are not independent: blocking reduces the dependence across their shared border but does not remove it (85 percent of the estimation points of the package’s test layer lie within the fitted range of a selection point), and the seed decides only which side selects, not where the cut falls. The level-count functions still draw their cells on every point, so the count they return is a count for the whole layer it will be applied to. select_features_forward() also returns score_holdout: the selected set fitted on the selection half and scored on the other, the honest number its selection-internal score is not. The cost is precision — half the points estimate, and a contiguous spatial half is less efficient than an exchangeable one (García Rasines and Young 2023). Data thinning (Neufeld et al. 2024) and data fission (Leiner et al. 2023) keep the whole sample and are noted on the help page, not implemented. Under criterion = "combined", which no longer ranks by the response (see Breaking changes), the split changes only the rows its diagnostics read.

  • make_folds() gains blocks: a polygon layer (sf or sfc) to use as the blocks of method = "block_kfold" in place of the grid it would otherwise build — the $cells of a build_tessellation() result, hexagons, watersheds, administrative units, the $blocks of blockCV::cv_spatial(). Each point takes the block that contains it and the blocks are assigned to folds exactly as grid cells are, so the fold builder can now consume every shape the tessellation half of the package produces. The grid-sizing arguments and boundary are ignored with a log line, auto_range compares the estimated range against the blocks instead of resizing them, and the leakage warning uses the median over blocks of the side of the square with the block’s area (params$block_scale). Points inside no block are assigned to the nearest one with a warning that counts them, except points within a millionth of the extent of a block — an edge that reprojection moved by a rounding error; points inside more than one block take the first, with a warning when the blocks concerned overlap in area rather than share an edge. params gains n_blocks (before empties were dropped; for a grid, grid_nx * grid_ny, the cells a boundary clips away included), blocks_supplied and block_scale on every block_kfold result; grid_nx/grid_ny are NA for supplied blocks. A blocks layer without a CRS is brought into the points’ CRS with an R warning naming it, as boundary is.

  • make_folds() gains balance_tol, the largest-to-smallest fold size ratio above which block_kfold reports its folds as imbalanced. The check was always there at a hard-coded 3:1, and it was a log line only; it is now an R warning (Inf disables it), the ratio achieved is returned as params$balance_ratio, and the help page says which methods balance what: only block_kfold balances point counts, by packing blocks largest first into the fold with the fewest points so far. No search over packings was added, because the packing is not where the imbalance comes from. Measured against the optimum by enumeration (two folds, up to ten blocks, heavy-tailed sizes), the greedy packing is optimal in 72 percent of cases and within two points of optimal on average; a local search with 30 random restarts moved the ratio by 0.004 on average over 480 block-size vectors and never brought one of the 91 above 3:1 below it. The remedy for an imbalance past the tolerance is the block design — the warning now says so — and blocks is how to supply one: on clustered layouts where the geometric grid exceeded 3:1 in 22 percent of draws (median 1.8, worst 6.3), Voronoi cells around 15 get_voronoi_seeds(method = "kmeans") seeds never exceeded 1.3 (median 1.09). With the default tolerance the folds of every existing call are unchanged.

  • metrics on cv_spatial(), cv_gwr(), cv_bayes(), cv_rf() and compare_models_cv(): a scoring function of your own, function(y, yhat) returning a named numeric vector (a named list of scalars or a one-row data frame also serve), applied the way the built-in metrics are — once per fold, so each name becomes a column of fold_metrics, and once to the pooled out-of-sample predictions, so each name becomes a column of overall — on the same finite pairs RMSE uses. This is the way to score what the Gaussian set cannot: a Poisson deviance, a log score on a probability, a weighted loss. The contract is strict where it should be (every element named, names unique and not a built-in column, one number per name — anything else is an error, because a scoring function of the wrong shape is a mistake to surface) and forgiving where it should be (a function that throws on a fold is logged and its columns are NA there; a fold is never dropped for it). Nor may a name reuse a per-fold extra (CRPS, coverage_*, gp_k, gp_n_basis, n_draws, bandwidth, or a name the fold_info_fn returns) or mean_CRPS: each used to replace the package’s value silently, and cv_bayes()$predictive_coverage then reported the user’s number. The empty frames of a run where every fold failed carry the columns, typed, when the function can be called on zero-length input. compare_models_cv() hands one function to every backend and protects it like the fold arguments, so the columns of its overall are comparable across rows. fold_info_fn is documented as the per-fold half of the same mechanism, with access to the fitted object and the held-out layer.

  • ensure_projected() gains purpose = c("distance", "area"). The default is what it always did: for lon/lat input, the candidate that distorts distances least. With "area" — densities or rates per cell are going to be computed — the choice is made among equal-area projections only (a Lambert azimuthal centred on the data, or an Albers conic where its parallels do not degenerate, whichever distorts distances less), which a UTM zone never enters, and global coverage gets Equal Earth rather than Web Mercator. Already-projected input is still returned untouched, but its area distortion over the extent is now measured — the spread of planar-to-geodesic area ratios over probe polygons — and logged as a warning above 1 percent. Measured: a UTM zone edge to edge 0.25 percent, a 2.5-degree extent inside one 0.04 percent, the conterminous United States forced into one zone 14 percent, Web Mercator over 2.5 degrees of latitude at 48N 4 percent, an equal-area projection a few tenths of a percent (the sphere the geodesic areas are computed on against the ellipsoid). The measurement works whether sf_use_s2() is on or off (with it off and no lwgeom it returned NA, so summarize_by_cell(area = TRUE) refused every grid and purpose = "area" skipped its warning), and its probe polygons are densified before their geodesic area is taken, so an equal-area grid over a near-global extent no longer measures 10 percent. With purpose = "area", a single polygon’s candidates are scored rather than falling back to the Lambert azimuthal unmeasured.

  • summarize_by_cell() gains area = TRUE: with cells_sf, the result carries cell_area (planar, in the squared units of the cells’ CRS; for lon/lat cells the geodesic area in square metres, not a planar area in squared degrees) and n_per_area, a point density; a rate of anything else is its agg_funs sum over cell_area. The request is refused with an error — not answered with a number — when the cells’ CRS distorts areas across them by more than 1 percent by the measurement above, because a density is a comparison between cells and means nothing where the map scale differs from one cell to the next; the message names the CRS, the figure and the remedy. A cell with no observations gets NA, not zero. Lon/lat cells pass the distortion check by construction; with s2 switched off their area needs lwgeom, and the request is refused without it. The measured spread is attached as attr(, "area_error"). A cells_sf with no ID column the summaries can be joined on is an error under area = TRUE, since the area columns cannot be produced.

  • build_tessellation(approx_n_cells = ) and get_voronoi_seeds(n = ) accept what the level-selection step returned: the integer vector of ranked candidates from determine_optimal_levels() (its first element is used), a select_resolution() result (its $best), or a resolution_profile() (read by cp; a profile with no cp is an error). Both were hard errors before, so nothing that worked changes; the count used and where it came from are recorded as params$approx_n_cells / params$approx_n_cells_from and as attr(seeds, "n_from"). The two functions the pipeline documents as a pair are now connected: get_voronoi_seeds(n = determine_optimal_levels(pts)) needs no number carried between the calls by hand. A hex or square lattice records params$cells_occupied and params$cells_empty, and a count taken from a profile or a selection warns when fewer than three quarters of it end up occupied: the count is of k-means cells, all of them occupied, and on clustered points a lattice leaves about half its cells empty.

  • Five diagnostic plots that show the curve behind a chosen point, the folds behind a pooled number, or the distribution behind a count. None recomputes anything; each draws what the result already carries.

    • plot_cv_metrics(cv, metric): one point per fold, sized by the held-out rows it contributed, with the pooled value from overall as a dashed line; a compare_models_cv() result gets one panel per model on a shared scale. Any column of fold_metrics can be drawn, including backend extras and columns a metrics function added; a column that is NA in every fold is refused with the reason (Adj_R2 without p, coverage without draws) rather than drawn empty, and a per-fold extra with no pooled counterpart draws without the line and says so. So does a count (n_pred, n_MAPE, n_SMAPE), whose overall value is the total over the folds; it was drawn as the pooled line, at 150 against folds of 30. A model with no finite per-fold value gets no panel and no pooled line, and the caption names it, whether or not overall has a value for it (RF’s bandwidth was dropped without a mention). A compare_models_cv() result keeps its model strip when only one model is left to draw.
    • plot.aoa(): the dissimilarity index of the prediction locations against the training DI — cross-validated over the folds passed, or else each point’s distance to its nearest other training point; the legend says which — as ECDFs, or a histogram with the training curve, threshold marked, with the share outside and how close the inside ones run to the edge in the subtitle, and whether the threshold came from cross-validated folds in the caption. Prediction locations outside on a predictor dropped for having no training variance (DI = Inf) count in the prediction curve, which then tops out below 1, and the caption says how many are off the axis. It counts the DI = NA rows (a missing predictor) as well. The curve used to leave the Inf rows out: it read 0.97 inside at the threshold while the subtitle counted 11 of 40 outside. A result with every row at DI = Inf was refused as “every row had a missing or non-finite predictor”, and the error now gives the true reason.
    • plot.spatial_fit(type = "variogram") overlays the response’s own variogram (hollow points, dashed fit) on the residual variogram, on the same points and lags, so the structure the model absorbed is the gap between the two curves. The response curve is whichever variogram estimate_sac_range() returns for the response, which is its widest single direction when the all-pairs fit is unusable (a response with a trend, whose residuals are fine). A single-direction response curve is labelled with its azimuth, and the caption compares the sills only when both ranges were identified and the two curves cover the same point pairs (such a curve used to be labelled plainly as the response, its sill set against the all-pairs residual curve’s: “Residual sill is 45% of the response sill” from a quarter of the pairs). response = FALSE restores the residual curve alone.
    • plot_calibration(cv): observed against nominal coverage of cv_bayes()’s posterior predictive intervals, pooled (blue) and per fold (grey), with the diagonal and a one-line verdict. Each level is drawn at the nominal value cv_bayes() records in coverage_levels (0.995 was drawn at 1.00), so coverage_levels = seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1) gives a full curve; the default three levels are unchanged. Its error for all-NA coverage names compute_pred_intervals = FALSE as well as failed draws.
    • One sweep drawer behind three methods: plot.resolution_profile() (a panel per criterion, the level each selects marked, its flat region shaded, a note when a bound rather than the criterion is choosing); plot.feature_selection() (the accepted variable’s score at each step as the path, every other candidate faint, the stop in red, the best candidate at the step after the stop, which was scored and not added, hollow and labelled “not added” rather than drawn like the accepted variables, the hold-out score as a separate mark when select_on = "split" computed one — and a caption saying whether the intercept-only model was scored, since for the RF and GWR backends it usually is not, so the path starts at the first variable); plot.gwr_model_selection() (every model’s AICc against its size, the best of each size joined, the winner marked, its lead over the runner-up in the subtitle). select_features_forward()’s result now carries class "feature_selection" so plot() finds the method; it is the same list otherwise.

  • cv_block_size_sweep(): the same cross-validation at a ladder of block sizes, with random folds as the reference, returned as a table with the fold-to-fold spread at each size and the estimated autocorrelation range alongside; plot() draws the curve with the range marked. The curve rises as the blocks widen because the held-out points sit farther from their training data: its height at a size is the error at that distance from the data, which is the error of a map only at locations that far from it. On simulated fields with a 100–130-unit range and a random forest with coordinates, the curve levels off from one to two times the estimated range. Each size is a full cv_spatial(), so a fit budget (max_fits, default 60) refuses to start rather than run past it. The default ladder runs up to the largest size, at most half the shorter side, whose grid still holds k cells. At the default k = 5 half the side is a 2 x 2 grid of four cells on any extent less than 1.5 times as long as it is wide, so that rung used to be dropped every time. n_sizes = 6 then ran five cross-validations, the last at 0.30 of the side, and missed ranges up to a third of it that a 3 x 3 grid reaches. The top is now about a third of the side on such an extent. Sizes the caller passes in block_sizes whose grid holds fewer than k cells are not run, and a warning names them and the largest size that gives k blocks; they were dropped with only a log line. A units object for block_sizes is refused by name. On clustered data make_folds() can still lower k at the top sizes, which the k column shows; the sweep warns once, naming those sizes. The default ladder also skips sizes whose grid would exceed the 1,000,000 blocks make_folds() builds (a 6 km x 2 m transect used to abort with an error about block_size), runs along the line for points on one axis-parallel line (they were refused as having “no extent”), and warns when every rung is below the estimated range while longer blocks would still fit k times along the longer side (a 10 km x 100 m corridor: rungs of 4 to 50 m against a 1.7 km range, a flat curve that read as no leakage). On a roughly square extent at k = 5 that warning also fired, as in the block-size tour script on a 996 m square, with two wrong numbers. It called the top rung it had run (300) “half the shorter side” (498). It said blocks only up to the longer side over k (199, smaller than rungs already run) still gave k blocks, when blocks up to 332 did. It now fires only where a longer block would still give k blocks, and it names the top rung run and the largest size that gives k blocks. User-supplied block_sizes over the grid cap are refused before any fit, and a sac estimated in another CRS is converted to the sweep’s units with a warning (a metre range on a US-foot axis was drawn 3.3 times too short). The plot’s caption reads every coverage_* column as “closer to the nominal level is better” (only coverage_50, coverage_80 and coverage_95 were known, as higher-is-better, so coverage_97.5 from cv_bayes()’s full-precision names was captioned “lower is better”).

  • fit_gwr_model() keeps its local collinearity survey. Every fitting window — not a sample of 30 — has scaled condition indices of its kernel-weighted local design computed, the way Wheeler and Tiefelsdorf diagnose GWR collinearity, and the fit carries them as info$local_collinearity (one row per observation: coordinates, window size, and two condition indices: cn, Belsley’s uncentred index with the intercept, and cn_slopes, the predictors centred in the window and scaled by their study-area standard deviation), with info$n_local_collinear, info$n_local_singular and the global info$condition_index (on the centred predictors) beside AICc. n_local_collinear and the warning count the windows whose slopes are collinear (cn_slopes above 30, or singular), so a predictor’s origin (degrees C or kelvin) does not change the verdict. The warning is now the exact fraction of locations rather than a sampled one, and its thresholds (a quarter of the locations, or any) are unchanged; it says that a coefficient an exactly singular window cannot estimate is NA. The weighted survey sees what the unweighted spot-check could not: a bisquare window’s edge points contribute almost nothing to the fit, so they contribute almost nothing to its conditioning. The survey also runs with a single numeric predictor, and its kernel weights equal GWmodel::gw.weight() exactly: a boxcar keeps a point at the kernel’s edge, and a zero-width adaptive kernel gives NaN, counted as singular, instead of weight 1 at the co-located points. (A grid with a boxcar bandwidth equal to its spacing used to be reported collinear at every location while GWmodel fitted windows of 3 to 5 points.)

  • plot(fit, type = "coefficients") for a GWR fit maps one local coefficient (term) at the training locations, which is the reason to fit GWR at all — and masks the locations where it is not to be believed: a collinear local design (for a slope, the slope condition index above 30 or singular; for the intercept, the condition index with the intercept above 30) or a non-finite coefficient is drawn hollow and grey, counted in the subtitle, because the smooth surface a naive map draws over them is the picture of an unstable estimate. mask = FALSE draws them anyway and says how many it is drawing. A fit with a duplicated predictor name is drawn rather than refused as “every location is masked”. A slope map in kelvin is drawn like the one in degrees C; before, every location was masked and the map refused.

  • kriging_adequacy(): what a block-kriging aggregator would deliver on a set of cells, computed beside the plain means and changing none of them. Per cell, from a fitted variogram (estimate_sac_range()’s, or estimated here): the block-kriging estimate and variance, that variance as a share of the variance the cell’s mean would have with no data at all (kr_ratio, the coverage score — near 1 the data tell the cell nothing; a share of the point sill never came near 1 for cells larger than the range), the error variance of the cell’s plain mean under the same variogram (plain_var), the share of it kriging removes (kr_gain), and the kriged-minus-plain shift over the standard deviation the variogram gives that difference (kr_shift); plus the variance of the standardised errors from blocked cross-validation (attr(, "cv")$zscore_var), which is about 1 when the kriging variance is right. Measured on simulated exponential fields: 0.93–1.07 with the true variogram, 0.85–1.01 with the estimated one; under blocked folds it checks the sill and range rather than the nugget (0.95–1.24 with the nugget understated tenfold), and random folds are the instrument for the nugget. The comparison the function exists for, against known cell averages on those fields: kriging cut the plain mean’s squared error by 54–56 percent under uniform and clustered sampling alike, where kr_var over plain_var predicted 55–58. A naive s^2/n below plain_var says the naive standard error is too small under the variogram; kr_var is not compared with s^2/n, which moves with the fitted sill. Repeat visits to one location are kriged from their mean, with their pooled within-location variance divided by their count; kriging them as separate rows made every kriging system singular and returned NA everywhere. Any cell or held-out location gstat still cannot solve is counted in a warning. This is the first kriging path in the package (gstat::krige()); its model families are the ones the package interprets elsewhere, and any other is refused by name. The cross-validation runs each make_folds() split on its own training set, so "buffered_loo" and "nndm" keep their exclusion zones (reduced to fold labels they ran as plain leave-one-out: with a 250 m buffer, a standardised-error variance of 1.02 and RMSE 0.757, against 0.873 and 0.944 with the buffer kept), and print() names the scheme instead of calling every one “blocked CV”. A cell holding locations that the nmax nearest its centre leave out is kriged from all of its own locations plus the nmax nearest outside it (a cell of 1,500 points was otherwise estimated from its middle 50: 0.43 off against 0.07), and the column kr_n_used says how many locations each cell was kriged from. max_neighbours (default 2000) leaves out, with a warning, a cell that would need a larger kriging system, and max_box_ratio (default 1000) a cell whose bounding box exceeds its area that many times, because gstat discretises over the whole box (+592 MB for one strip at 7,072); both are counted in attr(, "cells_left_out") and by print(). The points are put in the CRS the variogram was fitted in (attr(sac, "crs")), as summarize_by_cell() does: a sac fitted in metres used on points in km gave a CV statistic of 3.05 against 0.85. A sac whose variogram is of residuals (detrended = TRUE) is used with a warning that the response is kriged without its predictors and the variances come out too small (4.3–5.2 against 0.67–1.53). attr(, "rejected_reason") records why a sac’s range was refused, and the warning and print() say it instead of “sill never reached” for every refusal. The cell ID is found and matched as summarize_by_cell() finds it (cells keyed by id or grid_id too, and a double ID of 1e5 matches an integer 100000, where it used to leave that cell with n = 0), a point whose ID matches no cell is counted in a warning, and a layer with no CRS is taken to be in the other’s. Folds whose recorded rows sit at other locations in assigned_points_sf are refused, as in cv_*(). Folds built before assign_features_to_polygons() dropped points used to be applied by position, holding out the wrong points (cross-validation RMSE 1.82 against 2.11 with folds built on the assigned layer), with nothing said.

  • MAPE and SMAPE now say how many rows they were averaged over. Every metrics frame — model_metrics(), summary(), evaluate_insample(), compare_models(), and the overall and fold_metrics of cv_gwr(), cv_bayes(), cv_spatial(), cv_rf() and compare_models_cv() — gains two trailing integer columns, n_MAPE and n_SMAPE: the rows each percentage error actually used once those where its denominator is zero were dropped (y for MAPE, |y| + |yhat| for SMAPE, zero meaning no larger than 100 machine epsilons times the data’s own magnitude). They equal n (n_pred in the CV frames) when nothing was dropped, and are 0 in an empty frame. The values themselves are unchanged, apart from what now counts as zero (see Bug fixes): a MAPE over 58 of 120 rows is the same number 2.0.0 reported, but it now arrives labelled, where before nothing in the frame recorded that it was a subset average. print(summary(fit)) appends “(over k of n rows)” to its SMAPE line when the two differ. The columns sit after Adj_R2 so code addressing the seven metric columns by position is unaffected; code pinning the exact column set needs the two names added.

  • voronoi_seeds_kmeans() gains nstart, the number of starts (10 for partition = "kmeans", as before).

  • cv_bayes() and compare_models() say when a Bayesian fit did not converge. Both scored such a fit like any other, and only the fit’s WARN log lines (which tryCatch() and knitr never see, and spatialkit_quiet() hides) said that its posterior was not to be trusted. cv_bayes()’s fold_metrics gains convergence_ok: TRUE or FALSE as fit_bayesian_spatial_model() judged that fold’s sampler (divergent transitions, R-hat, effective sample size, E-BFMI), and NA when fit_args sets check_convergence = FALSE. A run with any FALSE raises one warning of class spatialkit_convergence naming those folds and the checks each failed. compare_models() gains the same column and warns once for each model that did not converge. Code that pins the exact column set of either table needs the new name added.

  • select_resolution() returns $seeds, the centres of the partition the profile scored at the chosen level, and get_voronoi_seeds(method = "kmeans") and voronoi_seeds_kmeans() return those centres when given the selection or the profile, instead of running a k-means of their own. A k-means partition is the Voronoi partition of its centres, so these seeds rebuild the very cells the criteria judged. The fresh k-means the seeding functions ran (Hartigan-Wong, 10 starts, on whatever cloud they were given) was a different partition: on 300 points it put 5–16 percent of them in a different cell from the one they were scored in, and on 2000 points (profiled on a 1500-point subsample) 26–29 percent, so the count was defended on cells nobody built. The profile keeps every level’s centres in attr(x, "centres") (with attr(x, "centres_crs")), the seeds come back in the CRS of the boundary or points they are for, and attr(seeds, "kmeans") assigns sample_points to them, each point to its nearest seed. A count passed as a number (n = sel$best) still runs a fresh k-means, as does a selection made before seeds were kept. voronoi_seeds_kmeans() did not accept a selection or profile as k before, and the advice in build_tessellation()’s occupancy warning now points at the selection rather than the bare count.

Bug fixes

  • A point layer in an sfc_GEOMETRY column stopped the fits, the cross-validations, the folds, the cell summaries, the tessellations, the seeders and the surface. A geometry column of the general class sfc_GEOMETRY can hold points only: sf::st_cast(x, "GEOMETRY") builds one, and so do c() of such a column with points and a point set with [[<- in place of the last other geometry of a mixed column. sf::st_coordinates() refuses that class, so fit_gwr_model(), fit_rf_model(), fit_bayesian_spatial_model(), gwr_model_selection(), prep_model_data(), predict() of a fit, model_metrics(), evaluate_insample(), compare_models(), cv_spatial(), cv_gwr(), cv_rf(), compare_models_cv(), cv_block_size_sweep(), area_of_applicability(), summarize_by_cell(), cell_values_at() (newdata, points and seeds), determine_optimal_levels(), resolution_profile() (and so select_resolution()), create_voronoi_polygons(), build_tessellation(method = "triangles"), get_voronoi_seeds(method = "kmeans") with sample_points, voronoi_seeds_kmeans() and predict_surface() (grid and covariates) stopped with sf’s “not implemented for objects of class sfc_GEOMETRY”. On the column sf::st_cast() returns, sf::st_dimension(), sf::st_union() and sf::st_transform() stop with “Not compatible with STRSXP”: make_folds() stopped with it, as points_sf and as prediction_points, and so did fold_separation(), ensure_projected(), harmonize_crs(), assign_features_to_polygons() and create_voronoi_polygons(), and every call that moves such a layer to another CRS, such as model_metrics() with it as newdata in another CRS than the fit. plot_tessellation_map() (features_sf, seeds_sf or boundary), plot_folds() and plot() of a fit whose layer is such a column returned a plot that stopped with that message when it was built or printed, and create_grid_polygons_cached() stopped with it on such points as boundary, where create_grid_polygons() refuses a boundary that is not polygonal. select_features_forward() reported that stop as a failure to build its inner folds, and on the other form of the column it scored no candidate and returned an empty selection. When every geometry of such a column is a POINT, these functions now read it as the same points in sfc_POINT and give the answer those points give, and when every geometry is a MULTIPOINT, as the same features in sfc_MULTIPOINT. A layer moved to another CRS comes back in that class, and so do the rows assign_features_to_polygons() returns; area_of_applicability() still returns the rows of newdata, and predict_surface() a grid it does not move, in the class they came in. A layer that mixes points with other geometry types is read as before. build_tessellation(method = "triangles") also stopped with sf’s message on a layer that mixes POINT and MULTIPOINT features, which sf holds in an sfc_GEOMETRY column; it now reads their vertices as it reads a MULTIPOINT layer’s.

  • resolution_profile() with a variogram stopped on a study area much longer than wide. The mean correlation over the study area, which reliability reads, came from a grid over the hull’s bounding box at a spacing that follows the hull’s area. On a strip along an axis narrower than half that spacing (300 points over 20000 x 10 m, in metres or in kilometres), the call stopped with “wrong sign in ‘by’ argument” whenever it held a fitted variogram (sac from estimate_sac_range(), or a ladder set with levels and sac = "auto"). On a thin strip at a slant, the grid’s rows crossed part of its length, or fewer than 10 nodes fell inside and the bounding box’s value was used: on the strip at 30 degrees the mean correlation was 0.058 where the strip’s own is about 0.096. A hull narrower than two steps of the grid is now laid out in the frame of its rectangle of least area, in bands along it with the nodes spread over each band’s width, so a hull that tapers (a wedge, a lens) is read over its area, and its value does not move with its angle. Every other hull keeps its grid and its results.

  • Areas in a CRS whose unit sf has no name for were read in square metres. For a projected CRS whose +to_meter unit sf has no name for (a unit of 1000 km, of 3.28 m or of 0.5 mm), sf::st_area() converts to square metres. summarize_by_cell(area = TRUE) returned that as cell_area, which its help gives in the CRS’s unit squared, so a square of 1000 m in units of 1000 km got 1e6 where its area is 1e-6, and n_per_area was a count per square metre. resolution_profile() divided the hull’s area in square metres by the square of a range in CRS units, so a range floor of 3 came out as 31 in units of 3.28 m, and in units of 1000 km the floor was not finite or the profile stopped with “wrong sign in ‘by’ argument”. Three checks read such an area beside lengths in the CRS’s unit as well. kriging_adequacy() left out every square cell as a sliver in units of 0.5 mm (a box 4e6 times its area) and let a real sliver through in units of 1000 km. make_folds() with supplied blocks read their scale in metres against a range in CRS units, so in units of 1000 km it gave no warning for blocks smaller than the range, and in units of 0.5 mm it quoted the wrong scale. create_grid_polygons() chose the edge strips to drop after its clip by comparing such an area with a bound in the CRS’s unit squared. All of them now take the planar area in the CRS’s unit squared. Layers in metres, in a unit sf names (such as US survey feet or kilometres) and in lon/lat, whose cells keep their geodesic square metres, give the same results as before.

  • Line midpoints in a CRS whose unit sf has no name for were off the middle. coerce_to_points() modes "auto" and "line_midpoint", and so prep_model_data() and the fits that pointize lines, took a line’s midpoint with sf::st_line_sample(), which measures the line in metres for such a CRS and reads half that length as a distance along the line in the CRS’s unit. A straight line from x = 0 to x = 20 got its point at x = 20, its end, in a unit of 2 m, and at x = 5 in a unit of 0.5 m; a MULTILINESTRING’s longest part the same. The midpoint is now taken at half the planar length in the CRS’s own unit, at x = 10 in every unit. Lines in metres, in a unit sf names (such as US survey feet or kilometres) and in lon/lat with tmp_project = TRUE get the same points as before.

  • Voronoi cells with no boundary changed with the unit of the coordinates. create_voronoi_polygons() and build_tessellation(method = "voronoi") clip the cells to the points’ convex hull, or to the cover, grown by 2 percent of its diagonal, as their help says; the margin was floored at 1 unit of the CRS. A layer whose diagonal is under 1 unit, such as a 500 m layer in a kilometre CRS, grew by 0.02 units (20 m) where in metres it grows by 15.9 m, and its edge cells covered 2.9 percent more ground. The margin is now 2 percent of the diagonal in every unit. A layer whose diagonal is 1 unit or more gets the same cells as before, and one location still grows by 0.02 units.

  • clip_target_for() returned disks around points whose box it should return, depending on where they lie. With no boundary, the points’ bounding box is the target, and a buffer around the points only when the short side of the box is under a millionth of the long side. A side whose two ends all.equal() called equal also took the buffer, and that test compares the ends relative to their size, so it read the origin: a 3 km x 2 km box at x = 1e12 got three disks of 150 m (an area of 211,961 for 6,000,000), and a 5 cm x 3 cm box at y = 4,000,000 got disks too. The sides are now read against the span only, so the box comes back at any offset.

  • clip_target_for() stopped with R’s “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” on points none of which has a location. With no boundary, points that are all empty, or all have a coordinate that is not finite or lies beyond 1e150, or that the move of lon/lat points into a projected CRS empties (a latitude beyond 90), have no bounding box. The call now refuses them with an error that says no point has a location. With a boundary, such points still get the boundary as their target.

  • clip_target_for() said it used a “small buffer” around points at one location, and gave neither its size nor its unit. With no boundary and every point at one location the bounding box has no extent to take a share of, and the target is a disk of radius 1 unit of the CRS: 1 m in a metre CRS and 1 km in a kilometre CRS. The target is unchanged. The message now gives the radius in the layer’s unit (in the units of the coordinates when the points have no CRS) and says to pass boundary for a target of real size, or an expand of 1 or more, which is taken as the radius; ?clip_target_for says the same.

  • Block folds, the join to polygons, the Voronoi cells and the fill of cell_values_at() changed with the origin of the coordinates. A point counts as on an edge while it lies within a margin of it, one part in 1e10 of the largest coordinate: 0.44 mm at a UTM northing of 4,400 km, but 100 m on a 4 km layer shifted to 1e12 and 100 km at 1e15. At 1e12 points within 100 m of a block edge went to the lower block, so make_folds() and the functions that make folds with it (cv_spatial() and compare_models_cv() without folds, fold_separation(), cv_block_size_sweep(), kriging_adequacy(), area_of_applicability() and select_features_forward()) gave other folds than at the origin; assign_features_to_polygons() gave points tens of metres inside a polygon to its neighbour; the 60 points of a layer fell in 39 Voronoi cells of create_voronoi_polygons() and build_tessellation(method = "voronoi"); and cell_values_at() gave other IDs. At 1e15 make_folds() refused with a false “single block” and the join called every point a tie. The margin is now at most a millionth of the diagonal of the coordinates’ bounding box, and at least four times the spacing of doubles at the largest coordinate, so at any offset where doubles hold the layer these results are the ones near the origin for every point farther than that from an edge. Where the diagonal is at least a ten-thousandth of the largest coordinate (400 m at a UTM northing of 4,000 km) the margin is unchanged; on a smaller layer it is the millionth of its diagonal (28 micrometres on a layer 20 m across). The help pages that state the margin say so.

  • Coordinates so far from their origin that doubles cannot hold the layer were read without a word. At 1e15 doubles are 0.125 apart, more than a millionth of a layer a few kilometres across, and the edges make_folds() lays for blocks and create_grid_polygons() lays for its grid are rounded to that spacing, so a point near an edge could fall in the next block with nothing said, and two points 0.25 m apart fell in one Voronoi cell. make_folds() ("block_kfold" and "buffered_loo"), assign_features_to_polygons(), create_grid_polygons(), create_voronoi_polygons() and build_tessellation() ("voronoi" and "triangles"; "hex" and "square" through the grid) now warn once, with class spatialkit_xy_imprecise, where the spacing of doubles at the coordinates is more than a millionth of the layer’s extent; the warning gives both and says to shift the layer nearer the origin or project it. A function that makes folds several times on one layer says it once.

  • clip_target_for() drew its buffer around points on one line or at one location at the rounding of their coordinates, without a word. With no boundary, GEOS draws the buffer at the size of the coordinates: at an offset of 1e15, where doubles are 0.125 apart, the 1-metre disk around one location had an area of 2.6875 for pi, and two points 0.5 m apart on a line got an empty LINESTRING for a target. The function now warns, with class spatialkit_xy_imprecise, where the spacing of doubles at the points is more than a millionth of the target’s extent, and refuses, with an error of class spatialkit_xy_imprecise_error, where the buffer comes back empty or with no area; both give the spacing and the radius and say to shift the layer nearer the origin or pass boundary. quiet = TRUE does not silence the warning.

  • clip_target_for() returned a point, a MULTIPOINT, an empty line or a disk of subnormal area for points less than about 3e-153 apart. With no boundary, points on one line were buffered by 5 percent of their spread, and a radius whose square is below the smallest normal double (about 1.5e-154) gave GEOS a disk whose area underflowed: points 1e-320, 1e-310 and 1e-160 apart got a MULTIPOINT, an empty LINESTRING and a disk of area 1.6e-322, with the message “using small buffer around points”; a box 1e-320 on a side came back as a POINT with no message. A side of the box, or a share of the spread, below that length now counts as none, so such points get the disk of radius 1 unit of the CRS that points at one location get, and the message gives their spread.

  • summarize_by_cell(area = TRUE) stopped on cells that carry M. Cells that are XYM or XYZM throughout reached GEOS, which does not read M, and the call stopped with GEOS’s “GEOS does not support XYM or XYZM geometries”. The cells are now checked and measured in x and y, as cells that mix dimensions were, and are returned with their own geometry.

  • estimate_sac_range() drew its n_max subsample over rows with nothing to model. 300 valued rows among 20,300 were estimated from the 74 that fell in the draw, and 100 among 20,100 came back NA. Rows with a missing or infinite response or predictor are now dropped first, and the subsample no longer depends on the order of the rows.

  • estimate_sac_range() counted rows, not locations, against its floor of 30. Rows that share a location are one place to the variogram and to its test for spatial structure, yet five locations visited 20 times passed the floor, got a variogram of ten pairs of locations, and were judged by a test of five location means, which called most such layers unstructured even where the range was three times the extent. The floor now counts distinct locations as well, among the rows the variogram is computed on. Below 30 the result is the unclassed NA whose rejected_reason gives the count (“5 distinct location(s) among the 100 point(s) with a finite value to model, fewer than the 30 a variogram range is estimated from”), and nothing is fitted. When the layer has 30 or more locations and the n_max subsample keeps fewer, the reason gives the subsample’s counts and says “of the n_max subsample”. The functions that estimate a variogram read it as they read the other early refusals: make_folds(auto_range = TRUE) builds geometric blocks and names it in its warning, summarize_by_cell(deff = "variogram") falls back to Kish with spatialkit_deff_fallback where the verdict of no structure had given a design effect of 1 in every cell, kriging_adequacy() stops with it, and the Bayesian fit’s check before fitting reports the range as not estimated. With detrend = "reml" such a layer got a warning that the REML fit did not converge when nothing had been fitted; it gets the same NA and no warning. Where a predictor is missing on every row of such a layer, there is no warning that the variogram is fitted to the raw response, since none is fitted. A layer whose rows all lie at one location gets this reason in place of “the points have no extent”.

  • estimate_sac_range(detrend = "reml") kept the first fit to converge, not the best. When the true range is short against the extent the starts of nlme::gls() lay in a valley of the likelihood: a layer with a 10 km range came back at 502 km and was refused. The start is now the best point of the profile likelihood on a grid, and the fit with the largest log-likelihood is kept (attr(, "reml") gains logLik, logLik_gain and n_fits).

  • estimate_sac_range() returned NA or an R error for a bad argument without naming it. cutoff, range_frac, n_max, seed, keep_directional_fits, n_lags and structure_alpha are checked, and a bad value is an error that names the argument. cutoff above 1 and n_max below 30 are errors; n_max = Inf means no subsample.

  • estimate_sac_range() called a response constant by an absolute floor. A response whose standard deviation was under 1.5e-8 in its own unit was refused, and so was one of standard deviation 1 on a mean of 1e8. The test is now relative: under 1e-12 of the largest absolute value.

  • The projection chosen for lon/lat input depended on the order of the rows. ensure_projected() scores candidate projections on a sample of the points, taken at even spacing along the rows: 400 points over the conterminous United States got an Albers CRS in some row orders and a Lambert azimuthal one in others. The sample is now taken along the points sorted by coordinate.

  • The projection chosen for a few detailed outlines, and the area check on more than 200 polygons, depended on the order of the features. A layer of fewer than 40 polygons or lines is scored on its outlines’ vertices too, and more than 160 vertices were first thinned at even spacing along the vertices as the layer lists them: five outlines of 200 vertices over the conterminous United States got an Albers CRS in three of eight feature orders and a Lambert azimuthal one in the other five. The area check of summarize_by_cell(area = TRUE), and of ensure_projected(purpose = "area") on projected input, measures at most 200 of a layer’s polygons, and they were taken at even spacing along the rows: 300 cells in a UTM zone, one of them 700 km east of its central meridian, were refused in five of eight row orders and given a density in the other three, and attr(, "area_error") changed with the order. The vertices are now thinned along the outlines’ distinct vertices sorted by coordinate, as the points of a point layer are sampled: a vertex listed twice (a ring’s closing vertex, a border two features share) counts once, so a ring listed from another vertex is scored the same, and a thinned outline is not densified between the vertices kept. The polygons are taken along the polygons sorted by their bounding boxes, and polygons that share a box, as the Delaunay triangles of gridded points do, by the means of their vertices; the polygons that reach furthest along x and y, either way, are always measured. For a given layer the CRS, the area error and the refusal can differ from before.

  • A small lon/lat layer whose features share edges, or meet another feature’s edge at a corner, got its projection chosen on rounding noise. When a polygon or line layer has fewer than 40 distinct feature points and fewer than 40 distinct vertices, ensure_projected() scores the candidates on points added along each edge of its outlines as well. An edge two features share was filled once from each end, some copies of an added point differed in their last bits, and the pair, about 1e-9 m apart, set the worst-case distance error of every candidate. Two boxes of 12 by 15 degrees, one above the other, scored 76.9 percent in UTM zone 13 and 86.8 percent in EPSG:5070, where their outline as one box scores 0.5 and 10.9 percent, and the zone was kept with “76.92% vs 76.92%”. A 2 by 2 grid of boxes moved to a Lambert azimuthal CRS with “11.22% against the zone’s 13.50%”, where its outline gives 0.06% and 0.26%. The same held where a point added along one feature’s edge falls on a corner of another (a T-junction, or a corner that touches the edge) or on a point added along an edge that overlaps it in part. Each edge is now filled from the same end whichever feature lists it, and an added point within about 1e-9 degrees (0.1 mm) of a vertex or of another added point is left out; the vertices are kept as they are. The two layers above score within a tenth of a percentage point of their outlines, and the log quotes the outlines’ figures. A layer on which no added point lies within 1e-9 degrees of another point scores as before, but for the last bits. For the others the CRS, attr(, "crs_choice") and the logged figures can differ from before, and the points added along an edge no longer depend on the direction in which its ring is listed.

  • The projection chosen for a lon/lat polygon or line layer depended on how many rows repeat one feature. ensure_projected() scores the candidates on one point per row, plus the outline’s vertices when there are fewer than 40 such points, and it thinned an outline of more than 160 vertex rows without filling its edges. A layer that lists one polygon once per year was scored by the number of years: a box of 52 by 22 degrees over the conterminous United States got a Lambert azimuthal CRS with “1.76% against the zone’s 10.87%” on one row, “1.28% against the zone’s 8.33%” on 33 rows, and from 40 rows every candidate scored NA and UTM zone 15 was kept “because the candidate projections could not be scored on this layer”. Copies of one point now count once, before the count of 40 and in the sample of 40 points, and an outline is thinned only when it has more than 160 distinct vertices. A layer whose features lie on distinct points, and whose outline lists more than 160 vertex rows only when it has 40 distinct vertices or more, scores as before. For the others the CRS, attr(, "crs_choice") and the logged figures can differ from before.

  • The projection chosen for a lon/lat point layer depended on how many rows list one location. ensure_projected() scores the candidates on 40 points taken at even spacing along the rows sorted by coordinate, and repeat visits to one station took places in that sample from the other stations. 39 stations scored 5.07 percent in UTM zone 14 and 0.61 percent in the Albers CRS chosen; with station 1 listed 100 times, 4.59 and 0.45 percent, and listed 1,001 times, 2.32 and 0.35 percent, the sample holding 4 of the 39 stations. The sample is now taken over the distinct locations. A layer with no location listed twice scores as before; for the others the CRS, attr(, "crs_choice") and the logged figures can differ from before.

  • The area check of summarize_by_cell(area = TRUE) and of ensure_projected(purpose = "area") on projected input depended on how many rows repeat one polygon. The check takes the spread of the ratios of planar to geodesic area over the layer’s polygons, and it counted rows: copies of a polygon weighted the median by their number, took places in the sample of 200 polygons, and two copies of one polygon passed as two probes. Three 50 km squares in UTM zone 14 measured 0.93 percent, and 1.04 percent with the left one listed three times, so ensure_projected() warned and summarize_by_cell() refused the cells only then; 150 squares of 1 degree in UTM zone 15 measured 24.98 percent, and 30.79 percent with one of them listed 300 more times; a box in Web Mercator listed twice measured 0, where alone it is unmeasured. The check now measures each distinct polygon once, the first of its exact copies kept, and a layer whose polygons are all copies of one is measured on the grid over its bounding box, as one polygon is. A layer with no polygon listed twice gets the same figure as before.

  • Two listings of one place a few bits apart, or at longitudes 180 and -180, set the distance error of every candidate CRS. ensure_projected() scores each candidate on the worst ratio of planar to geodesic length over pairs of sampled points, and it took every pair longer than 0. A corner two features share, written -107.2 in one and -110.6 + 3.4 in the other, a point listed twice a few bits apart, and a layer whose features meet at longitude 180, which lists (180, y) and (-180, y), each gave a pair about 1e-9 m long whose planar length is rounding noise, or the width of the world in Web Mercator. Two boxes side by side, typed that way, scored 13.7 percent in UTM zone 13 and 24.5 percent in EPSG:5070, where their outline as one box scores 0.26 and 0.97 percent, and got an Albers CRS. Two boxes either side of 180 reported a distance error of 1 for their one candidate. Pairs under 1 mm are now left out: the two boxes score 0.25 and 0.97 percent and get their outline’s Lambert azimuthal CRS, and the boxes either side of 180 report 0.35 percent. A layer with no pair 1 mm or longer is scored NA, as a layer of one location is. A layer whose sampled pairs are all 1 mm or longer scores as before; for the others the CRS, attr(, "crs_choice") and the logged figures can differ from before.

  • The geodesic distances that score candidate projections came out short on east-west pairs of a few millimetres. ensure_projected() compares planar distances with WGS84 ellipsoidal ones from Vincenty’s formula, whose iteration stopped once a pass moved its longitude on the auxiliary sphere by less than 1e-12 radians. On an east-west pair under about 2 mm at the equator, 2.5 mm at latitude 40 and 11 mm at latitude 80, the first pass already moved it by less, and the distance came out up to 0.34 percent short; pairs up to about a metre long stopped after the second pass, up to 1.1e-5 short. The shortest pair can set the worst-case distance error of every candidate: 30 points between latitudes 33 and 41 score 0.04 percent in UTM zone 13, and scored 0.20 percent with a 31st point 1.8 mm east of one of them. The iteration now stops once a pass moves the longitude by no more than 1e-12 of the pair’s longitude difference, taken the short way round (of 1 radian for pairs 1 radian or more apart), and such pairs agree with the ellipsoid to 1e-9, across longitude 180 too. Nearly antipodal pairs still fall back to the spherical distance. Pairs a degree or more long move by less than 1e-10 of their length, and other pairs by up to 1.1e-5 of theirs, the error the old test left on them; the distance errors in attr(, "crs_choice") and the log move by about as much, and the CRS chosen changes only where two candidates score that close.

  • One row of a lon/lat layer at a coordinate that is not finite made every candidate projection score NA. The geodesic distances stopped with “NAs are not allowed in subscripted assignments” on the pairs of that row, the scorer turned the stop into NA, and 39 stations over the conterminous United States with a 40th row at longitude Inf were put in UTM zone 14 with an NA in attr(, "crs_choice"), where the 39 get an Albers CRS. Such a row now takes no part in the scores, as an empty row does, and the zone’s figure is the stations’.

  • ensure_projected() kept a UTM zone that cannot place every location of a lon/lat layer, and coerce_to_points() then ended the R session. PROJ gives no coordinates for a point a UTM zone cannot place, about 90 degrees or more from its central meridian on the equator, and the distance score left such points out, so the zone was scored on the rest. LINESTRING (0 0, 180 0) kept UTM zone 46, which holds neither end of the line (278.82% against 1169.31% for the Lambert azimuthal CRS); ensure_projected() returned the line empty, and five points on the equator at longitudes 0 to 180 with two of them empty, without a word; and coerce_to_points() in mode "auto" (the default, also of prep_model_data() and of the functions that reduce a layer to points) or "line_midpoint" handed the empty line to sf::st_line_sample(), which segfaulted. A candidate is now used only if it places every located vertex of the layer (a vertex at a latitude beyond 90, which no CRS places, takes no part in this test): one that does not gets distance_error NA in attr(, "crs_choice"), is not chosen and is named in the log line, and when no candidate places the layer the global fallback (Web Mercator, Equal Earth for purpose = "area") is used. A sampled point that a candidate cannot place makes its score NA. The line and the five points now get the Lambert azimuthal CRS, and the line’s midpoint is (90, 0). When a move out of lon/lat still leaves a located row empty, or without some of its vertices (sf::st_transform() drops a vertex it cannot move), ensure_projected() warns with class spatialkit_rows_unplaced, naming the rows. coerce_to_points() never samples a line that its temporary projection did not place in full: it stops with class spatialkit_features_degenerate and site = "projection", naming the rows and offering mode = "centroid" or tmp_project = FALSE, and the functions that reduce a layer to points raise it in their own words. A lon/lat line with a coordinate that is not finite or lies beyond 1e150, which crashed the same way, gets an empty point, as an empty line does. Layers on which every candidate places each vertex and each point the score samples get the CRS, the scores and the points they got. A candidate that places every vertex but not a point the score samples along an edge now scores NA: on LINESTRING (0 0, 180 0) with purpose = "area", the Lambert azimuthal CRS, which is still used.

  • harmonize_crs() and the functions that move a layer into the CRS they work in returned a row the target CRS cannot place in full, emptied or short of a vertex, without a word. GDAL returns a point it cannot move as an empty point and drops such a vertex from a line or a ring. harmonize_crs(a, b, prefer = "b") with b in UTM zone 46 returned the point (10, 0.1) of a empty and LINESTRING (10 0, 90 0, 170 0) without its vertex at longitude 10, and a ring with a vertex at latitude 95 lost that vertex, through harmonize_crs() and through the boundary of predict_surface(); ensure_projected(target_crs =) did the same in silence from a projected layer, such as one in EPSG:3857. Every such move now warns with class spatialkit_rows_unplaced, naming the rows, the function called and the argument: harmonize_crs() (a or b, not after the on_transform_error = "set_crs" stamp), ensure_projected(target_crs =) from any CRS, the seeders and the tessellation builders (boundary, seeds, sample_points, cover, and the centres of a profile passed as n or k), assign_features_to_polygons() (features_sf, polygons_sf), kriging_adequacy(), cell_values_at() (values, and newdata where it is placed in the polygons of values), and the functions that move a layer they are given into the CRS of their data: make_folds(), cv_spatial(), cv_gwr(), cv_bayes(), area_of_applicability(), predict_surface(), fold_separation(), resolution_profile(), summarize_by_cell(), create_grid_polygons(), plot_folds(), the predict() methods of the GWR, random forest and Bayesian fits, and plot_tessellation_map() for every layer it moves into the plot’s CRS, with a CRS of its own or without one. So does a row of a projected layer with a coordinate beyond 1e10 that a move to a CRS in degrees empties. The warning names the CRS the layer was in (“a location in EPSG:3857”), and longitude and latitude for a lon/lat layer or for one without a CRS that is read as lon/lat. cell_values_at() and the pooled readers of summarize_by_cell() still report the locations and seeds they place in their own words. The rows come back as they did; layers the target CRS places in full raise no new warning and give the same results.

  • plot_tessellation_map() and plot_folds() drew rows without a location. A cell, boundary, seed or feature with a coordinate at Inf gave the map an infinite x range in silence, and one at 1e200 (beyond the package’s 1e150 bound) a map 1e200 wide where every other row shrank to a point, with ggplot2’s bare “Position guide is perpendicular to the intended axis”. plot_folds() drew the point make_folds() had just dropped as without a location, at that coordinate. Such a row is now left out of its layer, read as given before any move into the plot’s CRS, with one warning naming the argument and the count (“not drawing 1 row(s) of features_sf without a location”). plot_folds() also leaves out a boundary row with such a coordinate, and a point with no fold that make_folds() left out as empty or because the CRS the folds were built in cannot place it (a latitude beyond 90), which it drew at that latitude. A move into another CRS emptied the same rows before, so the map no longer depends on whether a move happens. Layers without such rows are drawn as before.

  • plot_tessellation_map(labels = TRUE) handed ggplot2 a label for a cell with an NA ID or an empty geometry, and ggplot2 warned at print “Removed 1 row containing missing values or values outside the scale range (geom_text())” (12 rows when every ID was NA). A cell is now labelled when it has a label and a location; when no cell has both, the labels are skipped with a log line, as they are when there is no ID column.

  • A layer without a CRS whose coordinates cannot be longitude and latitude was stamped with a CRS in longitude and latitude. plot_tessellation_map(target_crs = 4326) on CRS-less cells in metres found that they do not look like longitude and latitude, then stamped EPSG:4326 on them all the same: the map was drawn at “latitude” 4,000,000, and sf added its bare “bounding box has potentially an invalid value range for longlat data”. A layer without a CRS is now refused a CRS in longitude and latitude when it has an x outside -180 to 360 or a y beyond 90 north or south. The refusal names the argument, its coordinates’ box and the target CRS, and asks for the layer’s CRS (or, in plot_tessellation_map(), harmonize_crs(target_crs =) and ensure_projected(target_crs =), a projected target_crs). It applies where a layer without a CRS is brought into the CRS of another layer or argument: harmonize_crs(), ensure_projected(target_crs =), assign_features_to_polygons() (which names features_sf or polygons_sf; features in metres beside cells in degrees fell in no polygon, and polygons in metres stopped on an s2 refusal), plot_tessellation_map(), plot_folds(), make_folds() and the cv_*() functions, area_of_applicability(), predict_surface(), fold_separation(), kriging_adequacy(), resolution_profile(), summarize_by_cell(), cell_values_at(), create_voronoi_polygons(), create_grid_polygons() and build_tessellation(). It applies as well where a fit’s reading of its CRS-less training data as longitude and latitude is given to CRS-less new data: predict() on a random forest, GWR or Bayesian fit, and the grid, boundary and covariates of predict_surface(). Every prediction came back NA with a warning that the rows have a location in longitude and latitude, and such a boundary held no grid point. So does cell_values_at()’s reading of newdata or seeds without a CRS beside points without one in degrees, where every row came back NA with no word about newdata. In create_grid_polygons(crs =) and build_tessellation(crs =) a boundary with a y between 90 and 180 is still stamped, and refused by the row’s latitude as before. A target CRS that is projected is still stamped, with a warning (with a log line in ensure_projected(target_crs =)).

  • A row of a lon/lat layer with a vertex at a latitude beyond 90 shaped the projection ensure_projected() chose for the other rows. No CRS places such a row, but the choice read it in the extent, the longitudes of the antimeridian test and the centre. 39 stations over the conterminous United States get an Albers CRS (standard parallels 32.9 and 43.0); with a 40th row at (-96, 95) they got a Lambert azimuthal CRS centred on (-96.7, 40.7), and the Albers candidate’s parallels moved to 41.2 and 84.2. A row at (-100, -95), or a swapped row at (40, -96), did the same. Such a row now takes no part in the choice, the whole row, as a row with a coordinate beyond 1e150: the stations get the CRS and the crs_choice they get alone. The row is still moved, comes back empty or without the vertices the CRS cannot place, and the spatialkit_rows_unplaced warning names it. A layer each row of which has such a vertex gets the global fallback, and the log line says so. Layers with no latitude beyond 90 get the CRS they got.

  • The readers of a lon/lat data layer read a row with a latitude beyond 90 as given. sf warns “bounding box has potentially an invalid value range for longlat data” each time it reads the box of such a layer, and that warning reached the caller in sf’s words from coerce_to_points(), prep_model_data() and the fits on polygons, the k-means seeders (get_voronoi_seeds(method = "kmeans", sample_points =), voronoi_seeds_kmeans()) and assign_features_to_polygons() on its features. Where the row lasted to the end it was read where it was written: a square at 35 N with one vertex at 95 got a box centre at 65 N under pointize = "bbox_center", about 3,300 km from its other vertices, and ensure_stable_poly_id() keyed it and returned it after s2’s repair, without a word. Such a row of a layer in a geographic CRS now has no location in these readers, as a row with a coordinate beyond 1e150: coerce_to_points() gives it an EMPTY POINT in every mode, prep_model_data() and the fits drop it and count it, the seeders drop it from the cloud, assign_features_to_polygons() leaves it unassigned, and summarize_by_cell() and cell_values_at() leave it out of the pooled and scored rows, each in the words they use for a row without a location, which now name “a latitude beyond 90 degrees” for a lon/lat layer. coerce_to_points() and ensure_stable_poly_id() say so with a warning of class spatialkit_lat_beyond_90 that names the rows; ensure_stable_poly_id() keys such a row as an empty polygon, after the polygons with a location, and returns it as it came. A point layer with such a row no longer gets the projection’s warning that it cannot place the row beside the drop line. ensure_stable_poly_id(method = "centroid") and method = "surface_point" on a layer whose every polygon is empty stopped with base R’s “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”; they now give each row an ID. Layers with no latitude beyond 90 give the same results.

  • ensure_projected() stopped with “invalid crs” on a lon/lat layer whose box has no height and whose centre lies within 5 degrees of a pole. On such a box the Albers candidate’s standard parallels are 5 degrees either side of the centre on the sphere, and a line along one parallel that spans 180 degrees of longitude, such as LINESTRING (0 45, 180 45), runs over the pole, so its centre is the pole and the parallels were 85 and 95, which PROJ refuses. With purpose = "area" every such layer stopped, a single point included; with purpose = "distance" such a layer stopped where it reaches more than 5 degrees from its UTM zone’s central meridian. Every function that moves such a layer through ensure_projected() stopped with it. The Albers candidate is now built only when both standard parallels lie between -90 and 90; otherwise it is left out of the comparison, as a degenerate cone is. The line gets the Lambert azimuthal CRS centred on the pole, and a point at (10, 89) with purpose = "area" gets the one centred on it. Layers whose parallels lie in that range get the CRS and the crs_choice they got.

  • ensure_projected()’s warning on a lon/lat layer across a pole, or one whose longitudes are given outside -180 to 180, gave an offset from the UTM zone’s central meridian beyond 180 degrees. The zone comes from the centre on the sphere, whose longitude can lie far outside the box when the layer runs across a pole or its longitudes are given outside -180 to 180, and the offset was the difference of the box’s ends from the meridian, not wrapped. For two lines from (-10, 70) to (170, 70) and from (-10, 75) to (170, 75) the warning said the extent “reaches 257.0 deg from the central meridian of UTM zone 16”, and for points at longitudes 170, 185 and 200 it said “reaches 377.0 deg from the central meridian of UTM zone 1”. The offset is now the largest distance on the circle from the meridian to a longitude of the box, which is 180.0 and 17.0 there, and the 5-degree test that sends a layer to the comparison of candidates reads the same figure. That test changes its answer only for a layer whose longitudes are given outside -180 to 180 and lie within 5 degrees of the zone’s central meridian: points at longitudes 181 and 183, 2 degrees from the central meridian of UTM zone 1, were said to reach 360.0 degrees from it and got an Albers CRS, and now keep UTM zone 1, as a layer at -179 and -177 does; points at -181 and -183 now keep UTM zone 60 in the same way, as a layer at 179 and 177 does. Other layers get the CRS and the crs_choice they got.

  • A row of a lon/lat layer with a coordinate that is not finite or lies beyond 1e150 shaped the projection chosen for the other rows. ensure_projected() read the extent, the longitudes of the antimeridian test and the centre on every row. Among 300 points near (-80.4, 45.6), a row at longitude 1e200 was taken for a layer across the antimeridian, and the call stopped with sf’s “invalid crs” for a lon_0 of -2.95e190, as did every function that projects lon/lat input through it (resolution_profile() among them); a row at latitude 1e200 under purpose = "area" gave a Lambert azimuthal projection in place of the Albers conic the other 299 points get, and moved the second point by 21 km; the 39 stations above with a 40th row at longitude Inf were put in UTM zone 14. Such rows also raised sf’s “bounding box has potentially an invalid value range for longlat data”. The projection is now chosen with those rows empty, so the layer gets the CRS, and the other rows the coordinates, it gets with them empty, without that warning. A layer in which no row has a location gets Web Mercator (Equal Earth for purpose = "area"), and the log line says so, where it quoted a centre at “lon = NaN, lat = NaN”. Moved to another CRS, the rows come back empty in their own geometry type: by ensure_projected() from lon/lat, with or without target_crs, and from a projected CRS with target_crs; by harmonize_crs(); and wherever a function moves a boundary, cells_sf, polygons_sf or cover, or the polygons of cell_values_at()’s values, into the CRS of another layer. A polygon or line with one such vertex lost that vertex in sf::st_transform() and came back as a smaller finite shape, a half-degree square near (-93, 45) as a triangle of about half its area: create_grid_polygons() laid 55 cells over that triangle with nothing said, where it refuses the same row empty, and assign_features_to_polygons() joined a point inside the triangle to the square. A vertex at a northing of 1e200 in EPSG:32616 came back at a finite northing in EPSG:32615.

  • One coordinate that is not finite or lies beyond 1e150 made a layer without a CRS read as planar. The lon/lat test of a layer without a CRS read its bounding box, which one such row made infinite or put off the lon/lat envelope. Five points in degrees near (-93, 45) and a sixth at x = Inf were left in degrees by ensure_projected() with no warning, and prep_model_data() returned them in degrees for the fit; with a target CRS, or wherever a layer without a CRS takes the CRS of another (harmonize_crs(), a boundary beside projected points), the target was stamped on the degrees with a warning that they “do not look like lon/lat”; build_tessellation() on them stopped with GEOS’s “encountered NaN/Inf numbers”. A row at latitude 1e200 did the same. A boundary in metres without a CRS, given with points in EPSG:4326, was given EPSG:4326 when one vertex was infinite, and the call then stopped with “boundary must be polygonal”. The test now reads the box of the coordinates that have a location: the points are taken as EPSG:4326 and projected, with the warning, and the boundary is refused with the error that names both layers. A boundary without a CRS that has no such coordinate (no rows, or every coordinate infinite), given with points in a geographic CRS, is now refused with an error that says so; it was given the points’ CRS and refused later as “not polygonal”.

  • A polygon or line with a vertex at NA, and a row edited in place to a coordinate beyond 1e150, were read as located. The test of a row’s location read the layer’s bounding box first and read no vertex when the box was finite. sf::st_bbox() skips NA, so a ring with one vertex at (NA, y), which a file can carry as nan, passed: prep_model_data() kept it, the fits and predict_surface() gave it a value, make_folds() and fold_separation() read it as a point, harmonize_crs() moved it to a finite shape, and the readers of boundary and cover used the rest of its ring, where the same row with a vertex at Inf is left out. sf also keeps the box it stored on a geometry column when a row is replaced with [[<-, so a point edited to (1e200, y) or (Inf, y) passed: make_folds() put it in a fold with nothing said, where the same layer built whole leaves it out. The test now reads the coordinates themselves. kriging_adequacy() now reads cells_sf by the same rule: a cell with a vertex at NA, Inf or beyond 1e150 is left out (kr_ columns NA) with a warning that says why, as an empty cell is. It was repaired into the rest of its ring and kriged, and at 1e200 the call stopped with sp’s “invalid Polygon object”. print() of the result counts empty cells apart from thin ones.

  • coerce_to_points() gave a polygon with a vertex that is not finite or lies beyond 1e150 a point, and assign_features_to_polygons() joined such a polygon of polygons_sf. A line with such a vertex got an EMPTY POINT, but a polygon got a ring vertex under "auto" and "point_on_surface", (Inf, y) or (5e199, y) under "bbox_center", and (Inf, y) under "centroid" at 1e200. A geometry of any type with such a vertex now gets an EMPTY POINT in every mode. In assign_features_to_polygons() a polygon with a vertex at NA or Inf caught the points inside the rest of its ring, and with a vertex at Inf some of its neighbours’ too (15 points in a square that holds 5), and one at 1e200 stopped the call with GEOS’s “orientationIndex encountered NaN/Inf numbers”. Such a polygon now takes no point, and the points in it are unassigned, with the warning about unassigned features.

  • coerce_to_points() passed on sf’s warning “st_point_on_surface may not give correct results for longitude/latitude data”, and the summaries muffled it also where it was true. Every function that reduces a polygon layer in longitude and latitude to points (prep_model_data() and the fits, the cv_*() functions, make_folds(), fold_separation(), estimate_sac_range(), resolution_profile(), determine_optimal_levels() and others) raised it in sf’s words, while summarize_by_cell() and cell_values_at() muffled it. The point lies on the polygon read on the plane in degrees, the reading ?coerce_to_points states, and the warning is no longer raised; the points do not move. A polygon written across longitude 180 (from 179.5 to -179.5) GEOS reads the long way round the globe, and its point lay about 12,000 km from it: the summaries read it there with nothing said. Such a polygon now gets a point on it, taken with its longitudes read from 0 to 360; one whose point lies on it neither way, or that s2 cannot read, keeps GEOS’s point with a warning of class spatialkit_surface_point_off. A layer without a CRS whose coordinates look like longitude and latitude, which the functions that project it read as EPSG:4326, is read the same way, and coerce_to_points() says which rows that reading moves. The labels of plot_tessellation_map() on such cells are placed on them too.

  • coerce_to_points(mode = "bbox_center"), and mode = "centroid" with s2 off, put a lon/lat geometry written across longitude 180 near longitude 0. The box of a square from 179.5 to -179.5 spans the globe on the plane, and its centre, and GEOS’s centroid in degrees, lay at longitude 0, about 17,600 km from it at latitude 10, with nothing said. prep_model_data(pointize = "bbox_center") then read a layer of such squares as one that circles the North Pole and projected it in a Lambert azimuthal centred on the pole, where "auto" centres the projection on longitude 180. Such a geometry now gets the centre of its box, or GEOS’s centroid, with the longitudes below 0 read from 180 to 360, brought back into -180 to 180, as the points on the surface are read; a geometry wider than 180 degrees in both readings keeps the planar point. A layer without a CRS whose coordinates look like longitude and latitude is read the same way, with the warning that names the rows that reading moves. The same holds for the centroids "line_midpoint" takes of the rows that are not a LINESTRING, and "auto" of a MULTIPOINT and of the rows that are not points, lines or polygons, such as geometry collections: with s2 off, "auto" put a MULTIPOINT of (179.5, 10) and (-179.5, 10.5) at (0, 10.25). The centroids s2 takes and every other row’s point are unchanged.

  • prep_model_data() kept a row with a coordinate beyond 1e150 as a located row. It dropped a row whose geometry was empty or whose coordinates were not finite, but a point at (5e5, 1e200) in EPSG:32617 was kept, and so was the same point in EPSG:32616 beside a boundary in EPSG:32617, which the move put at a finite northing of 5,766,270. The fits read it as a location (fit_gwr_model() fitted 200 locations where the same layer with the row empty gives 199), and the grid of predict_surface() and the extent check of cv_block_size_sweep() read the extent of the prepared layer with the row in it. The bound is now read on the coordinates as given, before the projection, and again after it, so such a row is dropped with the rows whose geometry is empty, as the same row emptied is, and every fitter and cv_*() function that prepares its data here reads the layer without it. A polygon or line with such a vertex is dropped the same way. The predict() methods of rf_fit, gwr_fit and bayesian_fit moved newdata into the fit’s CRS before this reading, so a row of newdata at (5e5, 1e200) in EPSG:32616 beside a fit in EPSG:32617 was predicted at the finite point the move gave it (0.391 from a forest on the coordinates, where the same row emptied gives NA). They now empty such rows as given, before the move, and return NA for them; so does predict_surface() for such a row of a grid that is moved into the fit’s CRS or reduced from polygons (the row comes back empty), and a row of covariates without a location is no longer taken as the nearest feature of a grid point. The drop warning, and the log line of require_response = FALSE, count these rows as rows “without a location (an empty point, or a coordinate that is not finite or lies beyond 1e150)”, where they said “an empty or non-finite geometry”.

  • estimate_sac_range(), make_folds(), resolution_profile(), determine_optimal_levels() and fold_separation() kept a row at Inf or beyond 1e150, or read it after a move. They dropped a row whose geometry was empty or whose coordinates were missing, or not finite after the projection. A point at x = Inf or at a northing of 1e200 in EPSG:32617 made estimate_sac_range() return NA with the reason “the points have no extent”, where the same row empty gives a range; at latitude 1e200 in EPSG:4326 it stopped with FNN’s “Data include NAs”. make_folds(method = "block_kfold") stopped with base R’s “‘to’ must be a finite number” on the Inf row and gave the 1e200 row a block of its own (2 folds, of 299 points and 1, where the same row empty gives 5), random_kfold put either row in a test fold, and cv_block_size_sweep() stopped in make_folds() on either. resolution_profile() returned a WSS of NA at every level with the 1e200 row, and with sac in EPSG:32617 the same row in EPSG:32616 or EPSG:3857 was moved to a finite point and the profile built around it; determine_optimal_levels() stopped with base R’s “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”. A prediction point of fold_separation() or of make_folds(method = "nndm") and "knndm" at 1e200 in EPSG:32616 was moved into the data’s EPSG:32617 and measured there, and fold_separation() counted such a point in its print (“prediction target: 60 point(s)” where 59 have a location).
