A latitude beyond 90, finite as given, came back NaN from the projection and stopped estimate_sac_range() and make_folds(method = "nndm") and "knndm" with “Data include NAs”. The bound is now read on the coordinates as given, before the reduction to points and before any move, and again after the move: such a row is dropped with the rows whose geometry is empty, as the same row emptied is, and so is a lon/lat polygon with such a vertex. The drop warnings and log lines count these rows as points “without a location (an empty point, or a coordinate that is not finite or lies beyond 1e150)”, where they said “with empty or non-finite coordinates”. A row that loses its location in the projection is dropped too: estimate_sac_range() and make_folds() log a line that says it has none once projected, resolution_profile() and determine_optimal_levels() count it in their drop warning, and fold_separation() leaves it out of the distances as it leaves out an empty row. resolution_profile() drops a row that loses its location in the move into the CRS of sac with a warning that says so, where the move stopped the call with “some points have no coordinates in the CRS of sac”; with select_on = "split" the halves lose that row. The record of the rows’ locations that make_folds() keeps, and that the cv_*() functions and fold_separation() check folds against, leaves a row at Inf or beyond 1e150 out as it leaves out an empty one: in EPSG:3857 a row at x = 1e200 made make_folds() wait without end on PROJ’s move of it to EPSG:4326, and in a layer without a CRS a row at 1e200 widened the check’s tolerance to 1e191, so folds built on other data of the same size were accepted. cv_block_size_sweep() now runs on such a layer. An empty prediction point is no longer counted in make_folds()’s params$n_prediction_points. Layers whose rows all have a location give the same results as before.

  • make_folds(), the checks of supplied folds and compare_models() stalled on a projected row far beyond the Earth. The record of the rows’ locations that make_folds() keeps, and the record of a fit’s rows that compare_models() checks its AICc and LOOIC with, move the rows to EPSG:4326, and PROJ moves a point out of Web Mercator in time that grows with x: 1.6 s at x = 1e17, more than 20 s at 1e19, and no return within a minute at 1e20. Such a row is within 1e150 and has a location, so make_folds() on every method and the functions that build folds with it, compare_models_cv(), every cv_*() function, fold_separation(), kriging_adequacy() and area_of_applicability() given folds, and compare_models() with two or more AICc or LOOIC values did not return on an EPSG:3857 layer with a row at x = 1e20. A row of a projected layer with a coordinate beyond 1e10 in the CRS’s own unit, further out than any projected CRS places a point of the Earth, is now left out of both records, as an empty row is: the folds, the fits and the rows each function keeps are unchanged. The same move stalled ensure_projected(purpose = "area") and summarize_by_cell(area = TRUE) on polygons with such a vertex, which now find the area distortion unmeasured, and get_voronoi_seeds() and voronoi_seeds_kmeans() given a resolution profile and points in degrees, with or without a CRS, which now return such a centre of the profile empty. harmonize_crs(), and the shared step by which the package’s functions move one layer into the CRS of another or of a crs argument, now give such a row back empty when the target is in degrees: get_voronoi_seeds() with method = "kmeans" and a boundary in degrees stalled on such a sample point, and drops it now with its warning about points without a location, as it drops an empty one. Layers in degrees, without a CRS, or whose rows all lie within 1e10 of the origin, and moves into a projected CRS, give the same results as before.

  • The seeding functions, the Voronoi cells, clip_target_for(), assign_features_to_polygons(), the variogram design effect of summarize_by_cell() and kriging_adequacy() read a point at Inf or beyond 1e150 as a location, or read it after a move. With one of 300 sample points at a northing of 1e200, voronoi_seeds_kmeans() and get_voronoi_seeds(method = "kmeans") stopped with “no start gave a partition of the 300 point(s) into 15 cells”; the same point in EPSG:32616 beside a boundary in EPSG:32617 was moved to a finite point and clustered with nothing said. create_voronoi_polygons() and build_tessellation(method = "voronoi") with one of 30 seeds at x = Inf or a northing of 1e200 stopped with GEOS’s “Could not locate vertex”, “encountered NaN/Inf numbers” or “distance must be a finite value”, and with the seed in another CRS than the boundary’s with “Points of LinearRing do not form a closed linestring”; clip_target_for() stopped the same way at Inf and returned a target of infinite area at 1e200. One point of a cover at Inf or 1e200 set the whole cover aside, with the warning that it gives no polygon, and the cells covered 5,334 km^2 where the same point empty gives 10,516 km^2; a polygon cover in EPSG:32616 with a vertex at a northing of 1e200 was moved into EPSG:32617 as a boundary of 68,562 km^2, where the same row empty gives 8,983 km^2. assign_features_to_polygons() joined a point at 1e200 in EPSG:32616 to the polygon in EPSG:32617 where the move put it, and its warning said that a row at Inf or 1e200 falls inside no polygon and advised checking that the polygons cover the features. summarize_by_cell(deff = "variogram") correlated a point at 1e200, as given or moved into the variogram’s CRS, with the others of its cell (a standard error of 0.543 where the same row empty gives 0.664), and kriging_adequacy() stopped in gstat::krige() on a point at Inf and kriged from one at 1e200, as given or moved to a finite point (moved, its folds held 399 points and 1). The bound is now read on the coordinates as given, before any move, and again after it, and such a point is read as an empty point: dropped by the seeders with their warning, NA in index and counted with the empty seeds and points, left out of the clip target’s box and of the cover, matched to no polygon, and left out of the correlation and of the kriging. The warnings and log lines count these points as points “without a location” or with “no location (an empty point, or a coordinate that is not finite or lies beyond 1e150)”, where they said “with empty or non-finite coordinates” or “empty geometry”, and the refusal of kriging_adequacy() counts the points with a finite response and a location. Layers whose rows all have a location give the same results as before.

  • area_of_applicability() gave a location index to a row beyond 1e150, and refused training data with one for a false reason. With location measured (coords = "yes", or a fit whose predictions depend on it), a row of newdata at (5e5, 1e200) in the training CRS got a DI_location of 2.6e149 and AOA = FALSE, and the same row in EPSG:32616 beside training data in EPSG:32617, moved to a finite point, got 15.1; the same row emptied gets NA in both. Such a row in train_sf stopped the call with “every training row is at the same location”, which was false. The bound is now read on the coordinates as given and again after the move, so such a row of newdata gets NA in DI_location and AOA, and such a training row is left out of the reference distances, as the same rows emptied are. For a forest fitted with include_coords = TRUE the row’s "..x" and "..y" are NA (they held 1e200, or Inf for an infinite coordinate), and a row of newdata reprojected into the training CRS comes back with an empty geometry. The refusals for too few usable training rows, and for folds beside training rows that are left out, now name a missing location as a cause where location is measured; the second said “missing predictor values” for a row with an infinite predictor or no location.

  • area_of_applicability() dropped a predictor at a large offset as having no variance. Its test kept a predictor only where the standard deviation was more than 1.5e-8 of the largest absolute value, which reads the column’s distance from 0, not its spread. A predictor with standard deviation 1 at 1e8, or a timestamp in seconds, was dropped with the log line “dropping predictor(s) with no variance in the training data”, the index was computed on the other predictors, and new rows were read on that predictor through the slack of a dropped column instead: at 1e8, rows more than 1.5 beyond the training range got DI = Inf, the others were judged on the other predictors alone, and the threshold fell from 0.306 to 0.048; at 1.7e9, 19 of 20 rows 4 standard deviations out were inside the AOA, and at 1e15, 20 of 20 rows 6 out. A predictor the test drops is now kept where its values differ by more than their rounding (3 units in the last place of the largest absolute value), with its training mean and standard deviation in scaling, so dropped_vars, DI, the threshold and AOA are those of the same predictor at 0. The same reading keeps a predictor in units whose squares vanish or overflow (standard deviation 1e-170 or 1e200), which was dropped too. A predictor still dropped reads a new row as a different value when it lies outside the training range by more than 3 units in the last place of the training values, where the slack was 1.5e-8 of their size: 25 for a constant timestamp at 1.7e9, so a row 25 seconds away was not extrapolation. For a predictor that is 0 throughout, the slack is 3 units in the last place of 1 (6.7e-16) where it was 1.5e-8. Predictors the first test keeps give what they gave.

  • gp_lengthscale_bounds() read every row of coords_xy. A row of NA stopped it with base R’s “missing values and NaN’s not allowed if ‘na.rm’ is FALSE”, and a row at Inf or 1e200 made the upper bound Inf with no warning. A row with a coordinate that is missing, not finite or beyond 1e150 is now left out, with a warning of class spatialkit_rows_dropped that gives the count, and the bounds are those of the other rows.

  • The projection chosen for a small lon/lat MULTIPOINT layer depended on the order of the points in each feature. A layer of features that are not points, with fewer than 40 distinct locations, is scored on its features’ vertices too, with points added along the edges between them. A MULTIPOINT has no edges, but points were added on the segments between consecutive members of each feature, at places the layer does not have, and they moved with the order of the members: two MULTIPOINTs of five points each scored 0.75 percent in UTM zone 14 in one order and 0.78 percent in another. A MULTIPOINT layer is now scored on its member points with nothing added between them, which is the score of the same points as a POINT layer. For such a layer the CRS, attr(, "crs_choice") and the logged figures can differ from before; MULTIPOINT layers with 40 distinct locations or more score as before.

  • A lon/lat layer that mixes geometry types or holds GEOMETRYCOLLECTIONs was scored without its outline, and across 180 degrees ensure_projected() stopped on it. sf::st_coordinates() refuses such a layer (class sfc_GEOMETRY or sfc_GEOMETRYCOLLECTION, as rbind(), c(), sf::st_make_valid() and sf::st_intersection() can give), so the vertices that score a layer of fewer than 40 features were not read. Two boxes, one listed as a MULTIPOLYGON, were scored on the one pair between their interior points and got a Lambert azimuthal CRS with “0.12% against the zone’s 0.47%”, where the same boxes as MULTIPOLYGONs get an Albers CRS with “1.13% against the zone’s 6.57%”; a box over the conterminous United States listed as one GEOMETRYCOLLECTION scored NA for every candidate and kept UTM zone 15. The test for a layer that straddles longitude 180 read the coordinates the same way, outside any handler, so ensure_projected(), and the builders and fits that project a lon/lat layer through it, stopped with sf’s “not implemented for objects of class sfc_GEOMETRY” on such a layer across 180. Such a layer is now read feature by feature, each collection unpacked into its members, so it scores, chooses and logs as the same features in one type. The points of a POINT or MULTIPOINT among them are not filled between either. sf::st_is_empty() calls a GEOMETRYCOLLECTION, MULTIPOLYGON or MULTILINESTRING empty when its first part is empty, and such a feature was left out of the score: a box listed after an empty line in one GEOMETRYCOLLECTION scored NA for every candidate. Empty parts are now dropped before empty features, so such a feature is scored on its other parts. Layers of one geometry type with no empty part score as before.

  • ensure_projected() read a small CRS-less layer of mixed geometry types as planar, and gave a layer of mixed types that s2 refuses EPSG:3857. With no CRS, a layer under one degree across is taken as lon/lat when its coordinates have fractional degrees, and that test read the coordinates with sf::st_coordinates(), which refuses a layer of mixed types or of collections: two boxes of 0.3 degrees in Germany, one listed as a MULTIPOLYGON, were returned with no CRS and crs_assumed "none", where the same boxes as MULTIPOLYGONs are taken as EPSG:4326 and projected to UTM zone 32. A layer whose only feature has an empty first part, which sf::st_is_empty() calls empty, was read as planar too. When s2 refuses a lon/lat layer even after the repair (a bowtie polygon), its centre is the mean of its vertices, which were read the same way: a bowtie beside a MULTIPOLYGON got no centre and EPSG:3857, where the same features as MULTIPOLYGONs get a CRS centred on them. Both now read such a layer feature by feature, as the same features in one type.

  • A lon/lat layer with Z or M coordinates was not scored as its XY copy. The outline of a layer of fewer than 40 features is read ring by ring, and the key of a ring read Z and M as well, so an edge between two vertices with other Z or M was not filled: a box over the conterminous United States whose corners differ in Z got a Lambert azimuthal CRS with “0.97% against the zone’s 5.42%”, where its XY copy gets an Albers CRS with “1.13% against the zone’s 6.71%”. A line with Z kept its Z on the point that represents it beside XY vertices, and GEOS refuses M, so on a LINESTRING Z, or on a layer of lines, polygons or MULTIPOINTs with M, every candidate scored NA and the UTM zone was kept. The layer is now scored in x and y, and the ring key reads the ring and part columns alone, so such a layer scores, chooses and logs as its sf::st_zm() copy. The layer returned keeps its Z and

    1. Layers in XY score as before.

  • summarize_by_cell(area = TRUE) refused projected cells when s2 refused one of them in degrees. The area check compares the cells’ planar areas with their geodesic areas, which s2 measures on the cells’ copy in EPSG:4326, and it took the geodesic areas in one call. Two corners a fraction of a nanometre apart in the cells’ CRS can fall on one point in degrees, where s2 refuses the ring (“duplicate vertex”), and then the call failed for every cell. A vertex listed twice, which GEOS accepts, does the same. The k-means cells of a 30 by 20 lattice at 30 m, built and kept in EPSG:32615 from rows in degrees, are all valid in EPSG:32615 and s2 refuses 4 of the 133; the request was refused because “the area distortion of cells_sf’s CRS could not be measured”. ensure_projected(purpose = "area") on projected input skipped its check in silence the same way: 20 cells of 1 degree from 30N to 69N in Web Mercator, which distort areas by 214 percent, logged nothing when one cell had such a pair of corners. When the one call fails, the geodesic areas are now taken one cell at a time, and a cell s2 refuses is measured again without the vertices that repeat the one before them in degrees, which leaves its points and its area as they were. The lattice’s cells get a density, with attr(, "area_error") the spread over all 133 cells, and the warning is logged for the Web Mercator cells. A cell s2 refuses even then, such as one whose edges cross, still leaves the spread over the cells unmeasured: summarize_by_cell(area = TRUE) refuses the request (since GEOS calls such a cell invalid, with the error on invalid cells below), and ensure_projected() measures the grid over the extent instead. A layer whose cells s2 all accepts gets the same figure as before.

  • ensure_projected(purpose = "area") skipped its check in silence on a projected layer of one polygon, and summarize_by_cell(area = TRUE) refused one cell for a cause it did not have. One polygon gives one ratio of planar to geodesic area, which has no spread, so the distortion came out unmeasured and nothing was logged: a box from 100W to 90W and from 30N to 60N in Web Mercator logged nothing, where the same box split in two logs 26.2 percent. A layer with a polygon s2 refuses in degrees, such as one whose edges cross, was passed over the same way: 20 cells of 1 degree from 30N to 69N in Web Mercator, one of them a bowtie, logged nothing. summarize_by_cell(area = TRUE) refused a single cell, a 10 km square in UTM zone 15 among them, because “the area distortion of cells_sf’s CRS could not be measured (no polygon areas, or geodesic areas unavailable)”, though the cell has both; a single lon/lat cell was refused the same way. Both functions now measure such a layer on a 6 by 6 grid over its bounding box, as they measure a layer without polygons. ensure_projected() logs the grid’s figure when it exceeds 1 percent (65.2 percent for the box, 124.4 percent for the cells with the bowtie), and logs that the distortion could not be measured when the grid gives no figure either (a single point, or a line along one axis). summarize_by_cell() gives a single cell its density, with attr(, "area_error") the grid’s figure, or refuses it for the distortion. A layer whose polygons give a figure gets the same figure and the same log as before.

  • summarize_by_cell(area = TRUE) gave a projected cell whose edges cross a density over GEOS’s area of its ring. The area check measures up to 200 of the cells, together with the cells that reach furthest; a cell s2 refused among them made the request refused, but one outside them got sf::st_area()’s area, which for a ring whose edges cross is the signed sum of its lobes. Of 400 squares of 10 km in EPSG:32615 with a bowtie of 4.25e7 square metres, the bowtie got a cell_area of 2e7 square metres at cell 148 and the request was refused with the bowtie at cell 1, so the outcome turned on which cells the check took. Every non-empty projected cell is now checked with sf::st_is_valid() in its CRS before any summary, and a cell GEOS calls invalid makes the request refused, with the first such cells, GEOS’s reason and the remedy: repair the cells with sf::st_make_valid() and pass them again. A cell GEOS calls invalid that s2 measures in degrees, such as one with a hole outside its shell, is refused by the same check. Valid cells get the densities and attr(, "area_error") they got before. ensure_projected(purpose = "area") on projected input read the same planar area as a figure about the CRS: three 10 km squares of UTM zone 15 beside a square with a hole outside its shell logged a distortion of 40.0 percent, the difference between the shell minus the hole and the shell plus the hole. A layer with a polygon GEOS calls invalid is now measured on the 6 by 6 grid over its extent, which logs nothing for that layer.

  • resolution_profile() reported a layer too small for a ladder as supported. With fewer than two cells at min_cell_n it raised the ceiling to 2 with supported = TRUE. It still scores two cells, with supported = FALSE, ceiling_from = "fewer than two supported cells" and a warning of class spatialkit_not_supported that says what would work.

  • A constant response got a finite cp. A response of 1e6 plus rounding noise was scored on its rounding error and select_resolution() returned 2 cells for it. cp, moran_i and moran_z are now NA at every level, with a warning of class spatialkit_constant_response.

  • determine_optimal_levels() returned 1 for a layer with no rows. It is now an error.

  • The leakage warning of make_folds(method = "block_kfold") recommended settings that stopped with an error or returned fewer folds. It ended “Pass block_size = or auto_range = TRUE” whatever the layout. The warning now builds the grid the advice asks for and says what comes back: the setting when that gives k folds, and otherwise the largest block size that does and method = "nndm" ("knndm" above 5,000 rows) as the design that needs no block size. The single-block error names that size too.

  • make_folds() returned fewer folds than asked with only a log line. "random_kfold" with more folds than rows, "block_kfold" with fewer than k occupied cells and "leave_location_out" with more folds than groups now raise a warning of class spatialkit_k_reduced, which carries k_requested and k and, where there is one, gives a setting that works. params$k_requested records the k asked for, and params$block_width and params$block_height the cells built. cv_block_size_sweep() gathers the reductions of its sizes into one warning, and its table gains the columns block_width and block_height.

  • The default ladder of cv_block_size_sweep() gave other blocks in another unit. Its bottom rung is a twenty-fifth of the shorter side, which that side holds exactly 25 times. The rung was computed as exp(log(side / 25)), a hair above or below it, and the blocks per side as floor(side / size), so the last bits of the unit decided between 24 and 25 blocks. On an 8 x 8 lattice at 250 m the bottom rung’s blocks were 72.9 m wide in metres and 70 m in units of 1e-6 m, and blocks_used changed with the unit on other layers. The ladder now starts at side / 25 and ends at its top exactly. make_folds(block_size = ), which builds each rung’s grid, now reads a block size within one part in ten million above an extent over a whole number as that number of blocks, called from the sweep or directly. The bottom rung gives 25 blocks along the shorter side in every unit.

  • cv_block_size_sweep() stated its fits wrongly in four texts. With block_sizes supplied, the refusal over max_fits advised lowering n_sizes, which only the default ladder reads; it now advises fewer block_sizes or a smaller k. On either ladder, when the count includes the random reference, it also names include_random = FALSE, which at n_sizes = 1 and k = 2 is the only way to cut the count. When every size of the default ladder needs a grid of more than 1,000,000 blocks (points on a line a hair wide), the sweep refused with “no block size leaves at least k = 5 blocks …; pass smaller block_sizes”, where the sizes held too many blocks and smaller ones are refused; it now says so and names the largest size whose grid holds k blocks, to pass as block_sizes. The header of print() and the caption of plot() gave the fits planned before any fold was built, and the caption said k folds per size, where a size whose grid has fewer than k cells holding points builds fewer. Both now count the fits made from the k column, and the caption says “up to k folds per size” when a size built fewer. attr(, "n_fits") stays the count planned, which the max_fits check reads.

  • fold_separation() printed “this score is optimistic” from a share that cannot give a direction. Which way a score errs depends on how the held-out distances compare with the distances from the prediction locations to the data. Without prediction_points the function now reports the distances and draws no conclusion. The column within_range (the share of held-out points closer than the range) is replaced by mean_cor, the mean correlation between a held-out point and its nearest training point; code that reads the old column has to be changed. n_unknown_ids counts each row once; it counted fold entries, so five missing rows read as 25 at k = 5.

  • make_folds(method = "nndm") returned plain leave-one-out without a warning when the prediction points were nearer to the data than leave-one-out can reach. Excluding neighbours only lengthens a held-out distance. A warning of class spatialkit_nndm_out_of_reach now says that the cross-validated error is an upper bound for those locations, and params gains max_ecdf_deficit, loo_ecdf_deficit, target_out_of_reach and the Wasserstein distances.

  • cv_spatial(), cv_rf(), cv_gwr(), cv_bayes() and compare_models_cv() dropped block_size and auto_range = TRUE without a word when folds was supplied. They raise a warning of class spatialkit_fold_args_ignored.

  • cv_spatial() scored a fold’s predictions against response_var without checking that the fold’s fit models it. A fit_fn that fits price, called with response_var = "slope", had its predictions of price scored against slope on every fold, and the result was reported as the cross-validated score of a model of slope, with every fold ok. A fold whose fit’s response_var is not the call’s now fails, with both names in fold_status, as a fold whose fit_fn returns no spatial_fit does; when every fold fails so, the all-folds-failed warning gives that cause. The same holds in cv_block_size_sweep() and select_features_forward(), which run their fit_fn through the same folds; the hold-out score of select_features_forward(select_on = "split") is NA for such a fit, with a warning that gives both names. A named response_var, such as c(r = "price"), is compared by the column it names. The package’s own fitters fit the call’s response and are unchanged.

  • compare_models(fits, newdata = ) labelled training-residual Moran’s I as a newdata metric. A new column resid_morans_basis says "in-sample", or "out-of-bag" for a forest.

  • compare_models_cv(), cv_block_size_sweep() and select_features_forward() repeated the same data warning for every model, size or candidate set. The warnings prep_model_data() raises about a layer are raised once per call. With parallel above one core, a fold’s classed warning keeps its class and fields.

  • model_metrics(fit, newdata, draws = TRUE) stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”. draws = TRUE and se.fit = TRUE are refused by name: the metrics take one predicted value per row.

  • A predictor far from zero made fit_gwr_model() report every window as collinear. Windows whose condition index with the intercept (cn) was above 1e6 were counted, a rule for a solve of the uncentred normal equations. A window’s slopes now count as collinear on the slope index alone (cn_slopes above 30, or singular).

  • The GWR bandwidth search could select a bandwidth at which a term is estimable at no location. Such a bandwidth is not selected; when every bandwidth is like that the widest is used, with a warning and info$bandwidth_is_fallback = TRUE.

  • area_of_applicability() returned a threshold of 0 for repeat visits. With folds = NULL a training row that repeats another’s predictor values was its own nearest neighbour at distance 0: 60 sites visited 4 times put 30 of 200 new points inside. Each row’s reference is now its nearest row with different values, and the same layout puts 188 inside (n_duplicates counts the repeats). With folds, a threshold of 0 is a warning of class spatialkit_aoa_zero_threshold.

  • Without FNN, area_of_applicability() gave exact copies of training rows a small non-zero distance. About one copy in ten came out near 1e-8 and could fall outside a threshold of 0. The distance returned is now recomputed exactly.

  • area_of_applicability() counted points beyond the training extent as inside for a forest fitted with coordinates. Location was measured only through the forest’s ..x and ..y columns, which under weights = "auto" took the forest’s own importance, so a forest that barely split on its coordinates gave location almost no weight: in a test where half of 50 prediction points lay one half to one and a half extents beyond the data, 41 read as inside, 16 of them beyond the extent. Such a forest now gets the location index a GWR and a Bayesian fit get, and none of the 25 is inside. The predictor index is unchanged.

  • select_features_forward() always selected at least one variable with a forest or a GWR. A learner that could not fit an empty predictor set had no baseline, so the first variable was accepted whatever it scored. The baseline is now the learner’s own null model (a GWR fits one), null_fn, or the mean of each training fold. Under a fold-mean baseline the first variable is tested at the end and can be dropped (baseline$first); plot() draws the path as walked. A forest sweep can still add noise variables after the real ones, because an extra variable regularises the forest; ?select_features_forward says how to read that. tol takes any single number, Inf included.

  • plot() on an area of applicability with a location index counted the wrong rows beside the predictor threshold. It printed the rows outside on either index. The subtitle now counts the predictor index, location and the total separately.

  • One row of newdata with a factor level the model was not fitted with made predict() on a bayesian_fit return NA for every row. Rows with such a value are NA, the rest are predicted, and a warning of class spatialkit_new_levels names the predictor and the levels. Any other failed posterior draw is a warning of class spatialkit_predict_failed, where it was a log line.

  • prep_model_data() dropped incomplete rows with a log line only. When preparing data for a fit it raises a warning of class spatialkit_rows_dropped with the number and share of rows, the count by reason and by column, and how far the response of the dropped rows sits from that of the kept rows. A predictor with one value in every kept row raises spatialkit_constant_predictor. Preparing newdata for predict() raises neither. attr(, "dropped") gains by_column, response_std_diff, constant_predictors and n_duplicate_locations.

  • prep_model_data() measured the shift of the dropped rows on the rounding of a response at a large offset. response_std_diff and the spatialkit_rows_dropped warning’s “a difference of X SD” were a difference of the raw means of the dropped and the kept rows, and a double holds each mean of a response at 1e15 only to an eighth. On 40 rows with 6 dropped, the same stored values gave 0.87 SD at offset 0 and 0.93 SD at 1e15, and only the second added “more than two standard errors, so the rows are not missing at random”. Where the raw values of the response lose their spread, the means and the standard deviation are now taken less the response’s centre, as estimate_sac_range() takes it, and the centre is added back to the means the message quotes. The shift and the verdict are those of the same values at 0. A response of one value up to rounding, whose standard deviation is its last bit, now gets NA and no shift sentence, as a response of one value does: with the dropped rows one unit in the last place above most kept rows, it read “a difference of 1.61 SD, more than two standard errors, so the rows are not missing at random” at 1.23, 4.5e6 and 1e15 alike. Every other response is read as it was, to the last bit.

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model() stops before compiling when the response takes a single value, and raises a warning of class spatialkit_gp_basis_size when there are fewer rows than a tenth of the basis functions.

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model() handed brms the response as given, so its fit depended on the response’s origin and units. Stan starts every parameter between -2 and 2, and brms floors its default priors for the intercept, the residual SD and the GP’s SD at a scale of 2.5 in the response’s units. At an offset of 1e8 the posterior mean fitted values missed the response by the offset; in units of 1e-20 they were 1e15 response SDs off, after divergent transitions; near 1e160 the fit had no draws and said nothing; and cv_bayes() folds failed or scored the same way. Under the gaussian, student, skew_normal, exgaussian and asym_laplace families with an identity link, a response whose centre is more than 1,000 times its spread from zero is now handed to brms less that centre, and one whose SD lies outside 2^-20 to 2^20 is divided by the power of two nearest it. Under exgaussian and asym_laplace the rule is narrower, a centre more than 4 times the spread and an SD outside 2^-2 to 2^2, because brms’s default prior on exgaussian’s beta and Stan’s starting values do not follow the response: an exgaussian fit at an SD near 1,000, or 300 SDs from zero, had no draws, and an asym_laplace fit 300 SDs from zero or at an SD near 1e-4 came back with sigma at twice its value or more. fitted(), predict() and its draws, residuals(), coef(), $info$loo, $info$looic, $info$gp_adequacy$sdgp and $info$b_prior are given in the response’s units, and $info$response_scaling records the centre and scale. Every other response is handed over as it is, and its draws do not change. A prior on a class on the response’s scale keeps the response as given, with a warning of class spatialkit_response_scale. A response whose values differ only by rounding (1e15 and the next double) is refused as a constant one is; it was sampled. cv_bayes() takes yhat_sd at any size, where sd() of draws near 1e160 overflowed. The spatial share in $info$gp_adequacy is taken at any size of the response: its squares overflowed near 1e160 and underflowed below about 1e-162, so the share was NA and the length-scale rule decided whether the GP is identified in its place.

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model() returned a fit with no posterior draws and said nothing. When Stan rejected every starting value, rstan returned an empty fit, $info$convergence_ok was NA, $info$looic was NA, no warning was raised, and fitted() stopped later. Such a fit is now an error that gives the response’s median and SD as brms was given it and the family.

  • summarize_by_cell() let one infinite value through. An Inf in a response or predictor column made its cell’s mean Inf and, under deff = "kish", set the ICC to 0 for every cell. Infinite values are now left out of every statistic of their column, as NA is, with a warning of class spatialkit_nonfinite.

  • kriging_adequacy() kriged a factor on its level codes. A response that is not numeric or logical is an error that names the column and its class. A logical response is kriged as 0/1.

  • kriging_adequacy() capped the replicates’ variance at the nugget. Under a model with too small a nugget the means of repeat observations were kriged as more exact than their replicates show. Their pooled within-location variance sw2 is now used as it is: a mean of m replicates has error variance max(c0 - sw2, 0) + sw2 / m for a nugget c0. A warning of class spatialkit_replicate_var_above_nugget gives both numbers, and attr(, "replicates") records them.

  • A subset of an assigned layer kept its parent’s "unassigned" record. [ and the dplyr row verbs drop it, as they drop "dropped" and "ties".

  • plot.resolution_profile() says “fewer than two cells meet min_cell_n” of a profile that is unsupported for that reason; it said the floor exceeds the ceiling. plot_folds() and print() on a kriging_adequacy() result label kNNDM folds.

  • ensure_stable_poly_id() stopped on a cell that is valid in its own CRS and crosses itself in lon/lat, and took build_tessellation(method = "voronoi") with it. The sort key is measured on a lon/lat copy with s2. Only the vertices are transformed, and s2 joins them with great-circle arcs, so a long straight edge that passes about a metre from another vertex of the same ring can come out on the other side of that vertex. s2 refuses such a ring, the repair of the lon/lat copy does not split crossing edges, and st_centroid() and st_area() stopped with “Loop 1 is not valid: Edge 36 crosses edge 52”. Met on 1 of 291 Voronoi cells of Texas clipped to the state outline in EPSG:5070, where a 36.9 km cell edge passes 1.47 m from a vertex of the coastline and the great circle through its ends passes 0.37 m beyond that vertex: no cell of the state got an ID. A feature s2 still refuses after the repair now gets a second repair of its own sort copy with the crossing edges split, and if s2 refuses that too its centroid and area are measured as plane geometry in the layer’s own CRS and the centroid is transformed to the sort CRS. The function warns once, saying how many features took each route, and create_voronoi_polygons() and build_tessellation(method = "voronoi") pass the warning on. Those features’ keys are close to the spherical ones and not equal to them: the second repair moved the Texas cell’s area by about 40 square metres in 2,949 square kilometres, and its centroid taken in the plane of EPSG:5070 lay 20 m from the one the second repair gave on the sphere. Every other feature keeps exactly the key it had, so the other 290 Texas cells are numbered in the order they always would have been, the geometry returned is still the caller’s own, and the same 291 cells get the same IDs in EPSG:5070, EPSG:3083, UTM zone 14N, Web Mercator and lon/lat. A feature keyed in the plane is measured in the CRS the layer arrived in (the Texas cell’s plane centroid lies 9 to 73 m from the spherical one depending on that CRS), so it can take another place in the order when the same layer arrives in another projection, and the IDs between the two places move with it; the warning says so whenever that route is taken. With make_valid = FALSE no repair is tried, as the caller asked, and a feature s2 refuses goes straight to the plane: such a call used to stop with s2’s error and now returns IDs with the warning. All three methods are covered: for "surface_point" and "bbox_center" the point never went to s2, but the area, the third key of each, did, and both stopped there. An error that is not s2 refusing a feature is raised as it was.

  • resolution_profile() took the noise variance of C_p from the nugget of a variogram fit that had not converged, whenever the range was refused for another reason. Its documentation says a model that did not converge gives cp no nugget, the nugget and sill being where the optimiser stopped, and the profile decided that by looking for “converge” in rejected_reason. estimate_sac_range() gives a refused range one reason, and a falling variogram and a range past the largest lag come before the optimiser in it, so a fit that stopped at gstat’s iteration limit with a range past the fitted lags is recorded as "fitted range exceeds the largest lag fitted". That is most fits that do not converge: over 200 simulated layers (trends, ranges longer than the extent, 40–60 points, white noise) 96 of the 102 all-pairs fits that did not converge carried that reason and 6 "variogram model did not converge". With an east-west trend on an exponential field (300 points, nugget 0.1, 25 draws) every all-pairs fit stopped at the limit, every one was refused as past the lags, and C_p was given nuggets of 1.18–1.62; in the first draw the range reported was 29,180 against a largest lag of 647. Whether the model converged is now read from the model (attr(attr(sac, "variogram_model"), "converged"), which estimate_sac_range() already set); a sac that carries no such flag (made by hand, or built from REML parameters) is judged by its reason, as before, and a reason that says the fit did not converge is believed whatever the flag says. For a refused range whose model did not converge, cp takes its noise variance from the finest level whose cells hold at least two scored rows on average, attr(x, "cp_noise")$source reads "finest-level residual mean square", attr(x, "variogram") is NULL, and the warning names both facts: why the range was refused, and that the model did not converge. The existing notice that names the level and the variance cp was given follows it, so such a profile raises two warnings where it raised one. The finest-level value can be larger or smaller than the nugget it replaces (larger in 41 of 52 simulated layers, smaller in 11), so the cp pick can move either way: it stayed in 49, moved to fewer cells in 2 and to more in 1. When no level holds two scored rows a cell, cp is NA at every level for such a sac, where it was finite; the warning’s last clause says so, and the notice is not raised. A fit that converged to a range past the lags, or on a falling variogram, still gives cp its nugget. (estimate_sac_range() no longer fits with gstat’s iterative fit: the flag is now FALSE when the criterion has no minimum inside the ranges searched, and the reason "variogram model did not converge" is carried only by results stored by earlier versions.)

  • A clipped cell that also touched the boundary from outside was dropped, and its points left with no cell. st_intersection() returns such a cell as a GEOMETRYCOLLECTION of its area and a line or point (on an L-shaped boundary, the cell over the inner corner), and the Voronoi, grid and Delaunay builders kept only POLYGON and MULTIPOLYGON rows, so the whole cell went, area and all. On a 4 x 4 L with square cells of side 2, ten of thirty points had no cell and the cells covered 8 of the boundary’s 10 square units. Each collection is now reduced to its polygonal part, one row per cell still; a piece with no area is dropped as before.

  • build_tessellation() gave NA in index to a seed outside a boundary that is not convex, although its cell was built. A k-means centre is a mean of observations and can lie over a bay or a bend of a coast; its cell, the part of the study area nearer it than any other seed, holds ground and observations. index gave each point the cell it lies in, and such a seed lies in none, so it was NA and the warning told the user to pass a boundary that holds it. With seeds$cell_id <- tess$index, cell_values_at(seeds = ) then put every location nearest that seed in no cell and filled it from the cell of its nearest scored row, which is not always the cell that holds it: on a notched square with one seed in the notch, 89 of 591 locations were filled, 6 of them from another cell. build_tessellation(method = "voronoi") and create_voronoi_polygons() now carry each cell’s generator through the clip, and for seeds index holds the cell each one generates, so on that square no location is filled for want of a seed. Seeds are a layer a seeding function returned (rbind() of such layers included), the seeds of a select_resolution() result, points that carry a record of the count and are its seeds (a seed_id column, or the record’s centres), and points given with a cover. Other points are indexed by the cell that holds them, as before, so an observation outside the boundary is still NA, also one that carries a selection’s record as assign_features_to_polygons() returns it. A seed is NA only when the clip removed its cell whole or its geometry is empty, and the warning then says that the points are seeds and why they have no cell. The cells are unchanged. The cell that holds each seed, which index gave before, is assign_features_to_polygons(seeds, tess$cells, polygon_id_col = "cell_id", keep_unassigned = TRUE)$cell_id.

  • cell_values_at(seeds = ) filled the locations nearest a point placed by hand outside a boundary that is not convex. Points that are not seeds are indexed by the cell that holds them, so such a point used as a seed had NA in index, and the locations nearest it had no cell and were filled: the same 89 of 591 locations for the six points of the notched square. A selection’s seeds bound with rbind(), which drops the attributes that make them seeds, did the same. When values carries the cell polygons, a seed with an NA ID that lies in none of them now takes the ID of the cell it generates, the polygon no seed names that a point inside it finds as its nearest seed, so with index alone every location of the notched square takes the cell that holds it and none is filled for want of a seed. A seed with an NA ID inside a polygon keeps it, as does one whose cell the clip removed. Without the polygons in values the locations nearest such a seed still have no cell; get_voronoi_seeds(method = "provided", seeds = ) before the tessellation makes the points seeds, and index then gives each its cell.

  • For points placed by hand that share a cell in index, the error of cell_values_at(seeds = ) told the caller to do what had been done, and ?cell_values_at said such a point is NA. build_tessellation() gives a point that is not a seed and lies in no cell, but within a thousandth of the median cell width of one, the ID of the nearest cell. Beside a notch in the boundary that can be the cell of another point, so two points had one ID in index, and with seeds$cell_id <- tess$index the call stopped with “2 seeds have the cell of another”, which advised setting the column from index. The error now says why index repeats the ID, and that points passed through get_voronoi_seeds(method = "provided", seeds = ) before build_tessellation() each take the cell they generate. ?cell_values_at and ?create_voronoi_polygons now say such a point takes the ID of the nearest cell. The call still stops: two seeds at different locations cannot share a cell.

  • create_voronoi_polygons() counted the points and seeds in no cell in the name of build_tessellation(), and build_tessellation() counted the cover points in no cell in the name of create_voronoi_polygons(). Called directly, the spatialkit_unassigned warnings of create_voronoi_polygons() on points and seeds began “build_tessellation():”, a function the caller had not called, as did the log line on points and cover points assigned to the nearest cell. Through build_tessellation(method = "voronoi") the warning on cover points outside every cell began “create_voronoi_polygons():”, where the grid and triangle methods name build_tessellation(). Each now names the function called.

  • voronoi_seeds_kmeans() gave the distinct positions as the reason for a clamp set by the number of points. Asked for as many seeds as there are points, each at its own position, it returns one fewer, since stats::kmeans() refuses as many centres as rows, and warned “requested 10 seeds but only 10 unique positions among 10 point(s); clamping to 9”. The warning now takes the words of get_voronoi_seeds() for the same clamp: “the points support at most 9 (10 unique position(s) among 10 point(s))”. The help says k is clamped to the distinct positions or one fewer than the points with a location, whichever is smaller; k said nrow(points_sf) - 1, which counts the rows without a location that are dropped first. A count that is not whole, such as 9.5, is now given as requested in this warning and in the same warning of get_voronoi_seeds(), which said “requested 9 seeds” for a clamp to 9.

  • cell_values_at(seeds = ) filled every location, and raised nothing, when no seed had the ID of a cell of values. Seeds whose ID column is not the one the cells were built with (a column of that name from elsewhere, or the index of another tessellation) gave every location a cell that values has no row for, and each location took the value of the cell of its nearest scored row: on a layer of 107 cells, seeds numbered 1001 to 1107 filled all 120 locations asked for, and 18 of the values differed from those of the locations’ own cells. Seeds whose IDs are all NA did the same unless a seed outside the cell polygons of values took the cell it generates, and a values with no cell ID (no row, or every ID NA) gave every location the value NA. Each is now an error that names the argument to set: the seeds’ ID column, with how to set it from the tessellation, or values. The cells that seeds outside the polygons take count as their IDs, so points placed by hand outside the boundary, all NA in index, are still the seeds of their cells when values carries the polygons. One seed with a location and the ID of a cell of values is enough for the call to run, and a seed whose ID values has no row for still stands for a cell without a value.

  • cell_values_at(seeds = ) filled every location, with no error, when the seeds with the ID of a cell of values had no location. The check that some seed has the ID of a cell of values counted seeds with an empty point, or a coordinate that is not finite or lies beyond 1e150, though such a seed is the nearest seed of no location, and it read the coordinates only as given, so seeds that leave the globe once placed in the working CRS (metres given EPSG:4326, a latitude beyond 90) counted too. Seeds that kept their IDs and lost their points left every location without a cell, and so did one such seed with a cell’s ID beside seeds with NA IDs; beside seeds with other IDs it gave every location a cell that values has no row for. Each location then took the value of the cell of its nearest scored row: the seeds of a tessellation of 107 cells, every point emptied, filled all 120 locations asked for. Only a seed with a location, as given and in the working CRS, now counts, and when every seed with the ID of a cell has none the call stops with an error that says so; when they had a location as given, it names the working CRS and the CRS of seeds. A seed with a coordinate beyond 1e150 is no longer searched where a move between CRSs puts it (a northing of 1e200 in EPSG:32618 comes back finite in EPSG:32617). One seed with a location and the ID of a cell is still enough for the call to run. A cell whose ID only seeds without a location carry is now one no seed names, which step 3 offers to a seed with an NA ID outside the polygons: points placed by hand outside the boundary take their cells beside such a seed, where the locations in the cell it named were filled.

  • A row of newdata or points with a coordinate beyond 1e150 in another CRS than the working one was read where the move to that CRS put it. Such a coordinate stands for no location, but the bound was read only after the move, and a move can bring it back finite: a northing of 1e200 in EPSG:32616 lands at (87304, 5766268) in EPSG:32617, and one in EPSG:3857 at (5e5, 9997965). In cell_values_at() such a row of newdata took a cell, a value and a distance, where the help says it has NA in every column; a row of points was a scored location, which moved the spacing and so dist_ratio at every location. In summarize_by_cell(estimate = "pooled") such a row of points took part in the pooled columns and their record with no spatialkit_pool_rows_skipped warning. Such a row of points also took part in choosing how the other rows are read: in EPSG:4326 a longitude of 1e200 made summarize_by_cell() without a count record stop with an sf “invalid crs” error, and a latitude of 1e200 raised two sf warnings about the bounding box; in a layer without a CRS whose coordinates are lon/lat, one such row made every other row read as planar degrees, so that summarize_by_cell() recorded no CRS and cell_values_at() took the degrees for metres in the summary’s CRS, with no warning. The bound is now read on the coordinates as given, and again after the move, and the rows of points beyond it as given are emptied before the CRS is chosen: each such row gives what the same row with an empty point gives. Rows in the working CRS itself are read as before. The text of spatialkit_pool_rows_skipped, and its entry in ?summarize_by_cell, said such rows “have empty or non-finite coordinates”, which a row beyond 1e150 does not; they now read “no location (an empty point, or a coordinate that is not finite or lies beyond 1e150)”.

  • A layer of newdata, seeds or points that mixes XY and XYZ points stopped cell_values_at() and summarize_by_cell(estimate = "pooled") with a bare message from base R or sf, or was read at the wrong coordinates. sf reads a layer in the dimension of its first point, and rbind() of an XY and an XYZ layer builds such a layer without a word. With an XYZ point first, sf::st_coordinates() laid the values out of step, so that every later row was read at another row’s place, with only base R’s “data length is not a sub-multiple” warning: locations took another cell and distance, seeds another cell, and the pooled columns of every cell moved; in another CRS than the working one the call stopped with sf’s “OGR error”. With an XY point first the call stopped with base R’s “length of ‘dimnames’ [2] not equal to array extent”. The same held for a layer XYZ throughout whose features are not all points: the point taken on the surface of a POLYGON Z, and the empty point of an empty LINESTRING Z, are XY beside the POINT Z rows kept. These layers are now read in x and y: when a layer’s points, or the points taken from its other features, do not all have the same dimensions, Z and M are dropped from the copy read, and the call gives what the same rows in XY give. An XYM point is read as an XYZ point is. A layer of points in one dimension, XY or XYZ throughout, is read as before. Neither function returns these layers’ geometry, so the caller’s points keep their Z.

  • A layer that mixed XY and XYZ (or XYM) geometries was joined, measured and projected wrongly, depending on which row came first. sf reads a layer in the dimension of its first geometry: s2 drops Z and M only when the first geometry carries them, and GEOS and sf::st_transform() read an XYZ ring among XY rows as XY pairs. rbind() of an XY and an XYZ layer gives such a layer without a word. With a clean XYZ square in row 3 of six lon/lat squares, assign_features_to_polygons() left the point in it unassigned under the warning that it fell inside no polygon and counted three others as ties; an XYZ square whose ring repeats a vertex in x and y passed the validity test and misplaced its points, where the same square alone gets the spatialkit_cells_degenerate error; polygon features that mixed dimensions went to the wrong cell under the largest-overlap join; in a projected CRS the join stopped with GEOS’s “Points of LinearRing do not form a closed linestring”. summarize_by_cell(area = TRUE) gave the XYZ square 1.6e14 square metres for its 95 square km, and refused mixed projected cells as not measurable. ensure_projected() chose UTM zone 25 South for a layer in Missouri and returned the XYZ row as a ring of other points, and stopped with “OGR error” on points with an XYZ point first; harmonize_crs() did the same; both took such a layer in degrees without a CRS, a degree or less across, for planar coordinates, as their lon/lat test read its coordinates with sf::st_coordinates(), which stops on it; ensure_projected(purpose = "area") skipped its area distortion warning for such a layer in a projected CRS, as the distortion measured on it was NA; create_grid_polygons(), create_voronoi_polygons(), build_tessellation() and clip_target_for() stopped with GEOS’s message on such a boundary. Each geometry is now tested, and a layer that mixes dimensions is handed to sf without Z and M: both layers of the join, the cells whose areas and distortion summarize_by_cell() measures, the layer ensure_projected() chooses a projection from, and the builders’ boundary. The rows the join returns and the cells the summary returns keep the geometry they arrived with, Z and M included. ensure_projected() and harmonize_crs() return a transformed copy of a mixed layer in XY, with a warning of class spatialkit_zm_dropped, and so does the join for features without a CRS that are moved from lon/lat. A layer in one dimension, XY or XYZ throughout, is read and transformed as before, and so is a layer whose only geometries of another dimension than the first are empty and not points, which sf transforms with its Z.

  • A polygon layer without a CRS, in degrees and a degree or less across, was taken as planar when it held an empty polygon. The lon/lat test of ensure_projected() and harmonize_crs() reads the coordinates of such a layer to see whether they have the precision of decimal degrees; sf::st_coordinates() stops on a polygon layer with an empty polygon, so the test found no precision and the layer was not moved from lon/lat. The test now leaves empty geometries out.

  • coerce_to_points() stopped with a bare message from GEOS or sf, or returned points at the wrong place, on a polygon or line layer that mixed XY and XYZ (or XYM) geometries, and so did every function that reduces the caller’s layer to points first. sf hands GEOS and s2 every geometry of a layer in the dimension of its first, and rbind() of an XY and an XYZ layer gives such a layer without a word. On projected polygons the modes "auto", "centroid" and "point_on_surface" stopped with GEOS’s “ParseException: Unexpected EOF parsing WKB” or “Points of LinearRing do not form a closed linestring”; on lines "auto" and "line_midpoint" stopped with sf’s “OGR error” when the first line was XYZ, and gave a later XYZ line another midpoint in silence; on squares in degrees "centroid" put an XYZ square’s point 8,666 km from the square. prep_model_data(), and through it the fits, the cross-validations and predict() on newdata in the fit’s CRS, make_folds(), estimate_sac_range(), compare_models_cv() and select_features_forward(select_on = "split") stopped the same way. make_folds(), compare_models_cv() and select_features_forward(select_on = "split") also stopped with “OGR error” on a layer XYZ throughout that mixes POINT Z rows with POLYGON Z or LINESTRING Z rows, as the points taken from the polygons and lines are XY, and make_folds() stopped the same way on a point layer with an XYZ point first among XY points. coerce_to_points() now reads such a layer in x and y and returns XY points, with a warning of class spatialkit_zm_dropped that carries the rows with Z or M as rows. This includes a layer whose geometry types each have one dimension, such as XY polygons beside a POINT Z row: it was read right, and its points came back with Z on that row only. prep_model_data(), make_folds(), estimate_sac_range(), compare_models_cv() and select_features_forward(select_on = "split") read the layer in x and y with no warning, and give what the same rows in XY give. A layer in one dimension, XY or XYZ throughout, is read as before, and so is a layer whose only geometries of another dimension than the first are empty and not points. The mode "bbox_center" read each geometry’s box and gave the right points; it still does, with no warning.

  • coerce_to_points(mode = "auto") gave a MULTILINESTRING whose longest parts are of equal length the midpoint of the first of them in the feature’s part order, so the same geometry with its parts listed the other way round got a point 1 km away in a two-part example; congruent parts were also told apart by the last bits of their lengths, so the point moved with a shift of the origin. Among parts of equal greatest length, to one part in ten million, the midpoint lowest in x, then in y, is now taken, x values within one part in ten million of the diagonal of the midpoints’ bounding box counting as one: two congruent parts whose midpoints have one x, reached from other coordinates, differ in their last bits once the origin moves, and y now decides between them, so the point is the same at every origin. A feature with one longest part gets its midpoint as before. ?coerce_to_points states the rule.

The join and the cells are defined in x and y and M is read nowhere, so these layers are now read in x and y, with no warning, and give what the same rows in XY give. The rows assign_features_to_polygons() returns keep the geometry they arrived with, M included; features without a CRS in one dimension that are moved from lon/lat into the polygons’ CRS come back moved with sf::st_transform(), which keeps their M. A layer XY or XYZ throughout is read as before.

  • The smallest-area tie-break of assign_features_to_polygons() gave a feature to a polygon whose ring crosses itself as the smallest. GEOS measures such a ring as the signed sum of its lobes, which cancel: a bowtie whose two lobes cover 180,000 square metres measured 0, so a point inside a valid 100 m square and inside the bowtie went to the bowtie, without a warning, where the same bowtie repaired by the caller, or a valid polygon in its place, lost the tie. The largest-overlap join already repaired such polygons for its overlaps. The tie-break now checks the polygons it compares and measures the invalid ones on copies repaired with sf::st_make_valid(), with a warning in the words of the largest-overlap join’s; the polygons and features are returned as they arrived. Layers without ties, or whose tied polygons are valid, are assigned as before.

  • assign_features_to_polygons() on layers in longitude and latitude stopped with sf’s “package lwgeom required, please install it first” when sf::sf_use_s2() was FALSE. sf hands areas in degrees to lwgeom when s2 is off, and the package does not depend on lwgeom: the smallest-area tie-break stopped on a point in two polygons, and the largest-overlap join of polygon features stopped with “the largest-overlap join failed (package lwgeom required …). Pass largest = FALSE …”, whose advice stopped the same way. In degrees the largest-overlap join (its validity check, repair and overlaps) and the areas the tie-break compares now run on s2 whatever the session says, as the package’s other areas in degrees do, and give what they give with s2 on; the join by predicate keeps the session’s engine. The largest-overlap join no longer advises largest = FALSE for an error that the join by predicate meets too, such as a missing lwgeom. With s2 off, a polygon in a tie that s2 refuses even repaired (a bowtie in degrees) stops the call with the spatialkit_cells_degenerate error, which names it and the transform. With s2 off, the error of the largest-overlap join for a polygon s2 refuses offers largest = FALSE, whose join by predicate runs with GEOS, and these errors name s2 as the engine the package uses there, not as the one sf uses in the session.

  • cell_values_at() without seeds gave every location the value NA, marked filled, when values had no cell ID. A values whose ID column is all NA placed no location in a cell, so every location was filled from the cell of its nearest scored row, which values has no row for, and took NA; nothing was raised. The same values beside seeds was refused. It is now refused on both paths with the error the seeds’ path gave (“values has no cell ID (it has no row, or its ID column … is all NA)”), whatever the locations asked for. IDs that are NaN count as NA. A values of no rows, or one without polygons whose IDs are all NA, without seeds, refused before because it carries no polygons, gets that error too. A values with some IDs NA runs as before.

  • cell_values_at(seeds = ) gave a seed with an NA ID outside the polygons of values the first of several cells by the row order of values. Such a seed takes the cell no seed names whose inner point finds it as its nearest seed. When the inner points of several such cells found it, it took the first of them in the order of the rows of values, and every location nearest it took that cell’s value, not filled: one point placed by hand outside the boundary, passed alone as seeds, put all 120 locations of a layer of 107 cells in cell 1, and in cell 107 with the rows of values reversed. Such a seed generates at most one of those cells, and nothing says which, so it now keeps its NA ID: the locations nearest it have no cell and are filled, and a warning gives the count of such seeds. When no seed is then left with the ID of a cell of values, as for that lone point, the call stops with the error for seeds whose IDs are all NA; its text, with the polygons in values and without, now says when a seed outside the polygons is given its cell. A seed that the inner point of one such cell alone finds, such as a point placed by hand in the bend of a boundary that is not convex, takes that cell as before.

  • cell_values_at() refused seeds without a CRS beside points with one, with an error that did not say which CRS to set. For rows without a CRS whose coordinates look like longitude and latitude, get_voronoi_seeds() returns the seeds without a CRS, in degrees, and assign_features_to_polygons() returns the rows in the cells’ projected CRS, so on such rows cell_values_at() stopped on the seeds even once newdata was given its CRS. Such seeds are now read as build_tessellation() reads a boundary without a CRS, with a warning: beside points in a projected CRS, coordinates that look like longitude and latitude are taken as EPSG:4326 and transformed, and others are taken to be in the CRS of points, which the warning names; beside points in a geographic CRS, coordinates within the ranges of longitude and latitude are taken to be in it, and others are an error that names the CRS the summary measured in. newdata without a CRS beside points with one is still an error.

  • assign_features_to_polygons() stopped on cells returned in lon/lat with “duplicate vertex”. build_tessellation(crs = 4326) builds the cells in a projected CRS and transforms them. On gridded locations four centres can stand the same distance from one point, and two cells meet there at two corners that differ only by rounding, less than a nanometre apart; the transform puts them at one point, or at two that sf’s spherical engine (s2) cannot tell apart, and s2 refused the cell. Rows in lon/lat were joined on the sphere, so the join stopped: on 16 lattices at spacings of 1 to 1,000 m with rows in EPSG:4326, 27 of 32 paths stopped under the two kinds, and 3 of the 5 others put rows on an edge in another cell than the profile’s. Cells in lon/lat whose record says a profile scored them are now joined in the record’s projected CRS, where they were drawn: every row is in the cell the profile scored it in, a point on an edge goes to the cell of its nearest centre, and the summary’s check reads match on all 32. This holds for the cells s2 accepts too, so features that are not points get their cell from overlaps and areas measured in that CRS, and rows without a CRS, which also stopped, are joined there. cell_values_at() without seeds places locations on such cells there as well. Other cells in lon/lat are joined as before: cells without the record (from a count given as a number, or after a verb that drops attributes) and cells whose record says they are not the cells the profile scored (scored_cells = FALSE, such as the cells of centres refitted to every point). s2 can still refuse them, as it refuses sf::st_area() and sf::st_union() on such cells: transform them to a projected CRS first.

  • create_voronoi_polygons() and build_tessellation(method = "voronoi") handed on a seeds layer’s record of its count unchanged when the seeds were fewer or more than that count. The record survives row subsetting, so a selection’s 32 seeds cut down to 16 gave 16 cells whose record said they were the 32 cells the profile scored, and summarize_by_cell() warned that rows were dropped or moved between cells, by points outside every cell, a clipping boundary, a subset of the rows or another layer, when every row was assigned. Such seeds now carry the record with scored_cells = FALSE, as get_voronoi_seeds(method = "provided") marks them, so their cells are built as other seeds’ are and the summary reads “not checked: other cells were built from this count”. A selection’s seeds as they come are unchanged.

  • assign_features_to_polygons() stopped with s2’s bare message on polygons in lon/lat that s2 refuses. A join in longitude and latitude runs on the sphere, where s2 refuses a polygon with two corners it reads as one point, and the join stopped with “Loop 0 is not valid: Edge 20 is degenerate (duplicate vertex)”, which names neither the polygon nor a way on. Cells returned in lon/lat hold such corners on gridded locations, and the joins that do not run in the record’s CRS met them: s2 refuses 4 of the 133 k-means cells of a 30 by 20 lattice at 30 m returned in EPSG:4326, and the join of rows in degrees stopped once the cells had lost their record or their CRS; the cells of centres refitted to every point (scored_cells = FALSE) on a 50 by 40 lattice at 250 m stopped it the same way. The join by predicate now stops with an error of class spatialkit_cells_degenerate that gives the number and rows of the polygons s2 refuses (rows on the condition), quotes s2, names the cause and says to transform polygons_sf to a projected CRS, such as the one the cells were built in, where the join runs. Every refusal by s2 of a polygon of the layer gets this error, among them a hole that crosses its outer ring and two holes that share an edge, which also stopped with s2’s bare message. The largest-overlap join of polygon features still repairs the polygons s2 refuses, with its warning, and runs on most of them; on a polygon s2 refuses even after the repair (a hole that crosses its outer ring) it stops with the same error, where it advised largest = FALSE, which meets the same refusal. When the repair makes s2 accept a polygon and s2 then refuses a piece of its overlap with the other layer (a figure eight, repaired into two triangles that touch at a point), the join gave the same advice, and with s2 on the join by predicate then stopped on the polygon as it arrived; it now stops with the error that names that polygon and the transform. Whether s2 refuses such a piece follows the last bits of the vertices s2 computes for it, which differ between platforms and s2 versions: a figure eight pinched on the edge of two cells can give a piece that s2 refuses on macOS on arm64 and accepts on Linux on x86-64, and where s2 accepts the piece the join runs and gives each feature the polygon of its largest overlap. Where s2 refuses a polygon of either layer even after the repair, the error names that polygon, and not a polygon of the other layer that the repair made s2 accept. A polygon of features_sf that s2 refuses stopped the join by predicate with s2’s bare message, such as “Loop 0 is not valid: Edge 0 crosses edge 2” for a bowtie; it now stops with an error of class spatialkit_features_degenerate, with the fields of the cells’ class, that gives its rows, quotes s2 and says to transform features_sf to a projected CRS, and, where sf::st_make_valid() makes s2 accept the rows, that repairing them works too. Where s2 refuses polygons of both layers, the error for polygons_sf quotes each row’s own reason, where it quoted s2’s message for a feature as a cell’s, and says that s2 also refuses rows of features_sf (features_rows on the condition). cell_values_at() without seeds, which places its locations with this join, gives the error in its own words: it names values and the rows of values. Polygons s2 accepts are joined as before, and an error of another kind keeps its own message.

  • summarize_by_cell(area = TRUE) stopped without the cause on lon/lat cells that s2 refuses. The areas of lon/lat cells are s2’s, and s2 refuses a cell with two corners it reads as one point, which cells returned in lon/lat hold on gridded locations. When the area check measured such a cell, the request was refused because “the area distortion of cells_sf‘s CRS could not be measured”, which names neither the cell nor a way on; above 200 cells, when the check passed over it, the request ran through the summary and stopped at the cells’ areas with s2’s bare”Loop 0 is not valid: Edge 1 is degenerate (duplicate vertex)“. ?summarize_by_cell said the check passes by construction on lon/lat cells. Every cell’s area is now taken before any summary, and a cell s2 refuses stops the request with the error of class spatialkit_cells_degenerate that assign_features_to_polygons() gives: it gives the rows of cells_sf s2 refuses, names the cause and says to transform the cells to a projected CRS, such as the one they were built in or the equal-area one ensure_projected(purpose = "area") picks. Lon/lat cells s2 accepts get the density and attr(, "area_error") they got before, and with s2 off the request needs lwgeom as before.

  • coerce_to_points(mode = "centroid") and prep_model_data(pointize = "centroid") stopped with s2’s bare message on a polygon in longitude and latitude that s2 refuses. With s2 on, sf takes the centroids of a layer in degrees with s2, which refuses a ring with a vertex listed twice in a row, although GEOS accepts it, and the call stopped with “Loop 0 is not valid: Edge 1 is degenerate (duplicate vertex)”, naming neither the row nor a way on; a bowtie and a figure eight stopped it the same way. The same held for the rows other than LINESTRINGs under "line_midpoint", for collections under "auto", for the cv_*() and fit_*() functions that pass pointize = "centroid", and for the functions that reduce a layer they are given to points with "auto": make_folds(), fold_separation(), estimate_sac_range(), resolution_profile(), determine_optimal_levels(), cell_values_at(), summarize_by_cell() and select_features_forward() (the last wrapped the message in a plain error of its own). A polygon s2 refuses for a repeated vertex, on its own or inside a collection, now gets the centroid of the same ring without the repeat, whose points are unchanged. A polygon s2 refuses even then stops the call with an error of class spatialkit_features_degenerate that gives its rows (rows on the condition), quotes s2, and says to transform the layer to a projected CRS, or to pass another mode or pointize, or, in a function that takes neither, to reduce the layer to points first. The mode or pointize it offers runs on the rows it names: "auto" when each is a polygon or multipolygon, which "auto" reduces with a point on the surface, and "point_on_surface" when one is a collection, which "auto" takes the centroid of and refuses again. Each function raises it in its own name, naming its argument and that argument’s rows: prep_model_data(), compare_models_cv(), resolution_profile() and determine_optimal_levels() name data_sf, make_folds() points_sf or prediction_points, fold_separation() data_sf or prediction_points, estimate_sac_range() points_sf, cell_values_at() newdata or points, summarize_by_cell() assigned_points_sf and select_features_forward() train_sf, with the rows as passed. Layers s2 accepts get the centroids they got, and with s2 off the centroids are GEOS’s, as before, but for those of the next entry.

  • coerce_to_points() returned, without a word, a centroid far outside a polygon whose edges cross, in a projected CRS. GEOS, which takes the centroids in a projected CRS, without a CRS, and in degrees with s2 off, weights each part of a ring by its signed area. Where the edges of a ring cross (a bowtie), or a hole lies outside its shell, parts of the feature count with opposite signs: a bowtie 10 km across, one corner 1 m off symmetric, got a point over 33,000 km away, and the functions that reduce a layer to points ran on it. The transform that the refusal of the entry above names for such a bowtie in degrees led to that point. This held under "centroid", for the rows other than LINESTRINGs under "line_midpoint", and for collections under "auto". A centroid outside the bounding box of a feature GEOS reports invalid now stops the call with the error of class spatialkit_features_degenerate, which gives the rows (rows), quotes GEOS’s reason for each (reasons), carries site = "geos_centroid", and says to take a point on the surface or to repair the features with sf::st_make_valid(). The functions of the entry above, area_of_applicability() (train_sf or newdata) and predict_surface() (grid) raise it in their own name, naming their argument and its rows. A centroid inside the box is GEOS’s, as before, and so is every centroid of a valid feature.

  • The projection ensure_projected() chose for a layer in longitude and latitude moved, in silence, when s2 refused one of its polygons even after the repair. The centre that places the projection is the centroid of the layer’s union on the sphere. When s2 refused the layer and its repair (a bowtie, which s2’s repair leaves as it is), the centre fell back to the mean of every vertex of the layer, and nothing said so: on 100 one-degree squares, one of them drawn with 4,000 vertices, one bowtie moved the centre 4 degrees to that square, and the distance and area CRSs became an Albers CRS centred there, where the layer without the bowtie gets UTM zone 14 and a Lambert azimuthal CRS. The mean counted each ring’s closing vertex twice, so the same bowtie listed from each of its four corners gave four centres and four CRSs. The features s2 refuses are now repaired one by one (without their repeated vertices, then with crossing edges split), and the centre is taken over the features s2 then accepts; a log line names any feature s2 still refuses, which is left out. The vertex mean is used only when s2 accepts no feature, counts each closing vertex once, and is logged. Every function that projects a lon/lat layer through ensure_projected() reads this centre. Layers s2 accepts, or whose repair it accepts, get the centre and the CRS they got.

  • The distance score of a candidate projection put every feature that crosses 180 degrees on the far side of the globe when s2 refused one of them. Such a feature is scored at its centroid on the sphere, because GEOS reads it the long way round. The centroids of these features were taken in one call, and when s2 refused one of them (a vertex listed twice in a row) every one kept GEOS’s point: a box around Fiji with one vertex listed twice scored 25% in the Lambert azimuthal CRS chosen for it, where the same box without the repeat scores 0.02%, and crs_choice and the log reported that figure. They are now taken feature by feature: a feature s2 refuses for a repeated vertex gets the centroid of the same ring, one whose edges cross that of its rebuild with the crossing edges split, and only a feature s2 refuses after both keeps GEOS’s point. Features s2 accepts score as before.

  • Folds saved by spatialkit 2.0.0 were applied to other data in silence when that data held a lon/lat polygon s2 refuses. The cv_*() functions, area_of_applicability() and fold_separation() check that folds were built on the data they are given by retaking the location of the rows the folds recorded. A record saved by 2.0.0 (without kind) is retaken with the centroid sf takes in the session, and with s2 on a polygon s2 refuses stopped it; the check then passed without a word, so folds built on other data of the same size were applied. Such a record on such data can only have been taken with s2 off, and it is now retaken that way, so folds from other data are refused as they are with s2 off. When no location can be taken for the rows at all, the check is skipped with a log line that gives the cause, as it is when one side has a CRS and the other has none.

  • A grid laid in degrees (cellsize with a geographic crs) returned cells s2 refuses, and build_tessellation(method = "square") or "hex" stopped on them with s2’s bare message. With s2 on (the default) sf clips such a grid with s2, which writes some clipped cells with a corner listed twice in a row, or with two corners that differ by rounding (7e-15 degrees), which s2 reads as one point: on a 0.5 degree square at cellsize = 0.1, one of 25 square cells and three of 39 hexagons, and at cellsize = 0.05 seven of 137 hexagons; build_tessellation() stopped with “Loop 0 is not valid: Edge 5 is degenerate (duplicate vertex)”. sf::st_area() of the grid stopped the same way, and assign_features_to_polygons() gave a cause that speaks of seeds and of cells built in a projected CRS. create_grid_polygons() now returns such a cell without the repeat, and without a corner that lies within 1e-12 degrees of the one kept before it, which moves no corner and changes its area by rounding, and build_tessellation() runs on the grid; cells s2 accepts are returned as they were.
