    • area_of_applicability() with more training rows than normalizer_max_n, for the normaliser of the predictor index and of the location index. 1000 training rows at normalizer_max_n = 300 gave a normaliser of 1.018 as given and 1.155 reversed, and DI and the threshold with it; with a threshold supplied, the inside or outside call moved too.
    • gp_lengthscale_bounds() above max_n distinct locations, and the GP prior and basis that fit_bayesian_spatial_model() and cv_bayes() build from it. 1500 locations gave a lower bound of 675.7 as given and 684.0 reversed.
    • The GP pre-fit check of fit_bayesian_spatial_model() and cv_bayes() on more than 1500 rows, whose Moran’s I at the basis floor thins the rows at even steps. On 2400 rows, 10 row orders gave I from 0.031 to 0.061 at one floor, so the status, and the pre-fit message, was "below_floor_long_range" in 4 and "below_floor" in 6. The thinning still draws no random number.

    Each result is now the same for the input in any row order; under the cap nothing is drawn and the results are those of before. Above it the subsample is another one, so the figures differ from before for the rows as given.

  • kriging_adequacy() kept the last fold’s prediction for a location held out by several folds. Each location is kriged once, so a hand-built folds whose test sets shared rows wrote over a location’s prediction with each fold that held it out, and the cross-validation statistic moved with the order of the folds: 200 points with rows 1 to 50 in every test set gave a variance of the z-scores of 0.978 and 0.989 with the folds in the two orders. Such folds are now refused before anything is fitted, with an error that names the location’s row and the two folds, as area_of_applicability() refuses them. make_folds() results and vectors of fold labels never share a test row.

  • kriging_adequacy(folds =) refused a vector of fold labels with one per row of assigned_points_sf once a row was dropped for a missing response or no location. The labels were read against the rows kept, and the call stopped, after the variogram fit, with a message saying the labels must have one entry per row, which they had. A vector of labels is now read as every cv_*() reads one: one label per row of assigned_points_sf, the i-th for the i-th row, the labels of dropped rows unused. One label per row kept is read as before. A vector of any other length stops before anything is fitted, with an error that gives its length, the number of rows and, when rows were dropped, the number kept.

  • residual_morans_i() read its response, design and residuals at their origin and unit. It rebuilt the design and regressed the response on the raw columns to test whether the residuals are OLS residuals, and gave the same design to the residual moments. A predictor at 1e8 plus a spread of 1 was dropped by the QR, so the moments had rank 1, and a response at 1e8 left the rounding of the offset in the reference residuals. On 300 points with OLS residuals that are the same at every offset, null = "auto" used the randomisation null with nothing said (exact FALSE, z 28.24 where offset 0 gives 28.25), and null = "residual" logged that the residuals were not OLS residuals. The tolerance of that test was 1e-7 times max(sd(y), .Machine$double.eps), so for a response whose standard deviation is below about 1e-22 it passed residuals that are not OLS residuals. The test for residuals with no spread was an absolute floor on their sum of squares: residuals of real spread whose sum of squares was below .Machine$double.eps (a standard deviation of 1e-9 on 200 rows) were refused with the warning “degenerate weights or zero residual variance”, and compare_models() gave NA Moran’s I columns for them, while the residuals of an exact fit multiplied by 2^20 were scored. Now the response is taken about its centre and the predictors at an offset about theirs, as in the other OLS fits, and the moments read that design. Residuals pass as OLS residuals within 1e-7 of the response’s standard deviation, read at any size, of the OLS residuals about the centres or of those lm() gives on the raw columns where the raw design keeps the rank, or within the rounding a regression of the raw columns leaves, so a backend that regressed the raw response at an offset passes too, on any number of rows. Residuals are refused where they do not vary beyond the rounding of the response, or where they are the OLS residuals of an exact fit, the bound resolution_profile() and estimate_sac_range() read; the warning names that cause, and degenerate weights have their own. The sums are taken on the residuals divided by a power of two, so I, z and the p-value are the same in every unit. compare_models() and the residual check of fit_bayesian_spatial_model() read the same function. A fit whose columns show their spread, with residuals above the bound, gives the numbers it gave, except that the kurtosis, and through it the randomisation variance, can differ in the last bit: R takes the fourth power with pow(), which does not commute with the division. The rounding bound reads the offset the fit regressed the response at, so a GWR that fit_gwr_model() took about the response’s centre, at a working bandwidth with the response at 1e15, is no longer read as OLS: it took the residual null with exact TRUE where offset 0 gives the randomisation null.

  • The k-nearest-neighbour weights tied neighbour distances within 1e-9 map units on any layer. The weights behind residual_morans_i(), estimate_sac_range(), the Moran tests of determine_optimal_levels() and resolution_profile() and the range check of fit_bayesian_spatial_model() took two distances as one when they differed by less than 1e-9 of the coordinates’ size, and that size was floored at 1 map unit. A layer whose coordinates span less than about 1e-5 map units therefore got other neighbours than the same layer in metres, more of them as the unit shrank, up to every other point with equal weight: on 120 points in a 5 km square scaled by 2^-50, Moran’s I of the residuals was -0.008 with p 1 where the layer in metres gives 0.277, and estimate_sac_range() returned NA with “no spatial structure detected at the nearest-neighbour scale” where it finds a range. Ties now read the distances alone (see the next entry), so the weights, I, z, p and the range scale with the coordinates. compare_models() had the same floor where it checks that fits with an information criterion share their rows, on the coordinates of a layer with no CRS and on the response: rows whose coordinates differ by less than 1e-9 units, or responses that differ by less than 1e-10 (a response at 1e-12 and 1.5 times it), passed as the same, and the AICc or LOOIC column was kept. The check that folds passed to a cv_*() function, area_of_applicability(), fold_separation() or kriging_adequacy() were built on the data had the same floor on a layer with no CRS: folds built on other data whose rows sit less than 1e-9 units from this data’s rows were applied in silence. Both checks dropped the floor (their margin is now a part of the spread; see the entry on these checks at a large offset). The margin of one part in 1e10 of the coordinates, by which build_tessellation() and cell_values_at() read seeds as the centres a count record holds and assign_features_to_polygons() reads a point as on the edge between scored cells, had a floor of 1e-10 units: on a layer with no CRS whose centres are 1000 units apart and whose seeds lie 10 units from them, all scaled by 2^-40, the seeds were read as the centres, and the cells were drawn around the centres in place of the seeds. The margin is now one part in 1e10 of the coordinates in any unit, as the help of assign_features_to_polygons() says.

  • The k-nearest-neighbour weights moved with the origin of the coordinates. The weights behind residual_morans_i(), the residual Moran’s I of compare_models(), the structure test of estimate_sac_range() and sac_nugget(), the Moran tests of determine_optimal_levels(), resolution_profile() and select_resolution(criterion = "moran_z"), and the range check of fit_bayesian_spatial_model() took two neighbour distances as one when they differed by less than 1e-9 of the largest coordinate: 4 mm at a UTM northing, 1000 m at an offset of 1e12 and 1e6 m at 1e15. The same points moved by a whole number of map units therefore got other neighbours. On 80 points 2 km across, each point had 46 to 79 neighbours in place of 8 at an offset of 1e12; at 1e15 every point was every other point’s neighbour, Moran’s I was exactly -1 / (n - 1), and estimate_sac_range() returned NA with “no spatial structure detected at the nearest-neighbour scale”. Two distances are now tied when their squares are within one part in ten million of each other, the rule of the package’s other neighbour searches, with no term in the size of the coordinates. The weights, and every I, z and p read from them, are the same at any origin and in any unit wherever the doubles hold the coordinates to better than about one part in 1e8 of the distances between neighbours. A lattice ties as before. On a layer in UTM metres, distances less than 4 mm apart but more than that part apart no longer share a slot, and a point a few units in the last place from two co-located points no longer shares their slot at k = 1.

  • Ties lost to the rounding of coordinates far from their origin were read in silence. The neighbour searches tie two squared distances within one part in ten million of each other, which holds while the doubles hold the coordinates to about one part in 1e8 of the distances between neighbours. An 8 x 8 lattice at a spacing of 100.1 m moved by 1e11 is stored rounded to 1.5e-5 m, so its nominally tied neighbours are stored apart and which of them a row takes follows the rounding. The k-nearest-neighbour weights, the structure test of estimate_sac_range() (Moran’s I 0.4117 at 1e11 where the origin gives 0.4136), the density partition, the nearest other location of the pooling and of the short-lag semivariances, the k-means step of make_folds(method = "knndm") on large samples, the kriging neighbourhoods of kriging_adequacy() and the edge of a GWR’s boxcar window moved with the origin, with no warning (on a 10 x 10 lattice at 100.1 m, the fitted values of an adaptive boxcar GWR moved by up to 0.15 at 1e11). Each of these searches now compares the distance past a row’s tie with the rounding, and residual_morans_i(), estimate_sac_range(), determine_optimal_levels(), fit_bayesian_spatial_model(), resolution_profile(), select_resolution(), get_voronoi_seeds(), voronoi_seeds_kmeans(), build_tessellation(), make_folds(), summarize_by_cell(), kriging_adequacy(), fit_gwr_model(), predict() on its fit, cv_gwr(), gwr_model_selection() and cv_block_size_sweep() warn once, with class "spatialkit_xy_imprecise", where some neighbour distances lie past a tie by less than that rounding, naming the rounding, the distance and the remedy. A call that has already said, in that class, that its coordinates are rounded by more than a millionth of their extent says nothing more. Results do not change. A lattice whose ties hold at its offset (whole metres at 1e15) raises nothing; at 1e15, where the rounding is wider than the gaps between their distances, points off a lattice can raise it too. The nearest-row search of cell_values_at() and predict_surface() keeps a lattice’s ties at these offsets (its margin is at least four units in the last place of the largest coordinate) and says nothing.

  • The checks that folds and fits describe the same data passed other data at a large offset. On a layer with no CRS, the check that folds passed to a cv_*() function, area_of_applicability(), fold_separation() or kriging_adequacy() were built on the data, and the check by which compare_models() keeps AICc or LOOIC only for fits of the same rows, took two locations as one when they differed by less than 1e-9 of the largest coordinate, and compare_models() took two responses as one when they differed by less than 1e-10 of the largest response. At an offset of 1e12 that is 1000 units: folds built on a layer were applied to the same layer moved by 500 units, which offset 0 refuses, and a response near 1e12 and the same plus 50 were read as one response. The margins are now a part of the spread of the values plus eight units in the last place of their size, so they cover the rounding of the values and do not grow with the origin.

  • fit_gwr_model() read a predictor or a response at a large offset on the rounding of the offset. The global least-squares fit the GWR is read against was lm() on the raw columns, which drops a predictor whose spread is under about 1e-7 of its size (1e8 plus a spread of 1, a timestamp in seconds) as collinear with the intercept, in silence. On 300 points with a predictor of unit spread, info$global_ols and summary()’s line “Global least squares on the same rows” gave an AICc of 881.32 at offset 0 and 1364.41, that of the intercept alone, from 1e8. The local regressions divided a predictor by its standard deviation before they centred it, so from about 1e10 the slopes, fitted values and AICc moved with the predictor’s origin: at 1e15 the slopes by 2 percent and the AICc from 489.16 to 496.03. A response at 1e15 plus a spread of 1 was regressed on its raw values, which a double holds to an eighth: the residual sum of squares was 111.4 where the same values at 0 give 73.6, the bandwidth search chose 71 neighbours where it chose 41, and gwr_model_selection()’s table and the residuals residuals() and residual_morans_i() read were those of the same rounding. The collinearity survey centred a predictor at 1e15 about its rounded mean, so info$condition_index and the slope index cn_slopes of info$local_collinearity moved with its origin (a maximum cn_slopes of 2.05 where the same values at 0 give 2.15). A predictor whose centre is more than 1000 times its spread is now taken less its centre before the bandwidth search, the local regressions, the global fit and the collinearity survey, and so is a response whose raw values, or whose least-squares residuals on the predictors, lose their spread to rounding, as estimate_sac_range() takes it. The centres are added back only to the fitted values, the local intercepts, the intercept and fitted values of fit$engine$lm and predict()’s values, and predict() takes a new row’s predictors about the training centres. Residuals, slopes and their standard errors, AICc, the bandwidth chosen, the global fit, the condition indices of the slopes and the selection table are now those of the same values at 0, to rounding; fitted values and predictions of a response at 1e15 are in its units, to the eighth a double holds there, and residuals() is the centred response less the centred fitted values. model_metrics(), summary(), evaluate_insample(), compare_models(), cv_gwr(), cv_spatial() with a GWR learner and select_features_forward()’s score_holdout scored such a fit on its fitted values and predictions in the response’s units, which carry that eighth: on 300 points at 1e15 RMSE was 0.49555 where residuals() give 0.49543, cv_gwr()’s RMSE 0.65316 where the values at 0 give 0.65533, and R-squared was NA. They now score it on the response, the fitted values and the predictions less the centre, so RMSE, MAE and R-squared are those of the values at 0, and MAPE and SMAPE divide the same errors by the values in the response’s units. The predictions of a cross-validation whose fold fits took the response about a centre gain the columns y_centre, yhat_centred and y_train_mean_centred, which the pooled scores read; yhat stays in the response’s units. fit$engine$lm is solved on the centred columns and returned as the fit at the data’s origin, with the QR factor of the raw columns, so summary(), vcov(), confint() and predict() on it give the intercept at 0 and its standard error; with a predictor more than about 1e7 times its spread from 0, predict(se.fit = TRUE) on it stops with “singular matrix”. fit$engine$centres gives the centres. Every other predictor is fitted as it was, to the last bit (the next entry gives the response), and a predictor that is constant, or a linear combination of the others, is still left out of the global fit.

  • A GWR at a global window on a response at 1e8 or 1e10 failed residual_morans_i()’s check for OLS residuals. fit_gwr_model() took a response about its centre only where its raw values, or its least-squares residuals on the predictors, lose their spread to rounding, so 1e8 plus a spread of 1 was regressed on its raw values. The local solve’s residuals then carry the rounding of the offset, which grows with the rows. On 6000 rows with bandwidth = 6000, adaptive = TRUE and kernel = "boxcar", which is global OLS, the residuals missed the check at 1e8 and 1e10, and residual_morans_i() with null = "auto" used randomisation, with exact = FALSE and a z of 126.387931 where the same values at 0 give the residual null and 126.391564, in silence. A response at -1e8, and a model of the intercept alone, failed the same way. fit_gwr_model(), predict() and gwr_model_selection() now also take the response less its centre where that centre is more than 1000 times its spread, the gate a predictor already has. The global GWR then gives the OLS residuals, the residual null and the z of the values at 0 at any offset, and residuals() is the centred response less the centred fitted values. A response whose centre is within 1000 times its spread is fitted as it was, to the last bit.

  • select_features_forward()’s training-fold-mean baseline read the rounding of a response at a large offset. Where the learner cannot fit a model with no predictors (a forest, or a GWR fit_fn that refuses character(0)) and no null_fn is given, the baseline is the mean response of each fold’s training rows. It was scored on the response and those means in the response’s units, which a double holds at 1e15 to an eighth. On 300 points with a GWR learner the baseline’s RMSE was 2.4737792 at 1e15 and 2.4701674 at 1e12, where the same values at 0 give 2.4701727, so baseline$score, the step-0 rows of history and of fold_scores, which the “se” rule reads, and the figure in the message “the baseline is the training-fold mean” moved with the response’s origin (2.4521 at 1e15 against 2.4480 at 0), while every candidate set scored the same at both. The baseline is now scored on the response less a centre, with each fold’s training mean taken about the same centre: the centre of the GWR fit where a fold’s fit took the response about one, and otherwise, where a fold’s raw training response loses its spread to rounding, the centre estimate_sac_range() takes. Its RMSE and MAE are then those of the values at 0. Where no fold has a centre the baseline is scored as before, to the last bit, and cv_spatial() returns what it returned for every call.

  • fit_gwr_model() logged “predictor has near-zero variance; GWR may be unstable” for a predictor in small units. The test was a standard deviation under 100 times .Machine$double.eps, so a predictor of unit spread multiplied by 2^-46 had the note and the same predictor at 2^-40 did not, though the fit is the same at every scale. Where the standard deviation is under that floor, the column is now read again on its own scale, and the note is logged only for a column without spread beyond the rounding of its values.

  • The range check of fit_bayesian_spatial_model() before sampling read its Moran’s I tests at the origin of a column, and scored the rounding of an exact fit. The short-lag and floor-distance tests regressed the raw response on the raw predictors. A predictor at 1e8 plus a spread of 1 was dropped by the QR, and a response at 1e15 left the rounding of the offset in the residuals: on 600 points, the short-lag Moran’s I went from 0.770 to 0.177 with the predictor at 1e8 and to 0.023 (p 0.18) with the response at 1e15, and a layer whose range is below the basis floor went from “below_floor” to “below_floor_no_autocorrelation”. The only test for residuals without spread was a sum of squares of 0, so where estimate_sac_range() refused the layer as an exact fit of the response on predictor_vars, the check still computed Moran’s I on the rounding, and could log in the same line that the response “is autocorrelated at short range”. Now the predictors are fitted about their centres where the centre is more than 1,000 times the spread, as in the other OLS fits, and the response by the same rule; the moments read that design. A response whose residuals lose their spread through a trend is fitted again about its centre, as estimate_sac_range() fits it. Residuals within the rounding of an exact fit, the bound estimate_sac_range() and residual_morans_i() read, give no test ($info$gp_prefit$moran and moran_floor are NULL), and the log says nothing about autocorrelation. The sums are taken on the residuals divided by a power of two, so I, z and the p-value are the same in every unit. Every other layer gives the numbers it gave, to the last bit.

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model(standardize_predictors = TRUE) did not standardise a predictor in small units. A predictor’s scale was its standard deviation floored at .Machine$double.eps, so a predictor with a standard deviation below 2.2e-16 was handed to brms::brm() with a standard deviation of 0.063 (at 1.4e-17) down to 3.8e-6 (at 8.5e-22), while the slope prior is set for a predictor with a standard deviation of 1; the slope and its posterior depended on the predictor’s unit. The scales of the coordinates had the same floor. Now a predictor or a coordinate whose standard deviation is below .Machine$double.eps is read again: one with spread is scaled by its standard deviation, taken at any size. One without spread got a scale of .Machine$double.eps, which turned the rounding of a constant column into values of order 1; now a predictor without spread gets a scale of 1, and a coordinate axis without spread (a transect along the other axis) takes the other axis’s scale, so the basis’s resolution and the floor of the range check are those of the axis with extent. The scale used is stored in $info$predictor_scaling and $info$coord_scaling, and predict() reads it there. A predictor or a coordinate axis whose values differ only by their rounding was read as one without spread only while its standard deviation was below the floor: at 4.5e6 such a predictor was divided by a scale of 7.5e-10 and handed to brms::brm() with a standard deviation of 1, and a transect at x = 4.5e6 with jitter in the last bit of x got an x scale of 7.7e-10. Such a column is now read as without spread at any size. A predictor or a coordinate with spread whose standard deviation is at least .Machine$double.eps is scaled as before.

  • The print of a profile of one level read “1 levels” and “WSS rises at 0 step(s)”. Every default profile has one level. The print now reads “1 level”, and leaves out the count of steps the WSS curve rises at when fewer than two levels have a WSS, since there is no step between levels to count. A subset of a profile’s rows printed the count of the whole ladder; it now counts the steps between its own levels. plot() of a profile of one level has the subtitle “1 level of 133 cells” where it had “1 levels from 133 to 133 cells”.

  • Messages asked for FNN, which installs with spatialkit, and the work-limit errors printed two equal numbers. The texts that appear when FNN cannot be loaded (the work limits of the exact searches of resolution_profile(), summarize_by_cell() and cell_values_at(), the density kind’s log line, area_of_applicability(use_fnn = TRUE) and the weights of Moran’s z) said to install it, and spatialkit_moran_skipped said that it is not installed; they now say that it could not be loaded (and is to be reinstalled). The weights’ error asks for Matrix alone when FNN is loaded. The work and the limit are printed in full, with as many digits as tell them apart: a work 0.04 percent over the limit read “1e+10 … above the limit of 1e+10”. The fit guard of resolution_profile() named “the FNN package installed” in a way on; it now says that the random starts of the density kind need FNN only where FNN could not be loaded.

  • Texts of resolution_profile(), select_resolution(), summary() and the seeding functions that misstated the case. The note on a count that one mean matches said “within 2% of the optimum” also where one mean was lower; it says “is not above the optimum by more than 2%”, which is the rule. After Cp’s note, the note of a variogram that found no structure was pasted in lower case with its close said twice; it is a sentence of its own. At the support ceiling the hint said to lower min_cell_n, which moves every level of the ladder; it names levels that run past the count. A selection by size called the default 4.5 “asked”, a selection on one level read “(1 of 1 levels)”, the summary of one level “(133 to 133 cells)” and a profile of one start “1 k-means++ restarts”. summary() said that one cell does as well where the cells beat one cell and only the F test (or, for cp, the profile’s variogram) did not show structure; it now says which, and the result then carries attr(, "not_identified"). On a constant response the warning left out loo, loo_se and own_weight, which are NA too, and summary() stopped with an error that named neither the constant response nor loo; both now name them. The print of a profile whose nugget is at the fit’s lower bound, with no level to take a noise variance from, marks the nugget and says that cp is NA at every level, as the warning does. The sizes of a ladder held for the same reason raise one spatialkit_size_not_reached (Breaking changes has the fields). The numbers of one printed line or note share one notation, where “90200000 (one cell for the layer: 1.09e+08)” mixed two, and the summary’s closing line reads “every pick is 60 cells” where it read “picks span 60 to 60 cells (1.0x)”. voronoi_seeds_kmeans() and voronoi_seeds_random() refuse the NA of determine_optimal_levels() with the note get_voronoi_seeds() gives, which names on_no_elbow.

  • Texts of summarize_by_cell(), cell_values_at() and assign_features_to_polygons() that misstated the case. The no-structure warning said of predictors that a map of their pooled values looks smooth “not because the response varies smoothly”; it says “the column” or “the columns” unless the response alone is named. cell_values_at() on a logical, factor or character column asked for a summary that summarize_by_cell(), which summarises numeric columns only, cannot make; it says how to convert the column, and for a factor that as.numeric() gives the level codes, not the labels. Features with empty geometry were said to fall outside the polygons, with advice on their cover or the CRS; the warning counts them and says that they have no location to assign.

  • Texts of the folds, the variogram, the seeding, the fits and kriging that misstated the case. make_folds(auto_range = TRUE) with a block_size said that the range was used as the minimum block size, where the block_size given is; it says so, with the grid of blocks that gives, and ?select_features_forward no longer calls block_size a floor under the range. On one row make_folds(method = "random_kfold") wrote “1 folds” and offered fewer folds. get_voronoi_seeds(method = "random") or "provided", given a density setting under the k-means kind, said that the density kind would read it; it says that the method does not. model_metrics(se.fit = TRUE) on a fit that is not Bayesian pointed to cv_bayes(). The rejected_reason of a variogram with fewer than three lag bins holding pairs said “(singular fits)” (Breaking changes has the new text). detrend = "reml" without nlme said that the fit did not converge; it says that it was not fitted, and why (on fewer than 30 locations no fit is tried: see the entry on the floor of 30 locations). kriging_adequacy()’s print gave a pure nugget a gain with no word on it; it says that there the gain is that of averaging the locations a cell is kriged from (kr_n_used), its own among them, over averaging its own alone.

  • make_folds() advised fold counts that give the same folds or none, and kNNDM warned of folds it then refused to build. Where it cut k to the number of rows ("random_kfold", "knndm") or of groups ("leave_location_out"), the spatialkit_k_reduced warning advised k <= that number, which gives the same one-per-fold folds: 5 rows and k = 10 said “pass k <= 5”. It now names one fewer (“pass k <= 4”), and with 2 rows or 2 groups, where no smaller k exists, it gives no advice. Under "knndm" it names the range from the smallest k that min_train allows: 8 rows, k = 10 and min_train = 0.85 say “pass k = 7 for fewer, larger folds (min_train = 0.85 needs k >= 7)”, and where no k below the number of rows meets min_train it gives no advice. make_folds(method = "knndm") with more folds than rows and a min_train above 1 - 1/n warned “returning 8 folds” and then stopped with an error that ended “Use min_train <= 0.875, or more folds.”, though no more folds were possible. It now tests min_train before it warns, so such a call stops with the error alone; the error names the k asked for and the rows it was cut to, and offers more folds only where one fold per row would meet min_train (“Use min_train <= 0.875.” otherwise). The folds returned, k and the condition’s fields are unchanged.

  • Cp took a nugget at the fit’s lower bound as its noise variance, and one that the closest pairs of points contradict. resolution_profile() read Cp’s noise variance off the variogram’s nugget, and a nugget of 0 (or of at most 1e-4 of the sill), which estimate_sac_range() marks as nugget_at_bound since it is the bound and not an estimate, left Cp no penalty: it fell with every finer level to the ceiling whatever the field, with an unclassed warning. Such a nugget is no longer taken: Cp’s noise variance comes from the finest level whose cells hold two scored rows on average, as when the variogram gives no nugget, and the range still serves reliability. Whatever its source, the noise variance is now held to the semivariance of nearest-neighbour pairs the variogram carries (attr(sac, "short_lag_semivariance")), which bounds a nugget from above: a nugget or a residual mean square above it is replaced by it. attr(, "cp_noise")$source names the source used, "short-lag semivariance" among them, and under the hold the record adds cap, the semivariance, and uncapped, the source, value and level it replaced; the print’s variogram line says which. The cp column, its value at one cell and Cp’s count change wherever either applies. A profile on a ladder of sizes under sac = "auto" fits no variogram and is unchanged.

  • On gridded locations the nearest-neighbour pairs of estimate_sac_range() depended on whether FNN could be loaded. Each location is paired with its nearest other location, and on a lattice two to four are equally near. FNN’s kd-tree and the package’s own search took different ones, so short_lag_pairs and short_lag_semivariance, and with them Cp’s noise variance where that semivariance holds it, the cp column and Cp at one cell, differed between a session with FNN and one without (on a 12 x 12 lattice, 80 pairs against 143), and moved with the unit of the coordinates. Of several locations whose squared distances agree to within one part in ten million, the pair now takes the one with the lower x coordinate, then the lower y, with or without FNN, in any order of the rows and in any unit or origin. On a square lattice that pairs almost every location with its neighbour along x, so the semivariance measures the field along x. Where the ties are exact, as on a lattice in whole metres, that is the pick the search without FNN made, so on gridded layers a session with FNN gets other pairs and other cp values than before, and a session without FNN does where rounding had broken the ties. Layers on which each location’s nearest other location is nearer than the next by more than that part in squared distance are unchanged.

  • The two variogram warnings of resolution_profile() had no class. The warning that the variogram gives no usable range now has class spatialkit_variogram_unusable (fields reason, converged, nugget, nugget_used), and the warning on where Cp’s noise variance came from has class spatialkit_cp_noise (fields source, value, level, cap, uncapped_source, uncapped_value), so a script can catch each by its class. The warning that the nugget is 0 is no longer raised, since Cp does not take such a nugget: spatialkit_cp_noise says where its noise variance came from instead. Points dropped and a variogram of another variable are still warned about without a class.

  • A count chosen by cp carried no record of how it was set. On a profile without an estimate (one with predictor_vars or a logical response, or one built with estimate = NULL), select_resolution(criterion = "cp") returned no count_rule, so summarize_by_cell(estimate = "pooled"), the default, pooled on cells whose count was chosen for plain means and said nothing. A cp selection now carries the record (estimate = "mean", no scored list), and so do its seeds, the cells built on them and the assigned layer, and a summary of pooled values on them raises spatialkit_estimate_mismatch. The selection gains count_rule and nothing else. A profile without an estimate passed straight as the count is read by cp and carries it too. Selections by reliability, elbow and moran_z off such a profile still carry none.

  • The seeds of a profile without an estimate fitted to a subsample were the subsample’s centres. On a ladder of counts the centres are fitted to sample_n (1,500) points, and select_resolution() handed the chosen level’s centres on as they were, so on a larger layer the cells built on them were fitted to a few rows each, far from the cells a fit to every point gives (their within-cell sum of squares over every point is higher). Such a profile now keeps every point’s coordinates (attr(, "refit_rows")), and select_resolution() refits the level it chooses to every point before its seeds are handed on: the kind’s own iteration (Hartigan and Wong’s for "kmeans", Lloyd’s on every point’s density weights for "density") from the centres scored, with the profile’s iteration limit and no random draw; where Hartigan and Wong’s algorithm refuses the centres, Lloyd’s iteration with every weight one runs in its place, with a log line. The seeds carry attr(, "refit") (rows, subsample, kind, iter, iter_max, converged, wss_scored, wss), the seeding functions hand them on, and the selection’s print says so. The count is still the one the subsample gave, and the cells are not the ones scored: the record on the seeds says scored_cells = FALSE. The refit costs one fit of that level to every point; summary() and plot() of a profile, and build_tessellation() given a profile as the count of a lattice, refit nothing, and a refit that would pass the work limits of a profile’s own fits is not run (a logged warning says so), and a profile saved by an earlier version, which keeps no coordinates, is not refitted (a log line says so). The centres the profile scored are attr(profile, "centres")[[as.character(sel$best)]]. A profile with an estimate is not refitted: it scores the estimate on every row of the layer in the cells of the centres fitted to the subsample, so those centres are its seeds, and summarize_by_cell() checks the cells built on them against its record.

  • The print of a profile fitted to a subsample called density cells “k-means fitted to a subsample”. The header now names the kind: “density-weighted k-means fitted to a subsample of 1500” for the density kind, the default, and “k-means fitted to a subsample of 1500” for partition = "kmeans".

  • resolution_profile(select_on = "split") returned a loo read off no row, with nothing said, when no row of the selection half had a response. The estimate is scored on the selection half, and the check that estimate has rows to read is made on the layer, so a layer whose rows with a response all lay in the estimation half passed it, under a named estimate and under "auto", which became "pooled". loo and the estimate’s other columns are still NA at every level, and a warning of class spatialkit_no_scored_rows now gives the reason; the condition carries reason, n, selection, n_response and column. The profile’s print says “loo NA: no row of the selection half has a response” where it said “fewer than two rows”, and so does the print of the count record, which read “in NA cells”. select_resolution(criterion = "loo"), the criterion a profile of plain means is read by, stops with the same reason where it said that loo needs a level at which some cell holds two rows with a response, and summary() of the profile, whose error said that “cp needs a response”, gives it too. No number changes.

  • resolution_profile(select_on = "split") without an estimate returned rss, cp, moran_i and moran_z NA at every level, with nothing said, when no row of the selection half had a response. The warning of class spatialkit_no_scored_rows, which gave the reason only with an estimate, is now raised without one too, and with predictor_vars it counts the rows with a response and every predictor. It is not raised when no row of the layer has a response. The split the profile carries records the rows of the selection half with a response (n_response). summary() of the profile, which said that “cp needs a response”, and select_resolution(criterion = "cp") and "moran_z", and "auto" where it reads cp, which said what each criterion needs, now give the reason, with or without an estimate. On a size ladder that fitted no variogram, "cp", and "auto" where it reads cp, give the size ladder’s reason, as before. No number changes.

  • The warnings of make_folds(method = "block_kfold") on blocks smaller than the autocorrelation range said “Spatial CV may leak correlated information across folds”. That read blocks below the range as a defect whatever the map. A cross-validated error is the error at the distance the folds put between the held-out points and their training data, and it reads low only for predictions made farther from the data than that. The five warnings now say so, name fold_separation(prediction_points = ) as the comparison, and say that wider blocks give the error farther from the data before their advice on the block size, which is unchanged. The subtitles of plot_folds() and of plot() on a cv_block_size_sweep() result no longer say that blocks below the range leak, and the sweep’s caption and progress message no longer call random folds “the leaky reference”. When no range can be estimated (no gstat, or fewer than 30 points), the line make_folds() logs says that the check of the blocks against the range is skipped, not a “leakage check”.

  • Three run-time texts said which way an error errs without saying where the model will predict. print() on an rf_fit said the out-of-bag error “is optimistic under spatial autocorrelation”; the caution fit_rf_model(include_coords = TRUE) logs said the out-of-bag error and random cross-validation “overstate its accuracy”; and the caution select_features_forward(method = "random_kfold") logs said random inner folds “leak spatial autocorrelation” and that a blocked outer loop reports “honest-looking numbers for a dishonestly chosen feature set”. They now read as ?fit_rf_model and ?select_features_forward do: the out-of-bag error and random folds are the error of predicting among the samples, which is the error of a map over an area the samples cover evenly and reads low for predictions made farther from the data, so a map that predicts farther is scored with cv_rf() on folds at its distances; random inner folds choose the variables that predict best among the samples, and a blocked outer loop scores the chosen set at the blocks’ distance, for which it was not chosen. A forest with no row out of bag (replace = FALSE, sample_fraction = 1) has no out-of-bag error, and its print no longer describes one: it says to score the forest with cv_rf() on folds at the distances the map will predict at. No result changes.

  • The spatialkit_cells_differ warning named a cause the tie rule removed. With what = "loo" (the same rows in the same number of cells, another leave-one-out error) it said that rows exactly on a boundary between two cells (gridded locations) can be assigned to the other cell. assign_features_to_polygons() gives such a row the cell the profile scored it in on the cells the profile scored, kept in the CRS it measured the rows in and carrying the record of their count, for rows that have a CRS exactly when the record names one. The warning now names the cases that remain: rows the polygons alone placed (rows without a CRS beside a count record that names one or the reverse, rows assigned to cells without their count record, such as cells read back from a file, and rows given their cells by another join), cells built in, or transformed to, another CRS than the one the profile measured the rows in, cells that are not the Voronoi cells of the centres the profile scored (seeds moved, cells edited), and coordinates that reached that CRS by another transformation. ?summarize_by_cell names the same cases. No result changes.

  • coerce_to_points() crashed R on an empty line feature. sf’s st_cast() turns an empty MULTILINESTRING into one empty LINESTRING, not zero parts, and st_line_sample() on it segfaulted and took the session with it. A null geometry in a line layer loads exactly like this from a GeoPackage or a shapefile, and prep_model_data(), every cv_*() function and fold_separation() go through this path. GEOS’s st_point_on_surface() crashed the same way on a line feature holding an empty part beside real ones, which ensure_projected() reached on ordinary lon/lat input. Empty parts are now removed before either call, and an empty feature becomes an empty POINT in its own row, which prep_model_data() and make_folds() drop like any empty geometry. An empty LINESTRING used to raise an error; it now gives an empty POINT like every other geometry type.

  • cv_gwr(parallel = n) hung forever once a GWR had been fitted in the session. GWmodel is built with OpenMP, and GNU libgomp is not fork-safe: after fit_gwr_model(), a sequential cv_gwr() or a bare GWmodel::bw.gwr(), the forked mclapply() workers blocked on a futex and never returned, with no timeout. That is the ordinary fit-then-validate order on Linux. cv_gwr() now runs its folds one after another whenever parallel would fork, and says so in a warning. This gives up the speed-up parallel folds had in a fresh session; the other cv_*() functions still fork, since ranger does not use libgomp. A cv_spatial() fit_fn that calls GWmodel can still hang with parallel, which its help page now says.

  • When some folds failed, overall quietly left them out. A partial failure was only logged, so overall pooled the surviving folds with no R condition, and the folds that fail are usually the hardest to predict (a region or a factor level no training fold covers). cv_gwr(), cv_bayes(), cv_spatial() and cv_rf() now warn, naming each failed fold and how many rows overall covers. Folds dropped before fitting are already warned about and are not counted twice.

  • select_features_forward() could pick a variable for making folds fail. Each candidate was scored on whatever rows its CV run predicted, so a set whose fit failed on a fold (a factor level found in one block, an ordinary case under block folds) was scored on fewer, easier rows. A pure-noise factor beat the true driver: RMSE 2.35 on 192 rows against 2.63 on 250, although the driver scored 1.73 on those same 192 rows. Every candidate is now scored on one fixed row set (the rows the null model predicts, or, with no null model, the rows the step-1 sets predict), a set that leaves any of them unpredicted scores NA with a warning, and history gains n_pred.

  • compare_models_cv() ranked models scored on different rows. Shared folds guarantee the same splits, not the same scored rows: when one backend lost a fold or returned NA predictions its overall row pooled a subset, and the help page called the columns comparable. A fixed-bandwidth GWR scored on 158 of 200 rows ranked above a random forest scored on all 200, although the forest was 45 percent better on the 158 rows both predicted. When the predicted row sets differ, every model is now rescored on the rows all of them predicted, with a warning, overall carries n_pred, and the all-rows numbers stay in attr(overall, "all_rows"). The per-fold table and the Bayesian coverage columns are not rescored.

  • determine_optimal_levels() read an elbow into points that have none. The elbow was the level furthest below the chord of the WSS curve on linear axes. For points with no cluster structure WSS falls like c / k, and the furthest point below that chord is exactly sqrt(a * b) for a ladder from a to b, so the answer was set by the ladder’s ends: 1,500 uniform points gave 4, 4, 7, 9 and 13 for max_levels of 12, 20, 40, 80 and 160. At the default max_levels = 12 it also missed well-separated clusters (four clusters came back as 3). The elbow is now read on log-log axes, where c / k is a straight line, and counts only when the curve sags clearly below it. Two, three, four, five, eight and ten well-separated clusters are now recovered at the default on every seed tried (six came back as five on one seed in five). With no elbow the function returns NA (see Breaking changes), and under on_no_elbow = "warn" its linear-axis answer, each with a warning that the ladder chose that answer; build_tessellation() and get_voronoi_seeds() refuse a geometry-only resolution_profile() with no elbow instead of drawing a count from it. A ladder of two levels (max_levels of 1 or 2, or three points) has no line to test. The warning now says the ladder is too short to read an elbow from and names what ended it. It used to say the curve fell in a straight line “as it does for points with no cluster structure”, which two clusters 90 m apart at max_levels = 2 were told.

  • One invalid polygon changed the assignment rule for the whole layer. assign_features_to_polygons() wrapped st_join(largest = TRUE) in a retry without largest on any error. The comment blamed a predicate that cannot take largest, but sf never calls the predicate on that path; the retry fired when GEOS threw on an invalid ring, and every straddling feature was then assigned by tie_break instead: 95 of 200 buffered parcels changed cell, and a polygon 91 percent inside one cell went to its neighbour, with no warning. Invalid features and cells are now repaired with sf::st_make_valid() for the join only, with a warning counting them, and a join that still fails stops and names largest = FALSE.

  • Lon/lat polygons were assigned to projected cells on bent cell edges. assign_features_to_polygons() moved the cells into the features’ CRS, so lon/lat features pulled the package’s own projected cells into lon/lat, and with s2 the largest-overlap join failed and fell into the silent retry above: 55 of North Carolina’s 100 counties went to a cell other than their largest overlap on a 36-cell grid. The join now runs in the cells’ CRS whenever it is projected, and the features come back with the geometry they arrived with. Lon/lat points near a cell edge can change cell as a result; they now agree with a join done in the projected CRS.

  • build_tessellation(method = "triangles") dropped most points at UTM coordinates. qhull lifts each point onto x^2 + y^2, and at projected magnitudes (a northing near 5e6) the lift had no precision left to separate points a few metres apart, so they never became vertices: 200 points over 100 m gave 26 triangles instead of 386, and the help page’s own example lost 8 of its 20 points. The points are now centred before triangulation. Triangles that were already right are the same triangles, but qhull returns them in a different order, so triangle cell_id values change.

  • Data around a pole were projected to Web Mercator. A layer spanning more than 180 degrees of longitude with no gap was treated as global coverage. Antarctic stations came out with worst-case distance errors near 20,000 percent (the South Pole at y = -2.4e8 m), and Voronoi cells put 9.5 percent of Arctic locations in a station’s cell that was not their nearest. A layer that lies wholly on one side of the equator now gets a Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection centred on its pole whenever that measures a smaller distance error than the global fallback: about 2 percent on the same stations.

  • GWR mixed elevation into its distances. prep_model_data() kept the Z (and M) coordinate of POINT Z input, which GPS layers and st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y", "z")) produce. predict.gwr_fit() then handed GWmodel three coordinate columns, which it reshaped into two, scrambling the prediction locations with no warning; gwr_model_selection() ranked models on 3-D distances; and fit_gwr_model() and cv_gwr() failed. Z and M are now dropped in prep_model_data() and again where a GWR takes its coordinates.

  • predict.gwr_fit() lost every prediction to one bad location. It went through GWmodel::gwr.predict(), which returns nothing for any row if one location’s window is empty or singular, so fixed-bandwidth block CV failed every fold. It also never assigns its distance matrix once training and new rows together exceed 10,000 (a 100 by 100 prediction grid came back all NA), and it built the full training hat matrix for a variance it then discarded, which is cubic in the training size. Predictions now come from the package’s own local regressions, one per new location, and only a location with no estimable prediction is NA, with a warning counting them.

  • On brms 2.17 to 2.22, one far-off row moved every Bayesian prediction in the call. brms rebuilt the Hilbert-space GP’s boundary from the rows being predicted, and the package’s padding rows could only widen it, so a single row outside the training envelope changed the basis for every row, interior ones included: a 40 by 40 grid padded 15 percent moved the in-bbox cells by a mean of 22 percent of the surface’s standard deviation, and predict_surface() depended on chunk_size. On those versions the GP term’s boundary factor is now rescaled per call so the boundary stays at its fitted value, and a row beyond the boundary, where the basis means nothing, is NA with a warning. brms 2.23 stores the boundary itself; there only the NA rule applies. The help page no longer says the boundary “has to grow”.

  • A bayesian_fit’s cached fitted values could come from another model. The cache lives in an environment, so it is shared by every copy of a fit, and the entry was stamped with the row count and a digest of the training data only. Two fits over the same data hash identically however different their engines are, so refit <- fit; refit$engine <- <re-estimated> made fitted(), residuals(), model_metrics() and summary() on either object return the other’s numbers — and clear_fitted_cache(), which the help page offers for exactly this case, could not fix it, because clearing through one copy cleared the one shared entry and the next call re-wrote it. The entry now carries the environment rstan and brms create for each sampling run (@.MISC on the stanfit), which tells engines apart as well as the engine itself does and is written once, and is used only for the engine it came from (identical(), which settles the common case by pointer, so nothing is slower and no memory is held that the fit did not already hold, in a session or on disk). A stale entry is no longer deleted on a miss either: the fit that wrote it still wants it. new_spatial_fit() now always builds a fresh cache rather than adopting one that arrived in info, and summary() no longer carries .cache at all — a summary was not a value snapshot (its contents changed when anyone later called fitted() on the fit), clear_fitted_cache() on a summary emptied the fit’s cache, and saveRDS() on one serialised an environment holding the full n-vector.

  • Every CRPS was NA above 46,340 posterior draws. .crps_energy() formed its weights with m * m, where m is nrow(draws) and therefore an integer, so the product overflowed and took CRPS, mean_CRPS and the whole predictive_coverage summary to NA behind one "NAs produced by integer overflow" warning. 48,000 draws is an ordinary cv_bayes(fit_args = list(chains = 4, iter = 13000)) run. The arithmetic is now done in double precision; the values it produces were, and remain, exact against the closed-form Gaussian CRPS.

  • Fold numbers depended on the machine’s collation. Character fold labels are turned into a factor, whose levels as.factor() sorts under LC_COLLATE, and a fold’s number is its level’s position. Labels differing only in case or punctuation — "north" and "North" — therefore landed in a different order under C than under en_US, so fold_metrics$fold, predictions$fold and fold_status$fold named different groups on different machines from the same data and the same seed. The partition was never affected, so pooled scores were right. Character levels are now sorted with method = "radix", which is always C collation, making the numbering a property of the labels alone. The C order applies to character labels only: numeric labels are numbered in numeric order, as in 2.0.0, and a factor by its own level order (an earlier development build sorted numbers as strings too, so with ten or more numeric labels fold 2 was the user’s label 10). area_of_applicability() given a vector of fold labels now numbers them by the same rule; it sorted character labels with as.factor() under the session’s collation, so a message could name a different fold from the one cv_*() named for the same label. Its partition and threshold were never affected.

  • residual_morans_i(k = ) silently answered a different question. k reached the weight builder unvalidated, where min() collapses a vector: k = c(4, 8) built the k = 4 matrix and returned a statistic for neighbours the caller never asked for, with no condition raised, and k = NA aborted on "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed". k is now checked. Two neighbouring gaps are closed with it: a user-supplied weights matrix holding any NA, NaN or Inf is refused by name instead of aborting inside a guard after a log line reading "row sums range from NA to NA", and a row whose geometry is empty is now dropped with a count, as make_folds() and estimate_sac_range() already do — its residual is perfectly finite, so it used to survive into FNN::get.knn() and abort with "Data include NAs".

  • A scalar argument that reaches as.integer() is validated. Seven exported functions took a count or a distance and passed it straight into as.integer() or an if () test, where NA, Inf, a length-2 vector or any value above .Machine$integer.max aborts with "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed" or "'length = 2' in coercion to 'logical(1)'" — errors that name nothing the caller passed. fit_gwr_model(bandwidth = ) under adaptive = TRUE, predict_surface(chunk_size = ) (Inf being the natural way to ask for one chunk), voronoi_seeds_kmeans(k = ), voronoi_seeds_random(k = ) and the count resolved by build_tessellation() / get_voronoi_seeds() now report the argument and the bound. voronoi_seeds_kmeans(k = 0) and a negative k used to return one seed in silence, which “at most k” does not describe.

  • expand was ignored rather than refused. clip_target_for(expand = c(0.05, 0.05)) returned a clip target byte-identical to expand = 0 with no condition raised, and create_voronoi_polygons() did the same for a non-numeric expand, because both tested is.numeric(expand) && expand > 0 and short-circuited to FALSE. A malformed expand is now an error naming the argument; the same values on a degenerate bounding box used to abort inside the expansion helper instead.

  • summarize_by_cell(deff = "variogram") aborted when given no value column. With neither response_var nor predictor_vars the internal primary column is NULL by design, and df[[NULL]] raised "attempt to select less than one element in get1index". The variogram design effect is a function of the cell’s coordinates and the fitted correlation, not of any column’s values, so every point in the cell now counts and the call returns its counts and cell_weight as documented.

  • compare_models() aborted on a list holding no spatial_fit. evaluate_insample() warns and skips a non-fit, and returned NULL when every element was skipped (it is now an error, below); the NULL then became a bare list and seq_len(nrow(NULL)) raised "argument must be coercible to non-negative integer". It now says which argument is wrong and what belongs there.

  • fit_rf_model(include_coords = TRUE)’s caveat said “once per session” and was not. .log_warn_once() records the key in a package-level environment, and under cv_rf(parallel = ) that write happens inside a forked worker and dies with it: the paragraph printed once per worker, the parent’s registry stayed empty, and the next sequential fit printed it again. cv_rf() now raises it in the parent before dispatching any fold, so each worker inherits the already-warned flag and stays quiet. Measured on two workers: three occurrences before, one after.

  • The grid cache’s order registry outlived the environments it described. Insertion order is kept in a package-level environment keyed by the cache environment’s printed address, and clear_grid_cache() removes only the entry for the environment it is handed. Passing a fresh cache_env per call therefore left one permanent character vector per call, for environments that had since been garbage-collected and could no longer be named. A finalizer now removes an entry with its environment.

  • plot(fit, type = "variogram") no longer runs its subtitle off the edge of the figure. ggplot2 clips a label that is wider than the plot instead of wrapping it, and the sentence saying why no range was identified is up to 150 characters, so on a six-inch figure it was cut mid-word. Labels built from a fit’s own numbers are now wrapped at draw time.

  • ensure_stable_poly_id() could not give IDs to a tessellation this package had just built. It repaired the geometry in the layer’s own CRS and then transformed it to the sort CRS, but validity is a property of the geometry in the CRS it is measured in: two vertices a centimetre apart in a projected CRS can land on one longitude and latitude, and s2 calls the ring degenerate. On a clipped hex tessellation of North Carolina, 2 of 18 cells that are valid projected are invalid once transformed, and st_centroid() on one of them aborted the call with “Loop 0 is not valid: Edge 1 is degenerate”. The sort copy is now repaired after the transform as well. The geometry returned is still the caller’s own, and the same cell gets the same ID whether the layer arrives projected, in lon/lat or in Web Mercator, except where two fine cells’ centres lie within the sort key’s rounding step of the same longitude (36 of 2,500 100 m cells straddling a UTM central meridian changed ID via EPSG:3035); join such layers on geometry.

  • select_features_forward() now says when fit_fn is ignoring the variables it is handed. The learner it takes is a function of (train_sf, predictor_vars), but the one cv_spatial() takes is a function of train_sf alone, and a learner written for that — function(train_sf, ...) — swallows the second argument and fits the same model every time. Nothing errored, because the training layer still carries every column: each candidate scored exactly what the intercept-only model scored, no candidate improved on it, and the result was an empty selected and an NA score with no word about why. Two different predictor sets do not produce the same cross-validated metric to the last digit, so that pattern is now recognised at the first step and reported as a warning naming the fix. The result is still returned.

  • create_grid_polygons() warns when both cellsize and target_cells are supplied. It already did for cellsize and n, and the documentation says to supply exactly one of the three, but target_cells was dropped in silence when cellsize was present. Through build_tessellation() that meant method = "hex", approx_n_cells = 25, cellsize = 10 returned however many cells a 10-unit lattice holds and said nothing about the 25. cellsize still wins; the override is now logged like its sibling.

  • build_tessellation() warns when approx_n_cells or cellsize is supplied with method = "voronoi" or "triangles". Both arguments size the hex and square lattices and nothing else — Voronoi grows one cell per input point and Delaunay one triangle per neighbouring triple — and both used to be dropped in silence. So build_tessellation(pts, method = "voronoi", approx_n_cells = 25) returned one cell per observation: the degenerate nearest-neighbour case, where every cell holds a single point, there is no within-cell variation and every standard error is NA. The warning names the argument and points at get_voronoi_seeds(), which is where a Voronoi cell count is actually set. It adds that params does not record the request either, so a saved result carries no sign of it: the Voronoi branch returns create_voronoi_polygons()’s own list, which has no slot for the argument, and the triangles branch no longer echoes approx_n_cells back (below). The warning fires under quiet = TRUE, which gates this function’s message()s and is documented not to silence R warnings.

  • determine_optimal_levels() fits each k as the best of 25 k-means++ restarts (Arthur and Vassilvitskii 2007; Fränti and Sieranoja 2019; Steinley 2003) instead of stats::kmeans(nstart = 5). The WSS curve is read for its shape, and with a handful of random restarts it carried optimisation noise: on eight-cluster layouts a sweep over k = 1..30 rose at one or two steps in three of five draws, and an earlier form of the elbow rule once selected such a bump. With the new budget the same sweeps rose at no step. A curve that still rises is now logged as a warning naming the number of rising steps, and the model-aware diagnostics carry it as wss_bumps beside wss_spread (the relative spread of WSS across restarts at each k) and nstart. A selection made on a curve that had a bump can differ from before — those were the cases that were wrong; a clean curve gives the same answer. Under a model-aware criterion the function also now warns before the sweep when max_levels leaves no k above the nine-cell floor, rather than fitting every k first and falling back afterwards. The seeding draws each centre by inverting the cumulative squared distance rather than with sample.int(prob = ): the same law, and a resolution_profile() of 3000 points takes 10 s instead of 35 s (determine_optimal_levels() on 3000 points, 4 s instead of 13 s), but it gives different centres for the same seed than earlier development builds did.

  • make_folds(method = "block_kfold") can now raise its “block dimension < autocorrelation range” warning. The comparison was always there, but the range it compared against was estimated only under auto_range = TRUE, the one setting in which the blocks had already been sized from that range and the warning could never fire; on every default call the diagnostic was dead code. With auto_range = FALSE (the default) and a response_var to hand — always the case when a cv_*() function builds the folds — a range is now estimated for the diagnostic alone. It sizes nothing: the blocks are the same geometric blocks as before and the folds do not change. A hand-set block_size below the range raises the same warning. The estimate’s own log lines stay off the console, and the check is skipped (with an INFO log line saying so) when gstat is not installed or there are fewer than 30 points. Only a grid dimension that is split is compared with the range, because a single row (or column) of blocks borders no other block across its width. On points along a line the comparison was with 0, so the warning fired on every call that had a response: a 10 km line had 15 blocks 667 m long against a 499 m range. Its advice, block_size = 499, made the blocks shorter (19 of 523 m). A 10 km x 100 m corridor was compared with its 100 m width in the same way. A response_var that names no column of points_sf is now an error for block_kfold, whether or not auto_range is set. With auto_range off, a misspelt name used to switch the check off silently.

  • fit_rf_model(include_coords = TRUE) logs its caution once per session rather than once per fit. Inside a five-fold cv_rf() or a twenty-fit cv_block_size_sweep() the same paragraph printed on every fit, which reads as twenty problems rather than one decision; the message now says it will not repeat.

  • fit_rf_model() reports what ranger actually objected to. ranger diagnoses a bad argument in its C++ layer, writes the diagnosis straight to stderr and then throws “User interrupt or internal error.” — so mtry = 99 on a two-predictor forest printed “mtry can not be larger than number of variables in data. Ranger will EXIT now.” to the console and raised an error naming neither the argument nor the problem. That line is not an R condition, so suppressMessages(), withCallingHandlers() and tryCatch() all missed it: it escaped every handler to the console (and into CI logs, where it reads as an error from a test that is passing), while cv_*() recorded the placeholder as the fold’s cause. The message stream is now diverted for the duration of the call, so the diagnosis becomes the reported reason — fold_status$message included — and nothing is printed behind the caller’s back. Output from a call that succeeds is passed through unchanged, and when the stream is already diverted (under testthat, knitr or capture.output(type = "message"), where only one sink is permitted) the call runs exactly as before. So does a call made after the session temp directory has been deleted, when there is nowhere to divert the stream to; it used to fail with “cannot open the connection”.

  • One empty point made determine_optimal_levels() return 1. The function reduced every feature to a point and projected it but never dropped an empty or non-finite one, so a single POINT EMPTY made the k = 1 WSS NA, k-means failed at every k, and the failure handler shrank the sweep to nothing: two well-separated clusters that gave 2 1 3 gave 1 once one empty row was added, with only a log line about interpolating the WSS. Such rows are now dropped with a warning that gives their number, and under select_on = "split" the returned positions still index the layer as passed.

  • A few missing predictor values took Moran’s I away from determine_optimal_levels(). A cell mean over a row with one missing predictor was NA and dropped the whole cell, and how many cells that removed depended on the points per cell, so z was computed on a different subset of cells at each k. Three missing values in 400 rows made every z in the evaluated window NA, and the call fell back to the geometric ranking with a warning that did not mention missing values. Rows with a missing or non-finite response or predictor now stay in the WSS sweep and the cells and are left out of Moran’s I, with a logged count, so every cell mean uses the same rows.

  • A misspelt response_var or predictor_vars in determine_optimal_levels() silently changed the criterion. A column that was not there counted as “no model variables”: with the default criterion a typo kept "geometric" where supplying both variables then upgraded to "combined" (on one 400-point layer 7 6 8 instead of 11 10 7, with no warning and no diagnostics), and under "morans_i" or "combined" the one log line said the variables were required although both had been supplied. A named column that is not in the layer is now an error, as it is in resolution_profile(), and a model-aware criterion given no predictor_vars (or no response_var) falls back with an R warning that says which is missing, rather than a log line.

  • determine_optimal_levels() stopped one level short when locations repeat. The sweep was capped one short of the number of distinct locations, the bound stats::kmeans() needs only when no location repeats: five stations visited thirty times each could not reach k = 5. The cap is now the number of distinct locations, and still one short of the number of points. A k whose WSS is 0 (to within 1e-12 of the total: a cell on every location) is left out of the log-log elbow line, and when the rest of the curve has no elbow, the fall to zero is the elbow. Leaving the level out and reading the rest made the call warn that the five stations had no cluster structure and return 3 2 4 (one metre of jitter gave 5 4 6); it now returns 5 4. Two stations visited thirty times each give 2 1, not 1 2. Zero is relative because k-means leaves floating-point residue: two groups of ten stations visited ten times each have a WSS of 7.8e-17 at k = 20, which dragged the whole line down and, at max_levels = 30, reported no cluster structure (still answering 2). resolution_profile() reads its elbow column the same way. The no-elbow warning names the bound that ended the ladder (the distinct locations, the points or max_levels); it named max_levels whichever bound it was.

  • The same layer with its rows in another order gave determine_optimal_levels() another answer. The subsample and every k-means start index rows, so a permutation of the input moved the WSS curve and could move the count. The rows are now put in coordinate order (response and predictors breaking ties) before either, so any permutation of a layer gives the same result. Results for a given seed differ from 2.0.0’s for that reason too.

  • Under criterion = "morans_i", top_n could change the count determine_optimal_levels() ranks first. The model-aware criteria re-run k-means at each count of the window around the elbow, the elbow plus or minus max(4, top_n), and the re-runs drew from one random stream in order. A top_n above 4 starts the window lower, so more re-runs came before each count, and the cells of every count in the window changed, and with them wss_eval, moran_i and moran_z. On 480 points in twelve clusters with max_levels = 30, "morans_i" put 15 first at top_n 1 to 4 and 16 at top_n = 5, both counts in both windows, and k = 17 had a |z| of 0.0013 at top_n = 6 and of 0.30 at top_n = 7. Under "combined" the ranking stayed and the diagnostics moved. Each re-run is now seeded with one integer drawn before the sweep plus its count, and the stream is put back after it, so for one set_seed a count gets the same cells, wss_eval and Moran’s I in any window that holds it. A wider window still scores more counts, and under "morans_i" one of them can rank first: on the same layer the first count is 16 at top_n 1 to 4, 17 at 5 and 6 and 19 at 7, each the count of smallest |z| in its window, and 17 and 19 are counts the wider windows add. For a given seed, moran_i, moran_z, wss_eval and the "morans_i" ranking can differ from before, and a "morans_i" call can fall back to the geometric ranking where it ranked, or rank where it fell back; the sweep, the elbow and the "combined" ranking are as before. With set_seed = NULL the re-runs no longer draw from the caller’s stream, so the stream after the call no longer depends on top_n.

  • Moran’s I of the cell means was NA for a response in small units, and in determine_optimal_levels() moved with the response’s origin. Moran’s I and its z do not change under a change of unit or origin, but the statistic was refused whenever the residuals of the cell means had a sum of squares under .Machine$double.eps, whatever their unit. A response of standard deviation 0.5 in units of 1e-9 got moran_i and moran_z NA at every level of resolution_profile(), with no warning that names them, while cp was the same as in units. Under determine_optimal_levels(criterion = "morans_i") every count was NA, and the call fell back to the geometric ranking with no diagnostics and a log line that blamed too few cells with a response or a singular regression. determine_optimal_levels() also formed the cell means from the raw response and regressed them, so at an offset of 1e15 they carried the rounding of the offset: on 2000 points in 40 clusters, "morans_i" ranked 43 35 38 at that offset and 36 37 35 at 0, from the same spread. The residuals are now refused when they are within the rounding of the cell means they come from, a bound relative to those means, and a response whose raw values lose their spread is taken about its median first, as resolution_profile() already takes it. A response whose largest absolute value lies outside 2^-255 to 2^255 is divided by a power of two first, which leaves its I and z as they are; in units of 1e200 Moran’s I came out NaN, and in units of 1e-200 NA, so determine_optimal_levels() fell back there too. The layer above gets the same counts and the same moran_z in units, in units of 1e-9 and at 1e15, and the profile the same moran_i and moran_z in units and in units of 1e-9 and 1e-12. A constant response, one the predictors fit exactly and cell means that differ by rounding alone still give NA, now in any unit: under determine_optimal_levels(criterion = "morans_i") a response of 1e15 in every row, and one of 1e10 times (3 + 2 w) with w the predictor, were ranked by Moran’s z of their rounding, and now fall back to the geometric ranking. Both fallback log lines name cell means that differ by rounding alone among their reasons. A response whose raw values show their spread, through a predictor (1e15 plus 1e5 times the predictor plus a spread of 1) or at an offset such as 1e11 plus a spread of 1, can still leave residuals small beside the cell means, and the regression of the raw cell means then carried the rounding of the offset: with a predictor the call fell back at 1e15, and Moran’s I moved by a relative 4e-4 to 2e-3 at 1e13. Where the residuals’ sum of squares is under 1e-12 of the cell means’, or they show no spread, the cell means are now formed and regressed again about the response’s centre, as resolution_profile() takes its fit, and are refused only if those residuals are within the rounding of the regression or of the raw values. Where a response’s residuals are larger than that and its values lie between 2^-255 and 2^255, it gets the same Moran’s I as before, unless its cell means differ by rounding alone.

  • determine_optimal_levels() blamed the wrong cause when its model-aware criteria had nothing to score, and its help page understated the fix. The model-aware pass scores only the elbow’s neighbourhood, and on points with no cluster structure the elbow sits near sqrt(max_levels), so every candidate stayed at or below the nine-cell floor until max_levels was about 40 (measured on 1000 uniform points: 12, 20 and 30 all fell back, and 40 scored k = 10 and 11 alone). The help page said “above roughly 10”, and the fallback was logged as “Moran’s I could not be computed”. The logged warning now names the window and the floor and points to resolution_profile(), and the help page gives the measured numbers. Which candidates are scored is unchanged.

  • The lines determine_optimal_levels() logs where the window around the elbow ends at nine cells or fewer told a "combined" call that the response would take part with a larger max_levels, and named max_levels whatever bound ended the ladder. The line logged before the sweep (k_max of 9 or fewer) and the one logged after it said that the model-aware criteria carry no information there and that the call falls back to the geometric ranking for that reason, and the first said to raise max_levels “for the criteria to contribute”. "combined" ranks by the sag of the WSS curve and reads no response at any count: it returns the geometric ranking there by a fixed rule, and a larger max_levels gives the sag’s order. For "combined" the two lines now say that it returns the geometric ranking when the window ends at nine cells or fewer and that Moran’s I, which it reports beside its ranking, is computed from ten cells. The line before the sweep also began “max_levels leaves k_max = …” and advised raising max_levels when the distinct locations or the points ended the ladder: on 200 rows at 8 locations it said so at max_levels 12 and 30 alike, and no max_levels takes k_max above 8 there. It now names the bound that ended the ladder (“the 8 distinct locations leave k_max = 8”, “one short of the 10 points leaves k_max = 9”) and advises raising max_levels only where a larger max_levels takes k_max above 9; otherwise it says that no max_levels takes k_max higher on these points. Where max_levels equals the other bound (8 locations at max_levels = 8) the line names max_levels and no longer advises raising it. On a subsample (more rows than sample_n) the points and the distinct locations that end the ladder are the subsample’s, and the line, the warning for a curve with no elbow and the warning for a ladder too short to read named them as the layer’s (“one short of the 9 points” on 400 rows at sample_n = 9): they now say “one short of the sample_n = 9 points drawn from 400” or “the 8 distinct locations in the sample_n = 30 rows drawn from 361”, and the advice is to raise sample_n where that takes k_max higher. The warning for a ladder too short to read advised raising max_levels to 3 wherever max_levels named the bound, as on 3 distinct points at max_levels = 2, where no max_levels lengthens the ladder; it now says to choose the count on other grounds there. The "morans_i" lines bound by max_levels alone, the counts and the diagnostics are as before.

  • build_tessellation() could not tessellate CRS-less planar points inside a CRS-less boundary. ensure_projected() marks such points crs_assumed = "none" (“planar, leave alone”), and build_tessellation() read that mark as a CRS name: st_crs("none") failed with “invalid crs: none” for every method, including the documented boundary = clip_target_for(pts), so CRS-less planar data could not be gridded at all. Only a real assumption (EPSG:4326) is now given to the boundary, which is refused if its coordinates cannot be degrees (below); with no assumption both stay in the same unnamed space.

  • When only one of the points and the boundary had a CRS, the tessellation builders stopped on sf’s bare “st_crs(x) == st_crs(y) is not TRUE”. UTM points read from a CSV with a UTM boundary failed in all four methods of build_tessellation() and in create_voronoi_polygons(); projected points with a boundary that had lost its .prj failed in create_voronoi_polygons() and method = "triangles", and clip_target_for() returned a target with no CRS — for lon/lat points with a CRS-less lon/lat boundary, in degrees, with expand = 20 buffering by 20 degrees. The side without a CRS is now interpreted in the other’s, as harmonize_crs() does, with a warning: lon/lat-looking coordinates are reprojected from EPSG:4326, others are stamped. CRS-less points that do not look like lon/lat are refused, with a message saying what to do, when the boundary is geographic, because stamping degrees on them would be wrong; a CRS-less boundary beside geographic points is read as lon/lat or refused (below).

  • A boundary without a CRS got a log line in make_folds(), cv_*() and predict_surface(), where every other function raises an R warning, and cv_rf() warned twice about one lon/lat boundary.
